title: Baked Mac and Cheese
summary: Creamy elbow macaroni in a sharp cheddar sauce with a crisp buttered breadcrumb top. A potluck favorite that reheats well.
steps: Heat the oven to 375 F and butter a 9 by 13 inch baking dish.
Boil the macaroni in well salted water for 2 minutes less than the package says. It should still be firm. Drain well.
Melt 4 tablespoons of the butter in a large pot over medium heat. Whisk in the flour and cook for 1 minute, stirring, without letting it brown.
Slowly whisk in the warm milk. Cook, stirring often, for 5 to 6 minutes until the sauce is thick enough to coat a spoon.
Take the pot off the heat. Stir in the mustard, cayenne, salt, pepper, the gruyere and 3 cups of the cheddar until smooth.
Fold in the drained macaroni and pour everything into the baking dish.
Top with the last cup of cheddar. Melt the last 2 tablespoons butter, toss the panko with it and scatter it over the top.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, until bubbling at the edges and golden on top.
Let it rest for 10 minutes before serving so the sauce sets up.

title: Buttermilk Pancakes
summary: Fluffy diner-style pancakes with golden edges. The batter comes together in one bowl in about five minutes.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.prep: melted, plus more for the pan

steps: Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda and salt in a large bowl.
In another bowl, whisk the buttermilk, eggs, melted butter and vanilla.
Pour the wet mixture into the dry and stir just until combined. A few small lumps are fine. Rest the batter for 5 minutes.
Heat a griddle or large nonstick skillet over medium heat and brush lightly with butter.
Scoop about 1/4 cup of batter per pancake onto the pan.
Cook until bubbles form on top and the edges look set, about 2 to 3 minutes.
Flip and cook for another 1 to 2 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Keep the finished pancakes on a plate in a 200 F oven while you cook the rest. Serve warm with butter and syrup.

title: Classic Meatloaf
summary: A tender, old-fashioned meatloaf with a tangy ketchup glaze. Slices cleanly and makes great sandwiches the next day.
steps: Heat the oven to 350 F and line a rimmed baking sheet with foil.
Stir the breadcrumbs and milk together in a large bowl and let them soak for 5 minutes.
Add the beef, eggs, onion, garlic, Worcestershire, salt, pepper and 1/4 cup of the ketchup.
Mix gently with your hands until just combined. Overmixing makes a tough loaf.
Shape into a loaf about 9 by 5 inches on the baking sheet.
Stir the remaining ketchup with the brown sugar and vinegar. Spread half of it over the loaf.
Bake for 45 minutes, then spread on the rest of the glaze.
Bake 15 to 20 minutes more, until the center reads 160 F on a thermometer.
Rest for 10 minutes before slicing.

title: Chicken Pot Pie
summary: A creamy chicken and vegetable filling under a flaky double crust. Using a store-bought crust and rotisserie chicken keeps it easy.
steps: Heat the oven to 400 F. Fit one pie crust into a 9 inch pie plate.
Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, carrots and celery for 6 to 8 minutes until soft.
Sprinkle in the flour and stir for 1 minute.
Slowly pour in the broth and milk, stirring. Simmer for 4 to 5 minutes until thick.
Stir in the chicken, peas, thyme, salt and pepper. Let the filling cool for 10 minutes so it does not melt the crust.
Pour the filling into the crust and lay the second crust on top. Trim and crimp the edges.
Brush the top with the egg wash and cut 4 small slits for steam.
Bake on a baking sheet for 35 to 40 minutes until deep golden and bubbling.
Let it stand for 15 minutes before cutting.

title: Buffalo Chicken Wings
summary: Crispy oven-baked wings tossed in a buttery hot sauce. No deep fryer needed.
steps: Heat the oven to 425 F. Set a wire rack on a rimmed baking sheet lined with foil.
Pat the wings very dry with paper towels. Dry skin is the key to crispness.
Toss the wings with the baking powder, salt and garlic powder until evenly coated.
Arrange the wings on the rack in a single layer without touching.
Bake for 25 minutes, flip, then bake 25 to 30 minutes more until deep golden and crisp.
Meanwhile, melt the butter in a small pan and stir in the hot sauce and vinegar.
Toss the hot wings with the sauce in a large bowl.
Serve right away with celery and blue cheese dressing.

title: Southern Fried Chicken
summary: Juicy buttermilk-brined chicken with a craggy, crunchy crust. Plan ahead for the overnight soak.
steps: Stir the buttermilk, hot sauce and 2 teaspoons salt together in a large bowl. Add the chicken, cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Whisk the flour, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, pepper and cayenne in a wide dish. Add 1 teaspoon more salt.
Pour oil about 1 inch deep into a large heavy skillet and heat to 325 F.
Lift each piece from the buttermilk, let the excess drip off, and press firmly into the flour. Coat well.
Rest the coated chicken on a rack for 10 minutes so the crust sticks.
Fry in batches, skin side down first, for 6 to 8 minutes per side, turning once, until deep golden.
Check that the thickest pieces reach 165 F. Dark meat is best at 175 F.
Drain on a wire rack and serve hot.

title: Biscuits and Sausage Gravy
summary: Soft split biscuits under a peppery, creamy sausage gravy. A hearty weekend breakfast.
steps: Bake the biscuits first (see the Buttermilk Biscuits recipe) or use a tube of refrigerated biscuits.
Brown the sausage in a large skillet over medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes, breaking it into small crumbles.
Do not drain the fat. Add butter only if the pan looks dry.
Sprinkle the flour over the sausage and stir for 1 to 2 minutes until it disappears.
Slowly pour in the milk, stirring constantly to avoid lumps.
Simmer over medium-low heat for 5 to 8 minutes, until thick and bubbly.
Season with salt, plenty of black pepper and the garlic powder. Thin with a splash of milk if needed.
Spoon the gravy over split warm biscuits and serve right away.

title: Buttermilk Biscuits
summary: Tall, flaky biscuits made with cold butter and buttermilk. Ready in under half an hour.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.prep: divided, 8 tablespoons very cold and cubed

steps: Heat the oven to 450 F and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, sugar, salt and baking soda in a large bowl.
Cut in the 8 tablespoons cold butter with your fingers or a pastry cutter until the pieces are pea sized.
Pour in the buttermilk and stir until a shaggy dough forms.
Turn it onto a floured counter and pat into a 1 inch thick rectangle. Fold in thirds and pat out again. Repeat twice.
Cut rounds with a 2 1/2 inch cutter, pressing straight down without twisting.
Place the biscuits touching on the baking sheet and brush with the remaining 2 tablespoons butter, melted.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes until tall and golden. Serve warm.

title: Skillet Cornbread
summary: A golden cornbread with crisp edges, baked in a hot cast iron skillet. Not too sweet, so it goes with chili or greens.
steps: Heat the oven to 425 F and put a 10 inch cast iron skillet inside as it heats.
Whisk the cornmeal, flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda and salt together.
In a second bowl, whisk the buttermilk, eggs and 3 tablespoons of the melted butter.
Stir the wet ingredients into the dry until just combined.
Carefully take the hot skillet out and add the last tablespoon of butter, swirling to coat.
Pour in the batter. It should sizzle at the edges.
Bake for 18 to 22 minutes until golden and a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool for 5 minutes in the pan, then cut into wedges.

title: Texas Beef Chili
summary: A thick, beef-heavy chili with no beans, built on chili powder and slow simmering. Serve with cornbread.
steps: Pat the beef dry and season with salt. Heat the oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Brown the beef in 3 batches, about 5 minutes per batch, and set aside.
Lower the heat to medium. Cook the onions for 6 minutes, then add the garlic and cook 1 minute.
Stir in the chili powder, cumin, oregano, paprika and cayenne for 30 seconds.
Add the tomato sauce, diced tomatoes, broth and the beef with its juices.
Bring to a simmer, cover partly and cook on low for 2 hours, stirring now and then, until the beef is tender.
Whisk the masa harina with 1/4 cup water and stir it in. Simmer 10 more minutes to thicken.
Taste for salt and serve with sour cream and cheddar.

title: White Chicken Chili
summary: A mild, creamy chili with white beans, green chiles and tender chicken. Quick enough for a weeknight.
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic, green chiles, cumin, oregano and chili powder. Stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the broth and add the beans. Mash about a third of the beans against the pot with a spoon to thicken it.
Simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the chicken and cream cheese until the cheese melts.
Turn off the heat and stir in the sour cream and salt.
Serve topped with cilantro and a squeeze of lime.

title: Chicken Noodle Soup
summary: Comforting homemade chicken soup with plenty of vegetables and egg noodles. Simmering the chicken in the pot makes the broth rich.
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, carrots and celery for 6 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
Pour in the broth, then add the chicken, bay leaves and thyme.
Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer for 25 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Lift out the chicken and shred it with two forks. Discard the bones and bay leaves.
Bring the soup back to a boil and add the noodles. Cook for 6 to 8 minutes until tender.
Return the chicken to the pot. Season with salt and pepper.
Stir in the parsley and serve hot.

title: Broccoli Cheddar Soup
summary: A thick, creamy soup with tender broccoli and plenty of sharp cheddar. Great with a crusty roll.
steps: Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft, then add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Whisk in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Slowly whisk in the broth, milk and half and half. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the broccoli and carrots. Simmer for 10 to 12 minutes until the broccoli is tender.
For a smoother soup, blend a few ladlefuls with an immersion blender and leave some pieces whole.
Turn the heat to low. Stir in the cheddar a handful at a time until melted. Do not boil.
Season with nutmeg, salt and pepper and serve hot.

title: Loaded Baked Potato Soup
summary: Creamy potato soup topped with bacon, cheddar, sour cream and chives, like a baked potato in a bowl.
steps: Cook the bacon in a large pot over medium heat until crisp. Move it to a paper towel and pour off all but 1 tablespoon of fat.
Add the butter and onion and cook for 5 minutes. Add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Whisk in the broth and milk, then add the potatoes.
Simmer for 20 minutes, until the potatoes are very tender.
Mash some of the potatoes right in the pot, leaving it chunky.
Stir in the cheddar, sour cream, salt and pepper over low heat until smooth.
Ladle into bowls and top with the bacon, more cheddar, sour cream and green onions.

title: Pot Roast with Carrots and Potatoes
summary: A fall-apart chuck roast braised with carrots and potatoes in a savory gravy. Mostly hands-off cooking.
steps: Heat the oven to 325 F. Pat the roast dry and season all over with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat and sear the roast 4 to 5 minutes per side until deeply browned. Move it to a plate.
Cook the onion for 4 minutes, then add the garlic and tomato paste for 1 minute.
Pour in the wine, if using, and scrape up the browned bits. Add the broth, Worcestershire and thyme.
Return the roast to the pot, cover and bake for 2 1/2 hours.
Add the carrots and potatoes around the roast. Cover and cook for 1 hour more, until everything is tender.
Move the roast and vegetables to a platter. Simmer the juices on the stove, stir in the cornstarch mixture and cook 2 minutes for gravy.
Shred or slice the roast and serve with the gravy.

title: Beef Stew
summary: A hearty stew of browned beef, potatoes and carrots in a rich, thickened broth.
steps: Toss the beef with the flour, salt and pepper.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown the beef in two batches and set aside.
Add the last tablespoon of oil, then cook the onion for 5 minutes. Add the garlic and tomato paste for 1 minute.
Pour in the broth and Worcestershire, scraping up the browned bits. Add the beef, bay leaves and thyme.
Bring to a simmer, cover and cook on low for 1 1/2 hours.
Add the potatoes and carrots and simmer 45 minutes more until the beef and vegetables are tender.
Stir in the peas and cook for 5 minutes. Remove the bay leaves and adjust the salt.

title: Sloppy Joes
summary: Saucy, tangy-sweet ground beef piled on soft buns. A fast family dinner.
steps: Cook the beef in a large skillet over medium-high heat for 6 to 8 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink remains.
Add the onion and bell pepper and cook for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the garlic and cook for 30 seconds. Drain any extra fat.
Add the ketchup, tomato sauce, brown sugar, mustard, Worcestershire, vinegar and salt.
Simmer on medium-low for 10 to 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick.
Spoon onto the toasted buns and serve.

title: Classic Cheeseburger
summary: A juicy pan-seared or grilled cheeseburger with melty American cheese. Keep the patties simple.
steps: Divide the beef into 4 loose balls and flatten each to about 3/4 inch thick, a little wider than the bun. Press a shallow dimple in the center of each.
Season both sides generously with salt and pepper just before cooking.
Heat a cast iron skillet or grill over medium-high heat.
Cook the patties for 4 minutes without pressing. Flip and cook 3 to 4 minutes more.
Add a cheese slice to each patty during the last minute and cover so it melts.
Butter the buns and toast them in the pan for 1 minute.
Build the burgers with lettuce, tomato, onion, pickles and your sauces.

title: Philly Cheesesteak
summary: Thinly sliced beef, soft onions and melted provolone on a toasty roll.
steps: Freeze the steak for 20 minutes to make slicing it thin easier. Slice against the grain as thin as you can.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the onions, and peppers and mushrooms if using, for 12 to 15 minutes until soft and golden. Remove to a plate.
Turn the heat to high and add the remaining oil. Cook the steak in two batches for 2 to 3 minutes each, seasoning with salt and pepper.
Return everything to the pan and mix. Shape into 4 portions and lay 2 slices of provolone on each so it melts.
Warm the rolls in a 350 F oven for 3 minutes.
Scoop each cheesy portion into a roll and serve hot.

title: Reuben Sandwich
summary: Corned beef, Swiss cheese, sauerkraut and Russian dressing on griddled rye.
steps: Stir the mayonnaise, ketchup, relish and horseradish together for the dressing.
Spread dressing on one side of each bread slice.
On two slices, layer Swiss, corned beef, sauerkraut and another slice of Swiss. Top with the other bread, dressing side down.
Butter the outsides of the sandwiches.
Cook in a skillet over medium-low heat for 3 to 4 minutes per side, pressing gently, until the bread is golden and the cheese melts.
Slice in half and serve hot.

title: BLT Sandwich
summary: Crisp bacon, juicy tomato and crunchy lettuce on toast with mayo. Best when tomatoes are in season.
steps: Heat the oven to 400 F and lay the bacon on a rack over a foil-lined baking sheet.
Bake for 15 to 20 minutes until crisp. Drain on paper towels.
Toast the bread until golden.
Spread mayonnaise on one side of each slice.
Season the tomato slices with salt and pepper.
Layer bacon, lettuce and tomato on two slices and top with the others.
Cut diagonally and serve.

title: Grilled Cheese Sandwich
summary: Golden, crisp bread with gooey melted cheese. A simple classic.
steps: Spread butter, or a thin layer of mayonnaise for extra crispness, on one side of each slice of bread.
Heat a skillet over medium-low heat.
Place two slices butter side down in the pan. Top each with two slices of cheese.
Cover with the remaining bread, butter side up.
Cook for 3 to 4 minutes until deep golden, then flip.
Cook another 2 to 3 minutes until the cheese is melted.
Rest for a minute, slice and serve.

title: Tuna Melt
summary: Creamy tuna salad on toasted bread under melted cheddar. Ready in 15 minutes.
steps: Heat the broiler to high.
Mix the tuna, mayonnaise, celery, onion, lemon juice and pepper in a bowl.
Toast the bread lightly and butter one side of each slice.
Spread the tuna mixture on the unbuttered sides and place on a baking sheet.
Top with cheese and broil for 2 to 3 minutes until bubbly and spotty brown.
Serve open-faced or topped with another slice of toast.

title: Chicken Salad Sandwich
summary: Creamy chicken salad with celery, grapes and a squeeze of lemon. Good for leftover or rotisserie chicken.
steps: Stir the mayonnaise, yogurt, lemon juice, salt and pepper together in a large bowl.
Fold in the chicken, celery, grapes and green onions.
Chill for 15 minutes if you have time so the flavors blend.
Taste and adjust the salt and lemon.
Layer lettuce and a generous scoop of chicken salad on 4 slices of bread.
Top with the remaining bread and serve.

title: Egg Salad Sandwich
summary: Soft hard-boiled eggs in a creamy, tangy dressing. A quick lunch from pantry staples.
steps: Put the eggs in a pot and cover with cold water by 1 inch.
Bring to a boil, then cover, turn off the heat and let sit for 11 minutes.
Move the eggs to a bowl of ice water for 5 minutes, then peel.
Chop the eggs coarsely and put them in a bowl.
Add the mayonnaise, mustard, vinegar, celery, chives, salt and pepper and mix gently.
Pile onto bread with lettuce, dust with paprika and close the sandwiches.

title: Club Sandwich
summary: A triple-decker of turkey, bacon, lettuce and tomato on toast, cut into quarters.
steps: Cook the bacon until crisp in a skillet or in a 400 F oven, about 15 minutes, and drain.
Toast all 6 slices of bread.
Spread mayonnaise on one side of each slice.
On the first slice, layer turkey, cheese and lettuce. Add a second slice of toast, mayo side up.
Add bacon and tomato, season with salt and pepper, and top with the third slice, mayo side down.
Secure with 4 toothpicks and cut into 4 triangles. Serve with chips or fries.

title: Pulled Pork Sandwich
summary: Smoky, slow-cooked pork shoulder shredded and piled onto buns with barbecue sauce and slaw.
steps: Mix the brown sugar, paprika, salt, garlic powder, onion powder, pepper and cayenne.
Rub the spice mix all over the pork. If you have time, wrap and refrigerate for a few hours or overnight.
Place the pork in a slow cooker and pour the broth around it.
Cook on low for 8 to 10 hours, or until it shreds easily with a fork and reads about 200 F.
Move the pork to a bowl, discard large pieces of fat, and shred the meat.
Stir in the barbecue sauce and enough cooking juices to keep the meat moist.
Toss the coleslaw mix with the mayonnaise and vinegar.
Pile the pork on the buns and top with slaw.

title: Baby Back Ribs
summary: Tender oven-baked ribs with a sweet and smoky rub and a sticky barbecue glaze.
steps: Heat the oven to 275 F. Pull the thin membrane off the back of each rack using a paper towel for grip.
Mix the brown sugar, paprika, salt, garlic powder, onion powder, pepper and chili powder.
Rub the mixture all over both sides of the ribs.
Wrap each rack tightly in foil, meat side up, and set on a baking sheet.
Bake for 2 1/2 hours until very tender.
Heat the broiler or grill. Unwrap the ribs and brush with barbecue sauce.
Broil or grill for 3 to 5 minutes, watching closely, until the sauce is sticky and lightly charred.
Rest for 10 minutes and cut between the bones.

title: Barbecue Chicken Drumsticks
summary: Sticky baked drumsticks with a smoky rub and barbecue glaze. Easy and kid friendly.
steps: Heat the oven to 425 F and line a baking sheet with foil. Set a rack on top.
Pat the drumsticks dry and toss with the oil.
Mix the brown sugar, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt and pepper and rub it into the chicken.
Arrange on the rack and bake for 30 minutes.
Brush with half of the barbecue sauce and bake 10 minutes.
Turn, brush with the remaining sauce and bake another 10 to 15 minutes, until the chicken reads 175 F and the glaze is sticky.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Shrimp and Grits
summary: Creamy cheddar grits topped with garlicky bacon shrimp. A Southern classic that cooks in 40 minutes.
steps: Bring the water, milk and salt to a boil in a heavy pot. Whisk in the grits slowly.
Lower the heat, cover and simmer for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy.
Stir in the butter and cheddar. Keep warm.
Cook the bacon in a large skillet over medium heat until crisp. Move to a plate, leaving the fat in the pan.
Pat the shrimp dry, toss with paprika and cook in the bacon fat over medium-high heat for 2 minutes per side until pink.
Add the garlic for 30 seconds, then the lemon juice. Remove from the heat.
Spoon the grits into bowls and top with shrimp, bacon and green onions.

title: Jambalaya
summary: A one-pot Louisiana rice dish with smoked sausage, chicken and shrimp. It is spicy, savory and feeds a crowd.

ingredients.name: chicken thighs
ingredients.prep: boneless, skinless, cut into bite-size pieces

steps: Heat the oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown the sausage for about 5 minutes, then scoop it onto a plate, leaving the fat in the pot.
Season the chicken with a pinch of salt and half the Cajun seasoning. Brown it in the pot for 4 to 5 minutes, then move it to the plate with the sausage.
Lower the heat to medium. Add the onion, bell pepper and celery and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, scraping up the browned bits, until soft.
Stir in the garlic, the remaining Cajun seasoning and the thyme and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, rice and broth, then return the sausage and chicken to the pot. Stir well and bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce the heat to low and cook for 20 minutes without lifting the lid.
Nestle the shrimp into the top of the rice, cover again and cook for 5 to 7 minutes, until the shrimp are pink and the rice is tender.
Turn off the heat and let it rest, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork, season with salt and hot sauce, and top with green onions.

title: Chicken and Sausage Gumbo
summary: A deep, smoky gumbo built on a patient dark roux, with chicken thighs and andouille. Serve it over rice.
steps: Whisk the oil and flour together in a heavy Dutch oven over medium heat. Stir constantly with a wooden spoon or flat whisk for 30 to 40 minutes, until the roux is the color of dark chocolate. Lower the heat if it smells scorched, and start over if you see black flecks.
Add the onion, bell pepper and celery right away and stir for 5 minutes. The vegetables will stop the roux from cooking further and it will bubble.
Stir in the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the broth a little at a time, stirring until smooth, then add the Cajun seasoning, bay leaves, thyme and Worcestershire sauce.
Add the chicken, bring to a gentle boil, then reduce to a low simmer. Cook uncovered for 1 hour, skimming any oil from the surface.
Lift out the chicken, shred the meat off the bones and discard the bones and skin.
Return the chicken to the pot, add the sausage, and simmer for another 30 minutes. Remove the bay leaves.
Taste and add salt as needed. Ladle over rice and top with green onions and hot sauce.

title: Red Beans and Rice
summary: A creamy Monday-night New Orleans classic made with dried red beans, smoked sausage and the holy trinity of vegetables.
steps: Heat the oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat and brown the sausage for 5 minutes. Remove half and set aside.
Add the onion, bell pepper and celery to the pot and cook for 8 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the drained beans, broth, bay leaves, thyme, Cajun seasoning and paprika. Bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low, partly cover and simmer for 2 to 2 1/2 hours, stirring now and then, until the beans are completely tender. Add water if the pot gets dry.
Mash about a third of the beans against the side of the pot with a spoon to make the sauce creamy.
Stir in the reserved sausage and simmer for 15 minutes more. Remove the bay leaves and season with salt.
Serve over rice with green onions and hot sauce.

title: Hoppin' John
summary: A Southern New Year's dish of black-eyed peas simmered with smoky bacon and served over rice.
steps: Cook the bacon in a large pot over medium heat for 6 to 8 minutes until crisp. Remove with a slotted spoon, leaving the drippings behind.
Add the onion, bell pepper and celery to the drippings and cook for 6 minutes until soft.
Stir in the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the black-eyed peas, broth, bay leaf, thyme and cayenne. Bring to a simmer.
Cook, partly covered, for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the liquid thickens slightly.
Stir in the vinegar and half of the bacon. Season with salt and pepper.
Spoon over rice and top with the remaining bacon and green onions.

title: Collard Greens with Bacon
summary: Tender Southern collards simmered low and slow in a smoky, tangy broth.

ingredients.name: collard greens
ingredients.prep: stems removed, leaves cut into ribbons

steps: Wash the collards well in a sink of cold water, lifting them out so the grit stays behind. Remove the thick stems and slice the leaves into 1-inch ribbons.
Cook the bacon in a large pot over medium heat for 6 to 8 minutes until crisp. Leave the drippings in the pot.
Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes, then add the garlic and red pepper flakes for 1 minute.
Add the greens in handfuls, stirring until each batch wilts to make room for the next.
Pour in the broth, vinegar and sugar. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a low simmer.
Cover and cook for 45 to 60 minutes, stirring now and then, until the greens are very tender.
Season with salt and pepper, and serve with some of the cooking liquid spooned over the top.

title: Southern Green Beans
summary: Green beans cooked soft and savory with bacon and onion, the way they show up at a Southern Sunday dinner.
steps: Cook the bacon in a large pot over medium heat for 6 to 8 minutes until crisp. Remove it to a plate and leave 2 tablespoons of drippings in the pot.
Cook the onion in the drippings for 4 minutes, then add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the green beans, broth, sugar and pepper. Stir to combine.
Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer, cover and cook for 30 to 40 minutes, until the beans are soft and olive green.
Uncover and cook for 5 more minutes if there is a lot of liquid left.
Stir in the bacon and the butter if using. Taste and add salt as needed.

title: Creamed Spinach
summary: A steakhouse-style side of tender spinach in a rich, lightly nutmeg-scented cream sauce.
steps: Place the thawed spinach in a clean dish towel or a fine strainer and squeeze out as much water as you can. Fluff it with a fork.
Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion for 4 minutes until soft, then add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Sprinkle in the flour and stir for 1 minute.
Slowly whisk in the milk and cream. Simmer for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.
Stir in the spinach and cook for 3 minutes until hot and well combined.
Add the Parmesan, nutmeg, salt and pepper. Stir until the cheese melts, then serve warm.

title: Creamed Corn
summary: A quick skillet creamed corn with a creamy, sweet-savory sauce. It is easy enough for weeknights.
steps: Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat and cook the onion for 3 minutes until soft.
Add the corn and cook for 4 minutes, stirring, to take off the chill and bring out its sweetness.
Sprinkle the flour over the corn and stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the cream and milk, then add the sugar and pepper.
Simmer for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring often, until the sauce is thick and creamy. Mash a few spoonfuls of corn against the pan for extra body.
Season with salt and scatter chives on top if you like.

title: Corn Chowder
summary: A thick, comforting chowder with sweet corn, potatoes and bacon. It is ready in under an hour.

ingredients.name: yukon gold potatoes
ingredients.prep: peeled and cut into 1/2 inch cubes

steps: Cook the bacon in a large pot over medium heat for 6 to 8 minutes until crisp. Move it to a plate, leaving 2 tablespoons of drippings.
Add the onion and celery and cook for 6 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the broth, scraping up the browned bits, then add the potatoes and thyme.
Bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer, and cook for 12 to 15 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Add the corn and simmer for 5 minutes. Use a potato masher or immersion blender to lightly crush about a quarter of the soup so it thickens.
Stir in the half and half and warm through without boiling.
Season with salt and pepper and serve topped with bacon and chives.
