title: Coleslaw
summary: Crunchy, creamy and a little tangy, this classic slaw is ideal for barbecue, fish tacos or sandwiches.
steps: Whisk the mayonnaise, vinegar, sugar, mustard and celery seed together in a large bowl until smooth.
Add the coleslaw mix and toss until everything is coated.
Season with salt and pepper.
Cover and chill for at least 30 minutes so the cabbage softens slightly and the flavors blend.
Stir again before serving, and add a splash more vinegar if you want it tangier.

title: Deviled Eggs
summary: Silky, tangy egg yolk filling piped into tender whites. A potluck and holiday essential.
steps: Put the eggs in a saucepan in a single layer and cover with an inch of cold water. Bring to a boil over high heat, then turn off the heat, cover and let stand for 12 minutes.
Move the eggs to a bowl of ice water and chill for 10 minutes. Peel them under a little running water.
Cut each egg in half lengthwise and pop the yolks into a bowl. Arrange the whites on a platter.
Mash the yolks with a fork until fine, then stir in the mayonnaise, mustard, vinegar, salt and pepper until smooth.
Spoon or pipe the filling into the whites.
Dust with paprika and sprinkle on chives if using. Chill until serving.

title: Macaroni Salad
summary: A creamy, tangy picnic salad with tender elbows, crunchy celery and a little sweetness.
steps: Cook the macaroni in well-salted boiling water for 1 minute less than the package directions so it stays a little firm.
Drain and rinse under cold water until cool. Drain very well.
Whisk the mayonnaise, vinegar, mustard and sugar together in a large bowl.
Add the macaroni, celery, onion, bell pepper and eggs if using. Stir until coated.
Season with salt and pepper.
Chill for at least 1 hour. The pasta soaks up the dressing, so stir in a spoonful of mayonnaise or a splash of milk before serving if it looks dry.
Dust with paprika before serving.

title: Three Bean Salad
summary: A sweet-and-sour make-ahead bean salad that gets better after a night in the fridge.
steps: Combine the green beans, kidney beans, chickpeas and red onion in a large bowl.
In a small bowl or jar, whisk or shake the vinegar, sugar, oil, celery seed, salt and pepper until the sugar dissolves.
Pour the dressing over the beans and toss gently.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, ideally overnight, stirring once or twice.
Stir in the parsley if using, and serve chilled with a slotted spoon.

title: Cobb Salad
summary: A hearty main-course salad with rows of chicken, bacon, egg, avocado, tomato and blue cheese over crisp greens.
steps: Place the eggs in a pot, cover with cold water, bring to a boil, then turn off the heat, cover and let sit for 11 minutes. Cool in ice water, peel and chop.
Season the chicken with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the chicken for 6 to 7 minutes per side, until it reaches 165 F inside. Rest for 5 minutes, then dice.
Cook the bacon in a skillet over medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes until crisp. Drain on paper towels and crumble.
Spread the romaine on a large platter or divide it among 4 plates.
Arrange rows of chicken, bacon, egg, avocado, tomato and blue cheese on top.
Sprinkle with chives and drizzle with the vinaigrette just before serving.

title: Chicken Caesar Salad
summary: Crisp romaine with garlicky Caesar dressing, juicy grilled chicken, parmesan and crunchy homemade croutons.
steps: Heat the oven to 375 F. Toss the bread cubes with 3 tablespoons olive oil, garlic powder and a pinch of salt on a baking sheet. Bake for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring once, until golden and crisp.
Pound the chicken to an even 3/4 inch thickness. Season with salt and pepper and rub with 1 tablespoon olive oil.
Cook the chicken in a hot skillet or grill pan over medium-high heat for 5 to 6 minutes per side, until it reaches 165 F. Rest for 5 minutes and slice.
Whisk the mayonnaise, lemon juice, mustard, Worcestershire, garlic and water until smooth. Stir in half of the Parmesan and season with pepper.
Toss the romaine with enough dressing to coat the leaves.
Top with chicken, croutons and the remaining Parmesan and serve right away.

title: Waldorf Salad
summary: A cool, crunchy salad of apples, grapes, celery and walnuts in a light creamy dressing.
steps: Whisk the mayonnaise, yogurt, lemon juice, honey and salt in a large bowl.
Add the diced apples right away and toss so the lemon keeps them from browning.
Fold in the grapes, celery and most of the walnuts.
Chill for at least 20 minutes.
Serve in lettuce cups if you like, topped with the remaining walnuts.

title: Wedge Salad
summary: A steakhouse classic: a cold iceberg wedge under creamy blue cheese dressing, bacon and tomatoes.
steps: Cook the bacon in a skillet over medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes until crisp. Drain on paper towels and crumble.
Mash half of the blue cheese in a bowl, then stir in the sour cream, mayonnaise, buttermilk, vinegar, garlic powder, pepper and a pinch of salt. Thin with a little more buttermilk if needed.
Trim the base of the lettuce and remove any wilted outer leaves. Cut into 4 wedges, keeping the core attached so they hold together.
Place a wedge on each plate.
Spoon the dressing over the wedges, then top with the bacon, tomatoes, remaining blue cheese and chives.

title: Taco Salad
summary: Seasoned ground beef, crisp lettuce, cheese and crunchy tortilla chips with a creamy salsa dressing.
steps: Brown the beef in a large skillet over medium-high heat for 6 to 8 minutes, breaking it up. Drain excess fat.
Stir in the taco seasoning and water and simmer for 3 to 5 minutes until thickened.
Whisk the sour cream and half of the salsa together for the dressing, adding a spoonful of water if it is thick.
Layer the romaine, beans, tomatoes and cheese in large bowls.
Top with the warm beef, avocado and green onions.
Add the crushed chips and drizzle with the dressing. Serve with the remaining salsa.

photo.author: Jeff Kramer from Austin, Texas, United States

title: Buffalo Chicken Dip
summary: Creamy, spicy, cheesy and always the first thing gone at game day.
steps: Heat the oven to 350 F.
Stir the cream cheese, ranch and buffalo sauce together in a large bowl until smooth.
Fold in the chicken and 1 cup of the cheddar.
Spread into an 8 inch baking dish and top with the remaining cheddar.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until bubbling and golden at the edges.
Top with green onions and serve hot with chips and celery.

title: Spinach Artichoke Dip
summary: A bubbly, cheesy baked dip with spinach and tender artichoke hearts. Serve with chips or toasted bread.
steps: Heat the oven to 375 F.
Squeeze the thawed spinach in a clean towel until very dry.
Stir the cream cheese, sour cream and mayonnaise together until smooth.
Mix in the garlic, mozzarella, half of the Parmesan, red pepper flakes if using and salt.
Fold in the spinach and artichokes.
Spread in a 1 1/2 quart baking dish and top with the remaining Parmesan.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until hot and golden on top.
Let it cool for 5 minutes and serve with chips.

title: Seven Layer Dip
summary: A cold, no-bake party dip with refried beans, guacamole, sour cream, salsa, cheese, olives and tomatoes.
steps: Stir the refried beans and taco seasoning together in a bowl.
Spread the beans in an even layer in a 9 by 13 inch dish or a deep pie plate.
Spread the guacamole over the beans, then the sour cream, taking care not to mix the layers.
Spoon the drained salsa over the sour cream.
Sprinkle on the cheese, olives, tomato and green onions.
Chill for at least 30 minutes, then serve with tortilla chips.

title: Baked Ziti
summary: Pasta tossed with meaty tomato sauce and ricotta, then baked under a blanket of melted mozzarella.
steps: Heat the oven to 375 F and grease a 9 by 13 inch baking dish.
Boil the ziti in salted water for 2 minutes less than the package directions. Drain.
Brown the sausage with the onion in a large skillet over medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes, breaking up the meat. Add the garlic for 1 minute.
Stir in the marinara, crushed tomatoes and oregano and simmer for 10 minutes.
Mix the ricotta, egg, half of the Parmesan, the parsley and a pinch each of salt and pepper in a bowl.
Combine the pasta with the sauce and half of the mozzarella, then spoon half into the dish. Dot with the ricotta mixture, then top with the remaining pasta.
Cover with the rest of the mozzarella and Parmesan. Cover with foil and bake for 25 minutes.
Uncover and bake for 10 to 15 minutes more until bubbling and browned. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Chicken Parmesan
summary: Crispy breaded chicken cutlets topped with marinara and melted mozzarella, served over pasta.

ingredients.name: chicken breast
ingredients.prep: large, boneless, skinless, sliced in half horizontally into 4 cutlets

steps: Heat the oven to 425 F.
Pound the cutlets to an even 1/2 inch thickness and season with salt and pepper.
Set up three shallow dishes: flour in one, beaten eggs in the second, and the panko mixed with the Parmesan and Italian seasoning in the third.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, then egg, then the panko mixture, pressing to coat.
Heat the oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat and fry the cutlets for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden. Work in batches if needed.
Place the cutlets on a baking sheet, spoon marinara over each and top with mozzarella.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes until the cheese is melted and the chicken reaches 165 F.
Serve over spaghetti with basil on top.

title: Spaghetti and Meatballs
summary: Tender beef and pork meatballs simmered in a simple red sauce and piled over spaghetti.
steps: Stir the bread crumbs and milk together in a large bowl and let sit for 5 minutes.
Add the beef, pork, Parmesan, eggs, half of the garlic, parsley, salt and pepper. Mix gently with your hands until just combined, and roll into about 24 golf-ball-size meatballs.
Heat the oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown the meatballs in batches for about 5 minutes total, turning, then move to a plate.
Cook the onion in the same pot for 4 minutes, then add the remaining garlic for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, oregano and sugar, and bring to a simmer.
Return the meatballs to the sauce, partly cover, and simmer on low for 30 to 40 minutes, until the meatballs are cooked through and the sauce is thick.
Cook the spaghetti in salted boiling water until al dente, then drain.
Serve the spaghetti topped with meatballs and sauce.

title: Tuna Noodle Casserole
summary: A retro comfort casserole with egg noodles, tuna, peas and a creamy sauce under a crunchy crumb topping.
steps: Heat the oven to 375 F and grease a 9 by 13 inch dish.
Cook the noodles in salted boiling water for 2 minutes less than the package directions. Drain.
Melt 2 tablespoons butter in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the mushrooms and onion for 7 minutes until golden.
Stir in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the milk and mushroom soup. Simmer for 3 minutes until thickened.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in the cheese, tuna, peas, noodles, salt and pepper.
Spread in the dish. Toss the panko with the melted butter and sprinkle on top.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until bubbling and the topping is golden. Rest for 5 minutes.

title: Green Bean Casserole
summary: The Thanksgiving favorite, made with a quick homemade mushroom sauce and crispy fried onions.

ingredients.name: green beans
ingredients.prep: trimmed and cut in 2 inch pieces

steps: Heat the oven to 375 F.
Boil the green beans in salted water for 4 minutes, then drain and rinse under cold water.
Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the mushrooms for 8 minutes until browned, then add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Stir in the flour for 1 minute. Add the broth, cream and soy sauce and simmer for 4 minutes until thick.
Season with pepper and salt, then fold in the beans and half of the fried onions.
Spoon into a 2 quart baking dish and bake for 20 minutes.
Top with the remaining onions and bake for 5 to 10 minutes more until golden and bubbling.

photo.author: Rick Kimpel from Spring, TX, USA

title: Sweet Potato Casserole
summary: Creamy mashed sweet potatoes with a brown sugar pecan topping. Sweet enough for dessert, though it is a side.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.prep: divided, 4 tbsp softened and 4 tbsp cold and cubed

ingredients.name: brown sugar
ingredients.prep: divided, 1/4 cup for the filling and 1/2 cup for the topping

steps: Heat the oven to 400 F. Prick the sweet potatoes with a fork and roast on a lined baking sheet for 45 to 55 minutes until very soft.
Lower the oven to 350 F and grease a 9 by 13 inch dish.
Scoop the flesh into a large bowl and mash until smooth.
Beat in the 4 tablespoons softened butter, 1/4 cup of the brown sugar, milk, eggs, vanilla, cinnamon and salt. Spread in the dish.
Rub the remaining 1/2 cup brown sugar, the flour and the 4 tablespoons cold cubed butter together with your fingers until crumbly, then stir in the pecans.
Sprinkle over the casserole.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the topping is golden and the center is set.

title: King Ranch Chicken Casserole
summary: A Tex-Mex layered casserole with chicken, corn tortillas, green chiles and cheese in a creamy sauce.
steps: Heat the oven to 350 F and grease a 9 by 13 inch dish.
Melt the butter in a skillet and cook the onion and bell pepper for 6 to 8 minutes until soft.
Stir in the diced tomatoes with chilies, both soups, chili powder and cumin. Warm for 3 minutes, then season with salt.
Spread a thin layer of sauce on the bottom of the dish and cover with half of the tortilla pieces.
Top with half the chicken, half the remaining sauce and a third of the cheese. Repeat with the rest of the tortillas, chicken and sauce.
Cover with the remaining cheese.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until bubbly and golden, then rest for 10 minutes.

title: Shepherd's Pie with Ground Beef
summary: A savory beef and vegetable filling topped with fluffy mashed potatoes and baked until golden. Technically a cottage pie, and just as good.
steps: Heat the oven to 400 F.
Boil the potatoes in salted water for 15 to 20 minutes until tender. Drain, then mash with 3 tablespoons butter and the warm milk. Season with salt and pepper and stir in the cheese if using.
Meanwhile, melt the remaining 1 tablespoon butter in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Brown the beef for 6 to 8 minutes, then drain most of the fat.
Add the onion and carrots and cook for 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic and tomato paste for 1 minute.
Sprinkle in the flour, then pour in the broth and Worcestershire. Add the thyme and simmer for 5 minutes until thickened.
Stir in the peas and season with salt and pepper.
Spread the mashed potatoes over the beef, sealing it to the edges, and rake the top with a fork.
Bake on a baking sheet for 25 to 30 minutes until the top is golden. Rest for 10 minutes.

photo.author: Abhinaba Basu from Redmond, United States

title: Chicken and Dumplings
summary: Tender chicken and vegetables in a rich, creamy broth with fluffy drop biscuit dumplings.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.prep: divided, 2 tbsp for the stew and 2 tbsp cold and cubed for the dumplings

ingredients.name: all-purpose flour
ingredients.prep: divided, 1/3 cup for the stew and 2 cups for the dumplings

steps: Melt 2 tablespoons of the butter in a large Dutch oven over medium heat. Cook the onion, carrots and celery for 6 minutes. Add the garlic for 1 minute.
Sprinkle in 1/3 cup of the flour and stir for 1 minute, then slowly add the broth.
Add the chicken, thyme and bay leaf. Simmer gently for 20 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Lift out the chicken, shred it with two forks and return it to the pot. Remove the bay leaf and stir in the cream and peas.
For the dumplings, whisk the remaining 2 cups flour, the baking powder and salt. Cut in the 2 tablespoons cold butter with your fingers until crumbly, then stir in the buttermilk until just combined.
Bring the stew to a gentle simmer. Drop heaping spoonfuls of dough on top, leaving a little space between them.
Cover and cook for 15 minutes without lifting the lid, until the dumplings are puffed and cooked through.
Season with pepper, sprinkle with parsley and serve.

title: Chicken Fried Steak
summary: Tender cube steak with a crunchy seasoned crust, served under peppery cream gravy. A Southern diner classic you can make in one skillet.

ingredients.name: whole milk
ingredients.prep: divided, 1/2 cup for the egg wash and the rest for the gravy

steps: Pat the steaks dry and season both sides with a little of the salt and pepper.
In a shallow dish, mix 1 1/2 cups of the flour with the paprika, garlic powder, 1 teaspoon salt and 1 teaspoon pepper.
In a second dish, whisk the eggs with 1/2 cup of the milk.
Dredge each steak in the flour mixture, dip it in the egg mixture, then press it into the flour again so the coating is thick and even. Rest the steaks on a rack for 10 minutes.
Heat the oil in a large heavy skillet over medium-high heat to about 350 F.
Fry the steaks 3 to 4 minutes per side until deep golden and cooked through. Move them to a rack set over a sheet pan and keep warm.
Pour off all but 1/4 cup of the oil, leaving the browned bits. Whisk in 1/4 cup of flour and cook for 1 minute.
Slowly whisk in the remaining milk and cook, stirring, for 4 to 5 minutes until thick. Season with plenty of black pepper and salt.
Serve the steaks hot with the gravy poured over the top.

title: Salisbury Steak
summary: Seasoned beef patties simmered in a savory onion and mushroom gravy. Comfort food that is lovely over mashed potatoes or egg noodles.
steps: Mix the beef, bread crumbs, egg, ketchup, half of the Worcestershire, salt and pepper gently until just combined.
Shape the mixture into 4 oval patties about 3/4 inch thick.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Brown the patties 3 minutes per side, then move them to a plate. They will finish cooking later.
In the same skillet over medium heat, melt the butter and cook the onion and mushrooms for 6 to 8 minutes until soft and golden.
Sprinkle the flour over the vegetables and stir for 1 minute.
Slowly stir in the broth, then add the mustard and the rest of the Worcestershire. Simmer until slightly thickened, about 3 minutes.
Nestle the patties back into the gravy, cover, and simmer on low for 12 to 15 minutes until cooked through to 160 F.
Taste the gravy, adjust the salt and pepper, and serve the patties with plenty of gravy.

title: Smothered Pork Chops
summary: Seared pork chops braised in a rich onion gravy until fork tender. Serve with rice or mashed potatoes to catch every drop.
steps: Pat the chops dry. Mix 1/2 cup flour with the salt, pepper, paprika and garlic powder, and coat the chops, shaking off the extra.
Heat the oil in a large deep skillet over medium-high heat. Sear the chops 3 minutes per side until browned, then set aside on a plate.
Lower the heat to medium. Add the onions to the skillet and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring, until soft and golden.
Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds, then stir in 2 tablespoons flour for 1 minute.
Slowly pour in the broth, stirring and scraping up the browned bits, and add the thyme.
Bring to a simmer, then return the chops and any juices to the pan, spooning onions over the top.
Cover and simmer on low for 25 to 30 minutes until the pork is tender and reaches at least 145 F.
Uncover and simmer 3 to 5 minutes if the gravy needs to thicken. Taste and adjust the seasoning before serving.

title: Pan-Seared Steak with Garlic Butter
summary: A deeply browned skillet steak basted with garlic and thyme butter. It is ready in about 20 minutes and tastes like a steakhouse.
steps: Take the steaks out of the fridge 20 to 30 minutes ahead. Pat them very dry and season all over with the salt and pepper.
Heat a heavy skillet, ideally cast iron, over high heat for 3 minutes until very hot. Add the oil.
Lay the steaks in the pan away from you and sear without moving for 3 to 4 minutes until a dark crust forms.
Flip the steaks and cook 2 minutes more. Reduce the heat to medium.
Add the butter, garlic and thyme. Tilt the pan and spoon the foaming butter over the steaks for 1 to 2 minutes.
Check the temperature: 125 F for rare, 135 F for medium-rare, 145 F for medium. Remove the steaks a few degrees early.
Rest the steaks on a plate for 5 to 10 minutes, then slice against the grain.
Spoon the garlic butter from the pan over the slices and sprinkle with parsley.

title: Roast Chicken with Lemon and Herbs
summary: A whole chicken roasted over onions with lemon, garlic and fresh herbs until the skin is crisp and the meat is juicy. A reliable Sunday dinner.
steps: Heat the oven to 425 F. Take the chicken out of the fridge, remove any giblets, and pat the skin very dry.
Mash the butter with the garlic, thyme, rosemary and the lemon zest.
Loosen the skin over the breast with your fingers and spread about half of the herb butter under it. Rub the rest on the outside.
Season the chicken all over and inside the cavity with the salt and pepper. Put the lemon halves in the cavity.
Toss the onions with the olive oil in a roasting pan or large oven-safe skillet and set the chicken on top. Tie the legs together if you like.
Roast for 60 to 75 minutes, until the skin is deep golden and a thermometer in the thickest part of the thigh reads 165 F.
Rest the chicken for 15 minutes before carving.
Squeeze the second lemon over the carved chicken and serve with the roasted onions and pan juices.

title: Roast Turkey Breast
summary: A bone-in turkey breast rubbed with herb butter and roasted until juicy with golden skin. All the holiday flavor without cooking a whole bird.
steps: Heat the oven to 350 F. Pat the turkey breast very dry. For the best flavor, salt it up to a day ahead and leave it uncovered in the fridge.
Mix the butter with the garlic, sage, thyme, 1 teaspoon of the salt and the pepper.
Loosen the skin and rub half of the butter under it, then rub the rest over the skin.
Scatter the onion and carrots in a roasting pan, pour in the broth, and set the turkey on top, skin side up.
Roast for 1 1/2 to 2 hours, basting with the pan juices every 30 minutes, until the thickest part reads 160 F.
If the skin browns too fast, tent it loosely with foil.
Rest the turkey for 20 minutes. The temperature will rise to 165 F as it rests.
Carve the meat off the bone in slices and serve with the pan juices.

title: Herb Stuffing
summary: Cubes of toasted bread baked with butter, celery, onion and sage until crisp on top and tender inside. The side everyone goes back for at the holidays.
steps: Heat the oven to 300 F. Spread the bread cubes on two sheet pans and dry them in the oven for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring once, until crisp but not browned.
Raise the oven to 375 F and butter a 9x13 inch baking dish.
Melt 6 tablespoons of butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the onions and celery for 8 to 10 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic, sage and thyme and cook for 1 minute.
Put the bread in a large bowl and add the vegetables, parsley, salt and pepper.
Whisk the warm broth with the eggs and pour it over the bread. Toss gently until the bread is evenly moistened.
Spread the stuffing in the dish and cover with foil. Bake for 25 minutes.
Remove the foil and bake another 20 minutes until the top is golden and crisp.

title: Cranberry Sauce
summary: Fresh cranberries simmered with sugar and orange until they burst into a glossy, tangy sauce. It takes 15 minutes and beats the canned kind.
steps: Rinse the cranberries and pick out any soft or shriveled ones.
Combine the sugar, orange juice, water, zest, cinnamon stick and salt in a medium saucepan over medium heat and stir until the sugar dissolves.
Add the cranberries and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to a steady simmer and cook for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring now and then, until most of the berries have popped.
Press a few of the berries against the side of the pot if you want a thicker, smoother sauce.
Remove the cinnamon stick and let the sauce cool. It thickens a lot as it cools.
Chill for at least 1 hour. It keeps in the fridge for up to 1 week.

title: Mashed Potatoes
summary: Fluffy, buttery mashed potatoes with a hint of garlic. Simple, creamy and the right partner for nearly any dinner.

ingredients.name: russet potatoes
ingredients.prep: peeled and cut into 2 inch chunks

steps: Put the potatoes and garlic in a large pot, cover with cold water by 1 inch, and add the kosher salt.
Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer and cook for 15 to 20 minutes until a knife slides in with no resistance.
Drain well and return the potatoes to the hot pot over low heat for 1 minute to steam off extra moisture.
Mash with a masher or press through a ricer. Avoid a food processor, which makes them gluey.
Add the butter and stir until melted.
Pour in the warm milk a little at a time until the potatoes are as creamy as you like.
Season with the salt and pepper, taste, and serve hot.

title: Scalloped Potatoes
summary: Thin potato slices baked in a garlicky cream sauce until tender with a golden top. A rich side for ham, roast chicken or a holiday table.
steps: Heat the oven to 375 F and butter a 9x13 inch baking dish with a little of the butter.
Melt the remaining butter in a saucepan over medium heat and cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft. Add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Stir in the flour for 1 minute, then slowly whisk in the milk and cream.
Add the salt, pepper and nutmeg and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes until slightly thickened.
Layer half of the potatoes in the dish, pour over half of the sauce, and sprinkle with half of the cheese. Repeat with the rest.
Cover tightly with foil and bake for 45 minutes.
Uncover and bake another 30 to 40 minutes until the top is golden and the potatoes are tender when pierced.
Rest for 15 minutes so the sauce sets before serving.

title: Twice-Baked Potatoes
summary: Baked potatoes scooped out, mashed with sour cream, cheddar and bacon, then stuffed back in and baked until bubbly.
steps: Heat the oven to 400 F. Prick the potatoes with a fork, rub with the oil and kosher salt, and set them on a sheet pan.
Bake for 60 to 70 minutes until very tender. Let cool for 15 minutes.
Cut each potato in half lengthwise and scoop the flesh into a bowl, leaving a 1/4 inch wall so the skins hold their shape.
Mash the flesh with the butter, sour cream and milk until mostly smooth.
Stir in 1 cup of the cheddar, most of the bacon, half of the green onions, the salt and the pepper.
Spoon the filling back into the skins, mounding it, and set them on the sheet pan.
Top with the remaining cheese and bacon and bake for 15 to 20 minutes until hot and golden.
Sprinkle with the remaining green onions and serve.

title: Hash Browns
summary: Shredded potatoes pan-fried into a crisp, golden cake with a tender middle. The trick is squeezing the potatoes very dry first.
steps: Shred the potatoes on the large holes of a box grater.
Rinse the shreds in a bowl of cold water, swishing to remove the starch, then drain.
Wrap the potatoes in a clean kitchen towel and squeeze out as much water as you can. Dry potatoes crisp.
Toss the potatoes with the salt, pepper and onion powder.
Heat the oil and butter in a large nonstick or cast iron skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Spread the potatoes in an even layer and press down gently. Reduce the heat to medium and cook without stirring for 6 to 7 minutes until the bottom is deep golden.
Flip in sections with a wide spatula and cook another 5 to 6 minutes until crisp and cooked through.
Drain briefly on paper towels, season with a pinch more salt, and serve hot.

title: Home Fries
summary: Diner-style diced potatoes browned with onion and peppers until crisp outside and soft inside. A hearty breakfast side.
steps: Put the potatoes in a pot of salted cold water, bring to a boil, and cook for 5 to 6 minutes until just barely tender. Drain and let them steam dry for 5 minutes.
Heat the oil in a large cast iron or nonstick skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the potatoes in a single layer and cook without stirring for 5 minutes until the bottoms are golden.
Stir, then cook another 5 minutes, repeating until the potatoes are browned on most sides.
Add the butter, onion and bell pepper and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring, until the vegetables are soft.
Sprinkle with the paprika, garlic powder, salt and pepper and toss well.
Taste, adjust the salt, and serve hot with eggs.

photo.author: Marshall Astor from San Pedro, California, USA

title: Sweet Potato Fries
summary: Oven-baked sweet potato fries with crisp edges and a soft center. A cornstarch coat and a hot oven keep them from going soggy.

ingredients.name: sweet potatoes
ingredients.prep: peeled and cut into 1/2 inch sticks

steps: Heat the oven to 425 F with two sheet pans inside, or line them with parchment.
Soak the cut sweet potatoes in cold water for 20 minutes, then drain and dry them thoroughly with towels.
Toss the sticks with the cornstarch until lightly coated, then toss with the oil, paprika, garlic powder, salt and pepper.
Spread the fries in a single layer on the pans without crowding. Crowding makes them steam.
Bake for 15 minutes, flip, and bake 10 to 15 minutes more until the edges are crisp and browned.
Let the fries rest on the pan for 3 minutes to firm up, then serve right away.

title: Onion Rings
summary: Thick onion rings in a crunchy buttermilk batter, fried until golden. Crisp outside, sweet and soft inside.
steps: Separate the onion slices into rings and soak them in the buttermilk for 20 minutes.
Whisk 1 cup of the flour with the cornstarch, baking powder, paprika, salt and pepper in a shallow dish.
In another dish, whisk the egg with 1/2 cup of the soaking buttermilk. Put the panko in a third dish.
Heat 2 inches of oil in a heavy pot to 375 F.
Lift a few rings out of the buttermilk, dredge in the seasoned flour, dip in the egg mixture, then press into the panko.
Fry in small batches for 2 to 3 minutes, turning once, until deep golden.
Drain on a rack, sprinkle with salt right away, and keep warm in a 200 F oven while you fry the rest.

photo.author: Jess Sawrey from Los Angeles, California, USA

title: Baked Beans
summary: Slow-baked navy beans in a sweet and smoky sauce of molasses, brown sugar and bacon. Perfect for cookouts and potlucks.
steps: Heat the oven to 325 F.
Cook the bacon in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium heat for 6 to 8 minutes until crisp. Remove with a slotted spoon, leaving 2 tablespoons of fat in the pot.
Cook the onion in the fat for 5 minutes until soft, then add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Stir in the ketchup, molasses, brown sugar, mustard, Worcestershire, vinegar, pepper and water.
Fold in the beans and about two thirds of the bacon.
Bring to a simmer, then cover and bake for 1 hour.
Uncover and bake another 45 to 60 minutes, stirring once or twice, until the sauce is thick and glossy.
Top with the remaining bacon and let stand 10 minutes before serving.

title: Corn on the Cob with Herb Butter
summary: Sweet boiled corn slathered with garlic and herb butter. Summer on a plate in about 15 minutes.
steps: Mash the butter with the garlic, parsley, chives, thyme, salt and pepper until evenly mixed.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Do not salt it, which can toughen the corn.
Add the corn and cook for 4 to 6 minutes until the kernels are bright yellow and tender.
Lift the ears out with tongs and drain for a moment.
Spread a generous spoonful of herb butter over each hot ear and serve right away.

title: Roasted Brussels Sprouts with Bacon
summary: Brussels sprouts roasted until caramelized and crisp at the edges, tossed with salty bacon and a splash of balsamic vinegar.
steps: Heat the oven to 425 F and put a large sheet pan inside to heat up.
Toss the sprouts with the olive oil, salt and pepper.
Carefully spread the sprouts cut side down on the hot pan and scatter the bacon around them.
Roast for 20 minutes, then stir and flip the sprouts.
Roast another 8 to 12 minutes until the sprouts are deeply browned and the bacon is crisp.
Drizzle with the balsamic vinegar and maple syrup, toss, and serve warm.

title: Glazed Carrots
summary: Tender carrots cooked in butter and honey until they shine. A quick, sweet side that works for weeknights and holidays alike.

ingredients.name: carrots
ingredients.prep: peeled and sliced 1/4 inch thick on the diagonal

steps: Put the carrots, butter, honey, water, salt and pepper in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Bring to a boil, then cover and cook for 6 to 8 minutes until the carrots are almost tender.
Uncover and keep cooking, stirring often, for 5 to 7 minutes until the liquid cooks down to a shiny glaze.
Stir in the lemon juice and taste for salt.
Scatter with parsley and serve hot.

title: Succotash
summary: A summery skillet of corn, lima beans, peppers and onion in butter. It is colorful, fast and easy with frozen vegetables.
steps: Cook the bacon in a large skillet over medium heat for 5 to 6 minutes until crisp. Remove it to a plate and leave about 1 tablespoon of fat in the pan.
Add the onion and bell pepper and cook for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
Stir in the lima beans, corn and broth. Cover and simmer for 8 to 10 minutes until the beans are tender.
Uncover and cook for 2 minutes to reduce the liquid.
Stir in the butter, salt, pepper and most of the bacon.
Sprinkle with parsley and the remaining bacon and serve.

title: Fried Green Tomatoes
summary: Firm green tomato slices coated in a crunchy cornmeal crust and fried until golden. Tangy inside, crisp outside, and great with a little remoulade.
steps: Lay the tomato slices on paper towels, sprinkle with the salt, and let them sit for 10 minutes. Pat dry.
Put the flour in one shallow dish. Whisk the eggs with the buttermilk in a second dish.
In a third dish, mix the cornmeal, panko, paprika, pepper and garlic powder.
Dredge each slice in flour, dip in the egg mixture, then press firmly into the cornmeal mixture to coat both sides.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat to about 350 F.
Fry the slices in batches for 2 to 3 minutes per side until deep golden.
Drain on a rack, sprinkle with a pinch of salt, and serve hot.

title: Hush Puppies
summary: Crispy cornmeal fritters with a fluffy middle and a little onion. A Southern fish fry staple that disappears fast.
steps: Heat 2 inches of oil in a heavy pot to 350 F.
Whisk the cornmeal, flour, sugar, baking powder, salt and cayenne in a large bowl.
In a second bowl, whisk the buttermilk and egg, then stir in the grated onion.
Pour the wet mixture into the dry and stir until just combined. The batter will be thick.
Drop rounded tablespoons of batter into the hot oil, 5 or 6 at a time.
Fry for 2 to 3 minutes, turning once, until deep golden and cooked through.
Drain on a rack or paper towels and serve warm, with butter or tartar sauce.

title: Crab Cakes
summary: Mostly crab with just enough binder to hold together, pan-seared until crisp and golden. Serve with lemon or a quick tartar sauce.
steps: Whisk the mayonnaise, egg, mustard, Worcestershire, Old Bay and lemon juice in a large bowl.
Stir in the green onions, parsley and 1/2 cup of the panko.
Gently fold in the crab so the lumps stay mostly whole.
Shape into 8 patties about 3/4 inch thick, and press the outsides into the remaining panko.
Chill the patties on a plate for at least 30 minutes so they hold together. This is the key step.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Cook the crab cakes for 4 to 5 minutes per side until deep golden and hot through.
Serve right away with lemon wedges.

title: Lobster Roll
summary: Sweet chunks of lobster lightly dressed with mayo, lemon and celery in a buttery toasted split-top bun. A New England summer favorite.
steps: Pat the lobster meat dry with paper towels so the salad is not watery.
Stir the mayonnaise, lemon juice, celery, chives, salt and pepper together in a bowl.
Fold in the lobster gently until it is just coated. Chill for 10 minutes while you toast the buns.
Spread the butter on the outsides of the buns.
Toast the buns in a skillet over medium heat for 1 to 2 minutes per side until golden.
Pile the lobster salad into the warm buns and serve right away.

title: New England Fish and Chips
summary: Flaky white fish in a light, crisp beer batter with thick golden fries. Serve with tartar sauce, lemon and malt vinegar.
steps: Soak the potato wedges in cold water for 20 minutes. Drain and dry them completely.
Heat 2 inches of oil in a large heavy pot to 325 F. Fry the potatoes in batches for 5 to 6 minutes until pale and soft, then drain on a rack.
Raise the oil to 375 F.
Pat the fish dry and season with 1/2 teaspoon of the salt and the pepper. Dust lightly with the extra 1/2 cup flour.
Whisk 1 1/2 cups flour, the cornstarch, baking powder and 1 teaspoon salt. Whisk in the cold beer just until smooth. Do not overmix.
Dip each piece of fish in the batter, let the extra drip off, and lower it carefully into the oil.
Fry the fish for 4 to 5 minutes, turning once, until deep golden and the fish flakes. Drain on a rack.
Fry the potatoes a second time for 3 to 4 minutes until crisp and golden, then salt them with the remaining salt.
Serve right away with lemon wedges and tartar sauce.

title: Blackened Salmon
summary: Salmon coated in a smoky, spicy Cajun-style rub and seared in a hot skillet. It is ready in 15 minutes and finished with a squeeze of lemon.
steps: Mix the paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, thyme, oregano, cayenne, salt and pepper in a small bowl.
Pat the salmon dry, brush with the melted butter, and press the spice mix onto all sides.
Heat the oil in a large cast iron skillet over medium-high heat until it just begins to smoke. Turn on the vent fan.
Lay the fillets in the pan and cook for 3 to 4 minutes without moving until a dark crust forms.
Flip and cook another 3 to 4 minutes until the salmon flakes easily and reaches 130 to 140 F inside.
Serve right away with lemon wedges.

title: Shrimp Scampi
summary: Plump shrimp in a garlicky white wine and lemon butter sauce, tossed with linguine. Elegant enough for guests and ready in 25 minutes.

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.prep: plus more for the pasta water

steps: Cook the linguine in well-salted boiling water until al dente. Save 1/2 cup of the pasta water, then drain.
Pat the shrimp dry and season with the salt and pepper.
Heat the olive oil and 1 tablespoon of the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the shrimp for 1 to 2 minutes per side until just pink. Move to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium. Add 1 tablespoon of butter, the garlic and the red pepper flakes and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in the wine and lemon juice and simmer for 2 to 3 minutes until reduced by half.
Whisk in the remaining 2 tablespoons butter.
Add the linguine, shrimp, parsley and a splash of pasta water and toss until glossy and coated.
Taste, adjust the salt, and serve right away.

title: Fish Tacos with Lime Crema
summary: Spiced, pan-seared white fish in warm tortillas with crunchy cabbage and a cool lime crema. Fresh, fast and full of flavor.

ingredients.name: limes
ingredients.prep: 1 juiced and zested, 1 cut into wedges

steps: Whisk the sour cream, mayonnaise, lime juice, lime zest and a pinch of salt together for the crema. Chill until needed.
Pat the fish dry and toss with the chili powder, cumin, garlic powder and salt.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Cook the fish for 2 to 3 minutes per side until browned and it flakes easily.
Warm the tortillas one at a time in a dry skillet for 20 to 30 seconds per side, or wrap in foil and heat in a 350 F oven.
Fill each tortilla with fish, cabbage and avocado.
Drizzle with the lime crema and top with cilantro. Serve with lime wedges.

title: Beef Tacos
summary: Seasoned ground beef in warm tortillas or crisp shells, topped with all the fixings. A fast family dinner that everybody builds their own way.
steps: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the onion and cook for 3 minutes until soft.
Add the beef and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, breaking it up with a spoon, until browned. Drain off extra fat.
Stir in the garlic, chili powder, cumin, paprika, oregano and salt and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomato paste and water and simmer for 4 to 5 minutes until the sauce clings to the meat.
Warm the taco shells in a 350 F oven for 4 to 5 minutes.
Spoon the beef into the shells and top with lettuce, cheese, tomato, sour cream and salsa.

title: Chicken Quesadillas
summary: Crisp, golden tortillas stuffed with seasoned chicken, peppers and melty cheese. Great for lunch, dinner or a crowd.
steps: Toss the chicken with the chili powder, cumin, garlic powder and salt.
Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken for 5 to 6 minutes until browned and cooked through. Move it to a plate.
In the same skillet, cook the pepper and onion for 4 to 5 minutes until soft and lightly charred.
Wipe out the skillet and set it over medium heat with a thin film of the remaining oil.
Lay a tortilla in the pan, sprinkle half of it with cheese, then add a quarter of the chicken and vegetables and a little more cheese. Fold it over.
Cook for 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden and the cheese melts. Repeat with the others, adding oil as needed.
Rest for 1 minute, cut into wedges, and serve with salsa and sour cream.

title: Beef Burritos
summary: Seasoned ground beef, rice, beans and cheese rolled into warm flour tortillas. A filling weeknight dinner that reheats well.
steps: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the beef and cook, breaking it up, until browned, about 6 minutes.
Add the onion and cook until soft, about 4 minutes, then stir in the garlic for 30 seconds.
Stir in the taco seasoning and water. Simmer until most of the liquid is gone, about 3 minutes.
Fold in the black beans and rice and cook until hot, about 2 minutes. Take the pan off the heat.
Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet or wrapped in a damp paper towel in the microwave for 20 seconds so they bend without tearing.
Spoon about 3/4 cup of filling onto each tortilla and top with cheese and a spoonful of salsa.
Fold in the sides, then roll up tightly from the bottom.
For a crisp outside, brown the burritos seam side down in a lightly oiled skillet for 2 minutes per side.
Serve warm with sour cream and extra salsa.

title: Nachos
summary: A sheet pan of crisp chips under melted cheese, seasoned beef, beans and all the toppings. Easy to feed a crowd.
steps: Heat the oven to 400 F. Line a large rimmed baking sheet with parchment.
Brown the beef in a skillet over medium-high heat, breaking it up, about 6 minutes. Drain off extra fat.
Stir in the taco seasoning and water and simmer for 3 minutes until thick.
Spread half the chips on the baking sheet. Scatter half the beef, beans and cheeses over them.
Add the rest of the chips, beef, beans and cheese so more chips get topped.
Bake until the cheese is melted and bubbly, 6 to 8 minutes.
Top with jalapenos, tomatoes, salsa, sour cream, avocado and green onions.
Serve right away while the chips are still crisp.

title: Chicken Enchiladas with Red Sauce
summary: Shredded chicken and cheese rolled in corn tortillas, covered in red enchilada sauce and baked until bubbly.
steps: Heat the oven to 350 F. Spread 1/2 cup of the enchilada sauce in a 9 by 13 inch baking dish.
Mix the chicken, 1 cup of the cheese, the sour cream, onion and cumin in a bowl. Add salt if you like.
Warm the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Fry each tortilla for about 10 seconds per side, just to soften it, and drain on paper towels.
Dip each tortilla in the sauce, fill with about 1/3 cup of the chicken mixture and roll up.
Set the rolled enchiladas seam side down in the dish, packed snugly in a single layer.
Pour the remaining sauce over the top and sprinkle with the rest of the cheese.
Cover with foil and bake for 15 minutes. Uncover and bake 10 more minutes until bubbling.
Rest for 5 minutes, then sprinkle with cilantro and serve.

title: Cheese Enchiladas
summary: Corn tortillas stuffed with melty cheese and onion, smothered in red sauce. A simple meatless dinner.
steps: Heat the oven to 375 F. Spread 1/3 cup of the sauce over the bottom of a 9 by 13 inch dish.
Mix 2 cups of the cheddar with the Monterey Jack and onion.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Fry each tortilla about 10 seconds per side until pliable and drain on paper towels.
Dip each tortilla into the remaining sauce so it is coated.
Fill with a heaping 1/4 cup of the cheese mixture and roll up.
Place the enchiladas seam side down in the dish, side by side.
Pour the leftover sauce over the top, then add the last cup of cheddar and the olives.
Bake uncovered until the cheese is melted and the edges bubble, 15 to 20 minutes.
Serve with sour cream.

title: Breakfast Burritos
summary: Scrambled eggs, crispy potatoes, sausage and cheese in a warm tortilla. Make a batch and freeze extras for busy mornings.
steps: Heat the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat. Cook the potatoes with a pinch of salt, stirring now and then, until golden and tender, about 12 minutes. Move to a plate.
In the same pan, cook the sausage, breaking it up, until browned, about 6 minutes. Drain extra fat and add the pepper for the last 2 minutes.
Whisk the eggs, milk, salt and pepper together.
Pour the eggs into the pan and stir gently over medium-low heat until just set but still soft, about 3 minutes.
Fold the potatoes back in and take the pan off the heat.
Warm the tortillas so they do not tear. Sprinkle each with cheese, then add a scoop of the egg mixture.
Fold in the sides and roll up tightly.
Serve with salsa. To freeze, wrap each burrito in foil, freeze, and reheat from frozen in a 350 F oven for about 35 minutes.

title: Huevos Rancheros
summary: Fried eggs on crisp tortillas with warm refried beans and a simple chunky tomato sauce.
steps: Warm the refried beans in a small pot over low heat, stirring in a splash of water if they are thick.
Pour the salsa and cumin into another small pan and simmer for 5 minutes until slightly thickened.
Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Fry the tortillas one or two at a time until crisp at the edges, about 1 minute per side, and set aside.
Add the remaining oil to the pan and reduce the heat to medium. Crack in the eggs and fry with a pinch of salt until the whites are set, 3 to 4 minutes, so the yolks stay runny.
Spread beans over each tortilla and top with two eggs.
Spoon the warm sauce over and around the eggs.
Finish with queso fresco, avocado and cilantro and serve right away.

title: Western Omelet
summary: A fluffy diner-style omelet filled with ham, bell pepper, onion and cheddar.
steps: Melt half the butter in a 10 inch nonstick skillet over medium heat. Cook the ham, pepper and onion until the vegetables are soft, about 4 minutes. Move to a bowl.
Whisk the eggs, milk, a pinch of salt and some pepper until fully blended with no streaks.
Wipe out the skillet, add the remaining butter and melt it over medium heat.
Pour in the eggs. As the edges set, lift them with a spatula and tilt the pan so the raw egg runs underneath.
When the top is just barely wet, scatter the filling and cheese over one half.
Fold the other half over the filling and cook 1 more minute.
Slide onto a plate, cut in half and serve hot.

title: Scrambled Eggs and Toast
summary: Soft, creamy scrambled eggs cooked low and slow, with buttered toast on the side.
steps: Crack the eggs into a bowl, add the milk and a pinch of salt, and whisk until evenly yellow.
Start the bread in the toaster so it is ready when the eggs finish.
Melt half the butter in a nonstick skillet over medium-low heat.
Pour in the eggs and let them sit for about 20 seconds.
Stir slowly with a spatula, pushing the set curds from the edges toward the middle.
Pull the pan off the heat when the eggs look soft and slightly wet, since they keep cooking from the heat of the pan.
Butter the toast with the rest of the butter.
Season the eggs with pepper, top with chives and serve with the toast.

title: Eggs Benedict
summary: Poached eggs and Canadian bacon on toasted English muffins with a quick blender hollandaise.
steps: For the sauce, put the egg yolks, lemon juice, cayenne and a pinch of salt in a blender. Blend for 10 seconds.
With the blender running on low, slowly stream in the hot melted butter until the sauce is thick and creamy. Keep it warm in a cup set in a bowl of warm water.
Fill a wide pot with 3 inches of water, add the vinegar and bring it to a gentle simmer.
Crack each of the 8 eggs into its own small cup. Stir the water to make a gentle swirl and slip in four eggs.
Poach for 3 minutes for set whites and runny yolks. Lift out with a slotted spoon onto a towel and repeat with the other four.
Toast the English muffins and brown the Canadian bacon in a dry skillet for about 1 minute per side.
Stack bacon on each muffin half and top with a poached egg.
Spoon hollandaise over the top and sprinkle with chives and pepper. Serve at once.

title: Quiche Lorraine
summary: A classic custard quiche with bacon and Swiss cheese in a flaky crust.
steps: Heat the oven to 400 F. Fit the crust into a 9 inch deep pie plate and prick the bottom with a fork.
Line the crust with parchment and fill with pie weights or dry beans. Bake 12 minutes, remove the weights and bake 5 more minutes. Lower the oven to 350 F.
Cook the bacon in a skillet until crisp, drain on paper towels and crumble.
Scatter the bacon and cheese over the warm crust.
Whisk the eggs, cream, milk, nutmeg, salt and pepper until smooth.
Set the pie plate on a baking sheet and pour in the custard.
Bake until the center is just barely jiggly and a knife near the middle comes out clean, 35 to 40 minutes.
Cool for at least 15 minutes before slicing so the custard firms up.

title: French Toast
summary: Thick slices of bread soaked in cinnamon custard and griddled until golden. Great with maple syrup.
steps: Whisk the eggs, milk, sugar, vanilla, cinnamon and salt in a shallow dish until smooth.
Heat a large skillet or griddle over medium heat and melt a little of the butter.
Dip a slice of bread into the custard for about 10 seconds per side so it soaks in without falling apart.
Let the extra drip off, then lay it in the hot pan.
Cook until deep golden brown, about 3 minutes per side.
Repeat with the remaining bread, adding butter as needed, and keep finished slices on a rack in a 200 F oven.
Serve warm with maple syrup.

title: Belgian Waffles
summary: Light waffles with a crisp outside and airy middle, made with whipped egg whites.
steps: Heat a waffle iron according to its directions and heat the oven to 200 F to keep waffles warm.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, sugar and salt in a large bowl.
In another bowl, whisk the egg yolks, milk, melted butter and vanilla.
Pour the wet mixture into the dry and stir until just combined. A few lumps are fine.
Beat the egg whites in a clean bowl until stiff peaks form.
Fold the whites gently into the batter in two additions to keep it airy.
Lightly grease the waffle iron if needed and cook the batter until golden and crisp, about 4 minutes per waffle.
Keep finished waffles on a rack in the oven and serve with berries, butter and syrup.

title: Blueberry Muffins
summary: Tender bakery-style muffins packed with blueberries and topped with crunchy sugar.
steps: Heat the oven to 425 F and line a 12 cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk the flour, baking powder and salt in a large bowl.
In another bowl, whisk 3/4 cup of the sugar, oil, egg and vanilla, then whisk in the milk and sour cream.
Pour the wet mixture over the dry and fold until just combined. Do not overmix.
Gently fold in the blueberries.
Divide the batter among the cups, filling them nearly to the top, and sprinkle with the 2 tablespoons of topping sugar.
Bake at 425 F for 5 minutes, then lower the heat to 350 F and bake 16 to 18 minutes more, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool in the pan for 5 minutes, then move to a rack.

title: Banana Bread
summary: A moist, classic banana loaf. The riper the bananas, the better it tastes.
steps: Heat the oven to 350 F. Grease a 9 by 5 inch loaf pan.
Mash the bananas in a large bowl until mostly smooth.
Stir in the melted butter, then the sugar, egg and vanilla.
Sprinkle the baking soda and salt over the batter and stir them in.
Add the flour and mix just until no dry streaks remain, then fold in the walnuts if using.
Pour into the pan and smooth the top.
Bake 55 to 60 minutes, until a toothpick in the center comes out clean. Tent with foil if the top browns too fast.
Cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a rack and cool before slicing.

title: Zucchini Bread
summary: A moist spiced quick bread with shredded zucchini that stays tender for days.
steps: Heat the oven to 350 F. Grease two 8 by 4 inch loaf pans.
Wrap the shredded zucchini in a clean towel and squeeze out the extra water.
Whisk the flour, baking soda, baking powder, salt, cinnamon and nutmeg in a bowl.
In a large bowl, whisk the eggs, oil, both sugars and vanilla until smooth.
Stir in the zucchini, then add the dry ingredients and mix until just combined. Fold in the walnuts if using.
Divide the batter between the pans.
Bake 50 to 60 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool 10 minutes in the pans, then turn out onto a rack to cool fully.

title: Cinnamon Rolls
summary: Soft yeast rolls swirled with cinnamon sugar and topped with cream cheese icing.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.prep: divided: 1/3 cup melted for the dough, 1/4 cup softened for the filling, 2 tbsp softened for the icing

steps: Stir the warm milk, 1 tablespoon of the granulated sugar and the yeast in a large bowl. Let it foam, about 8 minutes.
Add the rest of the sugar, egg, melted butter, 3 cups of the flour and the salt. Mix, then knead on a floured counter for 6 to 8 minutes, adding flour as needed, until smooth.
Put the dough in a greased bowl, cover and let it rise in a warm spot until doubled, about 1 hour.
Mix the brown sugar and cinnamon. Roll the dough into a 12 by 16 inch rectangle, spread with the softened butter and cover with the cinnamon sugar.
Roll up from the long side into a log and cut into 12 equal rolls.
Place the rolls in a greased 9 by 13 inch pan, cover and let rise 30 minutes. Heat the oven to 350 F.
Bake 22 to 25 minutes, until light golden.
Beat the cream cheese, 2 tablespoons butter, powdered sugar and vanilla until smooth.
Spread the icing over the warm rolls and serve.

title: Overnight Oats
summary: No-cook oats soaked in milk and yogurt in the fridge. Grab a jar and go in the morning.
steps: Stir the oats, milk, yogurt, chia seeds, maple syrup, vanilla and salt together in a bowl.
Divide between two jars or containers and give each a good stir.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 6 hours or overnight.
Stir again in the morning. If it is too thick, add a splash of milk.
Top with blueberries and walnuts.
Eat cold, or warm it in the microwave for 1 minute. It keeps up to 4 days in the fridge.

title: Granola
summary: Crunchy oven-baked granola with big clusters, lightly sweetened with maple syrup and honey.
steps: Heat the oven to 325 F and line a large rimmed baking sheet with parchment.
Mix the oats, pecans, almonds, cinnamon and salt in a large bowl.
Warm the maple syrup, honey and oil in a small pot or microwave until runny, then stir in the vanilla.
Pour over the oat mixture and stir until every piece is coated.
Spread in an even layer on the baking sheet and press down firmly to help clusters form.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes, rotating the pan halfway, until golden. Do not stir.
Let it cool completely on the pan so it crisps up, then break into clusters and mix in the raisins.
Store in an airtight container for up to 2 weeks.

title: Breakfast Casserole
summary: An overnight-friendly bake of sausage, eggs, bread and cheddar. Assemble the night before and bake in the morning.
steps: Grease a 9 by 13 inch baking dish.
Brown the sausage in a skillet over medium-high heat, breaking it up, about 7 minutes. Drain well.
Spread the bread cubes in the dish and top with the sausage and 1 1/2 cups of the cheese.
Whisk the eggs, milk, mustard, salt and pepper until smooth and pour over the dish.
Press the bread down so it is mostly covered with egg. Cover and refrigerate at least 1 hour or overnight.
Heat the oven to 350 F and let the dish sit out while it heats.
Sprinkle with the remaining cheese and bake uncovered 45 to 50 minutes, until puffed, golden and set in the center.
Rest 10 minutes, then top with green onions and serve.

title: Sausage Egg and Cheese Biscuits
summary: Homemade buttery biscuits filled with a sausage patty, a fluffy egg and melted cheese.
steps: Heat the oven to 450 F and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, sugar and salt. Cut in the cold butter with a pastry cutter or your fingers until it looks like coarse crumbs with some pea-sized bits.
Stir in the buttermilk until a shaggy dough forms. Pat it to 3/4 inch thick on a floured counter.
Cut 6 rounds with a 3 inch cutter and set them close together on the sheet. Bake 12 to 14 minutes until golden.
Shape the sausage into 6 patties a bit wider than the biscuits. Cook in a skillet over medium heat, 4 to 5 minutes per side, until cooked through.
Fry or scramble the eggs in a lightly greased pan until set.
Split the warm biscuits. Fill each with a sausage patty, an egg and a slice of cheese.
Serve warm, or wrap and refrigerate for reheating.

title: Chicken Tenders
summary: Crunchy breaded chicken strips baked until golden, with a honey mustard dip.
steps: Heat the oven to 425 F. Set a wire rack on a baking sheet and spray it with oil.
Toss the panko with the oil, paprika, garlic powder, salt and pepper, and toast in a dry skillet for 3 minutes until lightly golden. Move to a shallow dish.
Put the flour in one dish and beat the eggs with the milk in another.
Pat the chicken dry. Dredge each piece in flour, dip in egg, then press into the panko to coat well.
Arrange the tenders on the rack with a bit of space between them.
Bake 15 to 18 minutes, flipping once halfway, until golden and the chicken reaches 165 F inside.
Stir the honey and mustard together for dipping.
Serve the tenders hot with the dip.

title: Hot Dogs with Onions
summary: Ballpark-style hot dogs topped with sweet, soft onions cooked in a skillet.
steps: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the onions and a pinch of salt and cook, stirring, for 10 minutes.
Sprinkle in the sugar and keep cooking for 5 to 8 minutes until the onions are soft and golden brown. Keep warm.
Cook the hot dogs in a grill pan or skillet over medium-high heat, turning often, until browned and hot, about 6 minutes.
Toast the buns in the pan or in a 350 F oven for 3 minutes.
Tuck a hot dog into each bun.
Pile on the onions and add mustard, ketchup and relish as you like.

title: Corn Dogs
summary: Hot dogs in a sweet cornmeal batter, fried until golden and crisp. A fair favorite made at home.
steps: Whisk the flour, cornmeal, sugar, baking powder and salt in a bowl. Add the egg and milk and stir to a thick batter. Pour into a tall glass for easy dipping.
Pat the hot dogs very dry and push a wooden skewer into each one, leaving a handle.
Roll each hot dog in the cornstarch so the batter sticks.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to 365 F.
Dunk a hot dog in the batter, turning to coat it fully and letting the extra drip off.
Lower it into the oil and fry, turning, until deep golden brown, 3 to 4 minutes. Cook two or three at a time.
Drain on a rack or paper towels.
Serve hot with mustard.

title: Pigs in a Blanket
summary: Little smoked sausages wrapped in flaky crescent dough and baked until golden. Perfect party food.
steps: Heat the oven to 375 F and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Unroll the crescent dough and separate it into triangles. Cut each triangle lengthwise into 3 thin triangles.
Pat the sausages dry with a paper towel so the dough sticks.
Place a sausage at the wide end of each dough strip and roll up toward the point.
Set them seam side down on the baking sheet.
Whisk the egg with the water and brush it over the dough. Sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Bake 12 to 15 minutes, until puffed and deep golden.
Serve warm with mustard.

title: Stuffed Bell Peppers with Rice and Beef
summary: Bell peppers filled with seasoned beef, rice and tomato, topped with melted cheese.
steps: Heat the oven to 350 F. Cut the tops off the peppers, remove the seeds and ribs, and stand them in a baking dish.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Brown the beef with the onion, about 7 minutes, then add the garlic for 1 minute and drain extra fat.
Stir in half the tomato sauce, the diced tomatoes with their juice, rice, Italian seasoning, salt and pepper. Simmer 5 minutes.
Stir in 1/2 cup of the cheese.
Spoon the filling into the peppers, packing it in.
Pour the rest of the tomato sauce over and around the peppers and add a splash of water to the dish.
Cover with foil and bake 35 minutes.
Uncover, top with the remaining cheese and bake 10 more minutes until the peppers are tender and the cheese is bubbly.

title: Stuffed Shells
summary: Jumbo pasta shells filled with a creamy three cheese mixture and baked in marinara.
steps: Heat the oven to 375 F. Boil the shells in salted water for 2 minutes less than the package time. Drain and cool on a baking sheet so they do not stick.
Mix the ricotta, 1 cup of the mozzarella, half the Parmesan, the egg, parsley, garlic powder, salt and pepper.
Spread 1 cup of the marinara in a 9 by 13 inch baking dish.
Spoon about 2 tablespoons of filling into each shell and set them open side up in the dish.
Pour the rest of the sauce over the shells.
Cover with foil and bake 25 minutes.
Uncover, sprinkle with the remaining mozzarella and Parmesan and bake 10 minutes more until bubbly.
Rest 5 minutes before serving.

title: Chicken Alfredo Bake
summary: Penne and chicken in a creamy Parmesan sauce, topped with golden melted cheese.
steps: Heat the oven to 375 F and grease a 9 by 13 inch baking dish.
Cook the penne 2 minutes less than the package directions. Drain.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Season the chicken with salt and pepper and cook until browned and cooked through, about 6 minutes. Move to a plate.
Melt the butter in the same pan, add the garlic for 30 seconds, then whisk in the flour for 1 minute.
Slowly whisk in the milk and cream. Simmer until slightly thickened, about 4 minutes.
Stir in the Parmesan and 1/2 cup of the mozzarella until smooth.
Fold the pasta and chicken into the sauce and pour into the baking dish.
Top with the remaining mozzarella and bake 20 minutes until bubbly and golden.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve.

title: Cajun Chicken Pasta
summary: Spicy blackened chicken with peppers in a creamy Cajun sauce over fettuccine.
steps: Cook the fettuccine in salted water until al dente. Save 1/2 cup of the pasta water, then drain.
Toss the chicken with 1 tablespoon of the Cajun seasoning.
Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken until browned and cooked through, 5 to 6 minutes. Move to a plate.
Add the remaining oil and the peppers and cook until crisp-tender, about 4 minutes. Add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Pour in the cream, broth and remaining Cajun seasoning. Simmer 4 to 5 minutes until it thickens a little.
Stir in the Parmesan until melted.
Return the chicken to the pan, add the pasta and toss, adding pasta water to loosen the sauce as needed.
Top with green onions and serve.

title: Pasta Primavera
summary: Spring vegetables tossed with pasta in a light garlicky lemon Parmesan sauce.
steps: Boil the penne in salted water until al dente. Save 1/2 cup of the pasta water, then drain.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the broccoli, zucchini and pepper with a pinch of salt for 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and tomatoes and cook 2 minutes more, until the tomatoes just begin to soften.
Add the peas and broth and simmer 2 minutes.
Stir in the butter until melted.
Add the drained pasta, Parmesan and lemon juice and toss, adding pasta water a splash at a time until the sauce coats everything.
Season with salt and pepper, top with basil and serve.

title: Garlic Bread
summary: Crusty bread brushed with garlic butter and herbs, baked until crisp outside and soft inside.
steps: Heat the oven to 400 F and line a baking sheet with foil.
Slice the loaf in half lengthwise and set both halves cut side up on the sheet.
Mash the butter with the garlic, parsley and salt until evenly mixed.
Spread the garlic butter generously over the cut sides, all the way to the edges.
Sprinkle with Parmesan if using.
Bake 8 to 10 minutes, until the butter is melted and the edges are golden.
For extra color, broil 1 minute while watching closely.
Slice and serve warm.

title: Dinner Rolls
summary: Soft, buttery pull-apart rolls with a tender crumb. Make them ahead and reheat for any holiday table.
steps: Stir the warm milk, yeast and a spoonful of the sugar in a large bowl. Let it sit about 5 minutes until foamy.
Whisk in the rest of the sugar, the melted butter and the egg.
Add the flour and salt and stir until a shaggy dough forms.
Knead on a lightly floured counter for 8 minutes, or 5 minutes in a stand mixer with the dough hook, until smooth and slightly tacky.
Put the dough in a greased bowl, cover, and let rise in a warm spot for about 1 hour, until doubled.
Punch down the dough and divide it into 12 equal pieces. Roll each into a smooth ball.
Arrange the balls in a greased 9x13 inch pan, cover, and let rise 30 minutes until puffy.
Heat the oven to 375 F. Bake 18 to 20 minutes, until deep golden brown.
Brush the hot rolls with melted butter and serve warm.

title: Chocolate Chip Cookies
summary: Classic cookies with crisp edges and chewy centers. Chilling the dough makes them thicker and more flavorful.
steps: Whisk the flour, baking soda and salt in a bowl.
Beat the butter, sugar and brown sugar for 2 to 3 minutes, until light and fluffy.
Beat in the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla.
Stir in the flour mixture until just combined, then fold in the chocolate chips.
Chill the dough for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 375 F and line two baking sheets with parchment.
Scoop rounded tablespoons of dough about 2 inches apart on the sheets.
Bake 9 to 11 minutes, until the edges are golden and the centers still look slightly soft.
Cool on the pan for 5 minutes, then move to a rack.

title: Oatmeal Raisin Cookies
summary: Chewy, spiced cookies packed with oats and plump raisins. A lunchbox favorite.
steps: Heat the oven to 350 F and line two baking sheets with parchment.
Beat the butter, brown sugar and sugar until fluffy, about 2 minutes.
Beat in the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla.
Whisk the flour, baking soda, cinnamon and salt, then stir into the butter mixture.
Stir in the oats and raisins until evenly mixed.
Scoop heaping tablespoons of dough onto the sheets, 2 inches apart.
Bake 10 to 12 minutes, until the edges are set and lightly browned.
Cool on the pan for 5 minutes, then transfer to a rack.

title: Snickerdoodles
summary: Soft, tangy cookies rolled in cinnamon sugar. Cream of tartar gives them their signature flavor.
steps: Heat the oven to 375 F and line two baking sheets with parchment.
Beat the butter and 1 1/2 cups sugar until light, about 2 minutes. Beat in the eggs and vanilla.
Whisk the flour, cream of tartar, baking soda and salt, then mix into the butter mixture.
Chill the dough for 20 minutes if it feels very soft.
Mix the remaining 2 tbsp sugar with the cinnamon in a small bowl.
Roll the dough into 1 1/2 inch balls and coat each in the cinnamon sugar.
Place the balls 2 inches apart on the sheets.
Bake 9 to 10 minutes, until the edges are set but the centers look soft.
Cool on the pan for 5 minutes before moving to a rack.

title: Sugar Cookies
summary: Soft rolled cookies that hold their shape for cutting. Frost them or enjoy them plain.
steps: Beat the butter and sugar until light and fluffy, about 2 minutes. Beat in the egg and vanilla.
Whisk the flour, baking powder and salt, then mix into the butter until a soft dough forms.
Divide the dough in half, flatten into disks, wrap, and chill for 1 hour.
Heat the oven to 350 F and line baking sheets with parchment.
Roll one disk on a floured surface to 1/4 inch thick.
Cut out shapes with floured cookie cutters and place them 1 inch apart on the sheets.
Bake 8 to 10 minutes, until the edges just start to turn golden.
Cool on the pan for 5 minutes, then move to a rack. Repeat with the remaining dough and decorate when cool.

title: Fudgy Brownies
summary: Dense, shiny-topped brownies made in one bowl. Rich with cocoa and chocolate chips.
steps: Heat the oven to 350 F. Line an 8 inch square pan with parchment, leaving an overhang for lifting.
Whisk the melted butter and sugar in a bowl until combined.
Whisk in the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla, for about 1 minute until glossy.
Sift in the cocoa, flour, salt and baking powder and fold until just combined.
Fold in the chocolate chips.
Spread the batter in the pan.
Bake 25 to 28 minutes, until a toothpick comes out with a few moist crumbs.
Cool completely in the pan before lifting out and cutting into 16 squares.

title: Blondies
summary: Chewy brown sugar bars with butterscotch flavor and chocolate chips. Easy to stir together by hand.
steps: Heat the oven to 350 F. Line an 8 inch square pan with parchment.
Whisk the melted butter and brown sugar until smooth.
Whisk in the egg and vanilla.
Stir in the flour, baking powder and salt until just combined.
Fold in the chocolate chips and the walnuts if using.
Spread the batter evenly in the pan.
Bake 22 to 25 minutes, until golden and set at the edges with a slightly soft center.
Cool completely in the pan, then lift out and cut into squares.

title: Rice Krispie Treats
summary: Gooey marshmallow bars that take about 10 minutes. No oven needed.
steps: Grease a 9x13 inch pan with butter or cooking spray.
Melt the butter in a large pot over low heat.
Add the marshmallows and stir until completely melted and smooth.
Remove from the heat and stir in the vanilla if using.
Quickly stir in the cereal until evenly coated.
Press the mixture into the pan with a greased spatula or wax paper. Do not pack it too hard.
Let it set for 30 minutes, then cut into squares.

title: Peach Cobbler
summary: Juicy cinnamon peaches under a golden, buttery biscuit crust. Serve warm with ice cream.
steps: Heat the oven to 375 F.
Toss the peaches with 1/2 cup of the sugar, the lemon juice, cinnamon and cornstarch. Spread in a 2 quart baking dish.
Whisk the flour, the remaining 1/4 cup sugar, the baking powder and salt.
Cut in the cold butter with your fingers or a pastry cutter until the mixture looks like coarse crumbs.
Stir in the milk and vanilla just until a thick batter forms.
Drop spoonfuls of the batter over the peaches, leaving some gaps.
Bake 40 to 45 minutes, until the topping is golden and the fruit is bubbling.
Cool 15 minutes before serving.

title: Apple Crisp
summary: Tender cinnamon apples under a crunchy oat topping. Warm, simple, and good with vanilla ice cream.
steps: Heat the oven to 350 F and grease a 9x13 inch baking dish.
Toss the apples with the sugar, lemon juice and 1/2 tsp of the cinnamon. Spread in the dish.
Mix the oats, flour, brown sugar, salt and remaining 1/2 tsp cinnamon in a bowl.
Work in the cold butter with your fingers until the topping is crumbly with some pea-sized clumps.
Sprinkle the topping evenly over the apples.
Bake 40 to 45 minutes, until the apples are tender and the topping is golden.
Cool 10 minutes and serve warm.

title: Blueberry Pie
summary: A double-crust pie bursting with juicy berries and a hint of lemon. Cool it fully so the filling sets.
steps: Heat the oven to 425 F with a rack in the lower third and a baking sheet underneath to catch drips.
Gently mix the blueberries, 2/3 cup of the sugar, cornstarch, lemon juice, zest and salt.
Fit one crust into a 9 inch pie plate and pour in the filling. Dot with the butter.
Top with the second crust, trim and crimp the edges, and cut 4 slits in the top.
Brush the top with the egg wash and sprinkle with the remaining sugar.
Bake 20 minutes, then lower the oven to 375 F and bake 35 to 40 minutes more, until golden and bubbling in the center.
Cover the edges with foil if they brown too fast.
Cool at least 4 hours before slicing.

title: Cherry Pie
summary: A double-crust pie with a sweet-tart cherry filling. Frozen cherries work all year.

ingredients.name: cherries
ingredients.prep: pitted, fresh or thawed frozen and drained, about 24 oz

steps: Heat the oven to 425 F with a baking sheet on the lower rack.
Stir the cherries, sugar, cornstarch, lemon juice, almond extract and salt in a large bowl.
Fit one crust into a 9 inch pie plate and pour in the filling. Dot with butter.
Cover with the second crust, or cut it into strips for a lattice. Trim and crimp the edges.
Cut vents in a solid top crust and brush everything with the egg wash.
Bake 20 minutes, then reduce the oven to 375 F and bake 35 to 40 minutes, until the crust is deep golden and the juices bubble thickly.
Tent the edges with foil if they brown too quickly.
Cool at least 4 hours so the filling sets.

title: Sweet Potato Pie
summary: A silky, spiced Southern pie with a smooth custard filling. Roast the sweet potatoes for deeper flavor.
steps: Heat the oven to 400 F. Prick the sweet potatoes and roast on a lined sheet for 45 to 60 minutes, until very soft. Lower the oven to 350 F.
Peel the potatoes and mash until completely smooth. Measure about 2 cups.
Beat in the butter while the potatoes are still warm.
Beat in the sugar, brown sugar, eggs, evaporated milk and vanilla.
Mix in the cinnamon, nutmeg and salt. For extra smoothness, press the filling through a sieve.
Fit the crust into a 9 inch pie plate and crimp the edges.
Pour in the filling.
Bake 50 to 55 minutes, until the center is just set with a slight wobble.
Cool completely before slicing.

title: Banana Pudding
summary: Layers of creamy vanilla pudding, ripe bananas and soft vanilla wafers. A potluck classic that chills in the fridge.
steps: Whisk the pudding mix and cold milk for 2 minutes, then let it thicken for 5 minutes.
Whisk in the sweetened condensed milk and vanilla until smooth.
Whip the heavy cream to stiff peaks, then fold it into the pudding.
Line the bottom of a 3 quart dish with a layer of vanilla wafers.
Top the wafers with a layer of banana slices, then a layer of pudding.
Repeat the layers, ending with pudding.
Crush a few wafers and sprinkle over the top.
Cover and chill at least 4 hours so the wafers soften.

title: Chocolate Cake
summary: A moist, deeply chocolatey layer cake with a fudgy frosting. Hot coffee or water in the batter keeps it tender.
steps: Heat the oven to 350 F. Grease and line two 9 inch round pans.
Whisk the sugar, flour, 3/4 cup of the cocoa, baking powder, baking soda and salt in a large bowl.
Add the eggs, 1 cup of the milk, the oil and vanilla and beat until smooth.
Stir in the hot water. The batter will be thin.
Divide between the pans and bake 30 to 35 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool 10 minutes in the pans, then turn out onto racks to cool completely.
For the frosting, beat the butter until creamy, then beat in the powdered sugar and the remaining 1/2 cup cocoa, alternating with the remaining 1/3 cup milk, until fluffy.
Spread frosting between the layers and over the top and sides.

title: Yellow Cake with Chocolate Frosting
summary: A tender buttery birthday-style cake under rich chocolate buttercream. Reliable and crowd-pleasing.
steps: Heat the oven to 350 F. Grease and line two 9 inch round pans.
Whisk the flour, baking powder and salt together.
Beat 1 cup of the butter with the sugar for 3 minutes until pale and fluffy.
Beat in the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla.
Add the flour mixture in three parts, alternating with the milk, mixing just until smooth.
Divide the batter between the pans and bake 28 to 32 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool 10 minutes in the pans, then turn out onto racks and cool completely.
For the frosting, beat the remaining 1 cup butter until creamy. Beat in the powdered sugar and cocoa, then the cream, until light and spreadable.
Stack the layers with frosting between them and cover the top and sides.

title: Red Velvet Cake
summary: A soft, tangy cocoa cake with a bold red color and cream cheese frosting. A showstopper for special days.
steps: Heat the oven to 350 F. Grease and line two 9 inch round pans.
Whisk the flour, sugar, cocoa, baking soda and salt in a large bowl.
In another bowl, whisk the oil, buttermilk, eggs, food coloring, 1 tsp of the vanilla and the vinegar.
Pour the wet mixture into the dry and whisk until smooth.
Divide between the pans and bake 28 to 32 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool 10 minutes in the pans, then turn out onto racks and cool completely.
For the frosting, beat the cream cheese and butter until smooth. Beat in the powdered sugar and remaining 2 tsp vanilla until fluffy.
Frost between the layers and over the top and sides. Chill 30 minutes for neat slices.

title: Pineapple Upside-Down Cake
summary: A buttery caramelized pineapple topping baked over a tender vanilla cake. Flip it while it is still warm.
steps: Heat the oven to 350 F.
Melt 1/4 cup of the butter in a 9 inch cake pan or oven-safe skillet and stir in the brown sugar. Spread it evenly over the bottom.
Arrange the pineapple rings on the sugar and put a cherry in the center of each ring if using.
Whisk the flour, baking powder and salt.
Beat the remaining 1/2 cup butter with the sugar until fluffy. Beat in the eggs and vanilla.
Add the flour mixture in two parts, alternating with the milk, mixing until just smooth.
Spoon the batter over the pineapple and smooth the top.
Bake 40 to 45 minutes, until golden and a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool 10 minutes, run a knife around the edge, and flip onto a plate. Serve warm.
