title: Strawberry Shortcake
summary: Flaky buttermilk biscuits piled with juicy strawberries and fresh whipped cream. A summer favorite.
steps: Toss the strawberries with 1/3 cup of the sugar and let them sit for 30 minutes until juicy.
Heat the oven to 425 F and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Whisk the flour, the remaining 1/3 cup sugar, baking powder and salt.
Cut in the cold butter until the mixture looks like coarse crumbs.
Stir in the buttermilk just until a shaggy dough forms.
Pat the dough to 1 inch thick and cut out 6 rounds. Place them on the sheet.
Bake 15 to 18 minutes, until golden brown. Cool slightly.
Whip the cream with the powdered sugar and vanilla to soft peaks.
Split the warm biscuits, spoon in strawberries and cream, and add more on top.

title: Lemon Bars
summary: A buttery shortbread crust topped with a bright, tart lemon custard. Dust with powdered sugar before serving.
steps: Heat the oven to 350 F. Line a 9x13 inch pan with parchment, leaving an overhang.
Mix the butter, 1/2 cup powdered sugar, 1 3/4 cups of the flour and the salt until a soft dough forms. Press into the pan.
Bake the crust 18 to 20 minutes, until lightly golden.
Whisk the eggs, sugar, lemon juice, zest and the remaining 1/4 cup flour until smooth.
Pour the filling over the hot crust.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes more, until the center is set and no longer jiggles.
Cool completely in the pan, then chill 1 hour for clean cuts.
Lift out, cut into squares, and dust with powdered sugar.

title: Chocolate Pudding
summary: Silky stovetop pudding made from scratch with cocoa and cornstarch. Ready in 15 minutes, then chilled.
steps: Whisk the sugar, cocoa, cornstarch and salt in a medium saucepan.
Gradually whisk in the milk until no lumps remain.
Cook over medium heat, whisking constantly, until the mixture thickens and bubbles, about 6 to 8 minutes.
Keep whisking for 1 more minute, then remove from the heat.
Stir in the butter, vanilla and the chocolate chips if using, until smooth.
Pour into 4 small dishes or a bowl.
Press plastic wrap onto the surface to prevent a skin and chill at least 2 hours.

title: Rice Pudding
summary: Creamy stovetop rice pudding with cinnamon and a touch of vanilla. Comforting warm or cold.
steps: Bring the rice and water to a boil in a heavy saucepan. Cover, lower the heat, and simmer 15 minutes until the water is absorbed.
Stir in the milk, sugar and salt.
Cook uncovered over medium-low heat, stirring often, for 25 to 30 minutes, until thick and creamy.
Whisk the egg with the cream in a small bowl.
Stir a few spoonfuls of the hot rice into the egg mixture, then stir it all back into the pot.
Cook 2 minutes more, stirring, until slightly thicker. Do not boil.
Remove from the heat and stir in the vanilla, cinnamon and raisins if using.
Serve warm, or chill and stir in a splash of milk before serving.

title: Bread Pudding with Vanilla Sauce
summary: Custardy baked bread pudding with cinnamon and raisins, topped with a warm buttery vanilla sauce.
steps: Heat the oven to 350 F and butter a 9x13 inch baking dish.
Spread the bread cubes in the dish and scatter the raisins over them.
Whisk the milk, eggs, 3/4 cup of the sugar, 2 tsp of the vanilla, cinnamon and nutmeg.
Pour the custard over the bread and press down gently. Let it soak 15 minutes.
Bake 40 to 45 minutes, until puffed, golden and set in the center.
For the sauce, melt the butter in a small saucepan. Stir in the remaining 1/2 cup sugar and the cream.
Simmer 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until the sugar dissolves and the sauce thickens slightly. Stir in the remaining 1 tsp vanilla.
Serve the pudding warm with the sauce spooned over.

title: Lemonade
summary: Fresh-squeezed lemonade with a simple syrup base. Tart, sweet, and very refreshing.
steps: Warm the sugar and 1 cup of the water in a small saucepan, stirring until the sugar dissolves. Let the syrup cool.
Squeeze the lemons and strain out the seeds.
Stir the lemon juice and cooled syrup together in a large pitcher.
Add the remaining 4 cups cold water and stir.
Taste and add more sugar or water as you like.
Chill until cold, then serve over ice with lemon slices.

title: Sweet Tea
summary: Smooth Southern-style iced tea sweetened while hot. A pinch of baking soda keeps it from tasting bitter.
steps: Bring 4 cups of the water to a boil in a saucepan.
Remove from the heat, add the tea bags and baking soda, and steep 5 minutes.
Remove the tea bags without squeezing them.
Stir the sugar into the hot tea until dissolved.
Pour into a pitcher and add the remaining 4 cups cold water.
Chill until cold and serve over ice with lemon slices if you like.

title: Chocolate Milkshake
summary: A thick, frosty diner-style shake made with three simple ingredients. Add malt powder for the old-fashioned touch.
steps: Chill two tall glasses in the freezer while you gather the ingredients.
Put the ice cream, milk and chocolate syrup in a blender.
Blend on low speed, then medium, until smooth and thick, about 30 seconds.
Add a splash more milk if it is too thick to blend, or a little more ice cream if it is too thin.
Pour into 2 chilled glasses.
Top with whipped cream if you like and serve right away with a straw.

title: Hot Chocolate
summary: Rich stovetop hot chocolate made with cocoa, chocolate and milk. Better than any packet.
steps: Whisk the cocoa, sugar and salt in a small saucepan.
Whisk in a splash of the milk to make a smooth paste.
Whisk in the rest of the milk and warm over medium heat until steaming, but not boiling.
Add the chocolate chips and whisk until melted and smooth.
Remove from the heat and stir in the vanilla.
Pour into mugs and top with marshmallows if you like.

title: Caramel Popcorn
summary: Crunchy baked popcorn coated in buttery brown sugar caramel. Great for movie night and gifts.
steps: Heat the oven to 250 F. Line two rimmed baking sheets with parchment.
Pop the kernels in a large pot with the oil, covered, until the popping slows. Pour into a very large bowl, discarding any unpopped kernels.
Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Stir in the brown sugar, corn syrup and salt.
Bring to a boil and cook without stirring for 4 minutes.
Remove from the heat and stir in the baking soda and vanilla. It will foam.
Pour the caramel over the popcorn and fold gently until coated.
Spread on the sheets and bake 45 minutes, stirring every 15 minutes.
Cool completely, then break into pieces.

title: Ranch Dressing
summary: Tangy, herby buttermilk ranch that beats the bottled kind. Great for salads, wings and veggies.
steps: Whisk the mayonnaise, sour cream and buttermilk until smooth.
Stir in the lemon juice, parsley, dill, garlic powder, onion powder, chives, salt and pepper.
Taste and adjust the salt and pepper.
Thin with a splash more buttermilk if you want a pourable dressing.
Cover and chill at least 30 minutes so the flavors blend.
Keep in the fridge up to 5 days.

title: Barbecue Sauce
summary: A sweet, tangy and smoky sauce made from pantry staples. Simmer once and use it on ribs, chicken or burgers.
steps: Combine the ketchup, vinegar, brown sugar, molasses and Worcestershire sauce in a medium saucepan.
Whisk in the mustard powder, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, pepper, salt and cayenne if using.
Whisk in the water.
Bring to a simmer over medium heat, then reduce the heat to low.
Simmer uncovered for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring often, until thickened to your liking.
Taste and adjust with more vinegar, sugar or salt.
Cool and store in a jar in the fridge for up to 2 weeks.

title: Mapo Eggplant
summary: Tender eggplant simmered in a spicy, savory Sichuan-style sauce with a little ground pork. Serve it over rice.
steps: Toss the eggplant with 1/2 teaspoon salt in a colander and let it sit for 15 minutes, then pat dry.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat and cook the eggplant until golden and softened, about 6 minutes. Move it to a plate.
Add the remaining oil and the pork. Cook, breaking it up, until browned, about 4 minutes.
Stir in the doubanjiang, garlic and ginger and cook for 30 seconds until the oil turns red.
Add the broth, soy sauce, wine and sugar, then return the eggplant to the pan.
Simmer for 6 to 8 minutes, until the eggplant is very tender.
Stir the cornstarch into the water and pour it in. Cook for 1 minute until the sauce turns glossy.
Top with the scallions and the ground Sichuan pepper if using, and serve with steamed rice.

title: Dan Dan Noodles
summary: Chewy noodles in a nutty, spicy sesame sauce with crispy seasoned pork. Mix it all together at the table.
steps: Whisk the sesame paste with the soy sauce, vinegar, chili oil, sugar and half the garlic until smooth, then whisk in the hot broth.
Heat the vegetable oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and cook the pork until browned and crisp at the edges, about 6 minutes.
Add the remaining garlic, the wine and a splash of soy sauce, plus the preserved greens if using. Cook 2 minutes more.
Boil the noodles in a large pot of water according to the package, usually 3 to 5 minutes.
Drain the noodles well and divide them among four bowls.
Spoon the sauce over the noodles, then top with the pork.
Sprinkle with scallions and peanuts, and toss everything together before eating.

title: Scallion Pancakes
summary: Flaky, chewy pan-fried flatbreads layered with scallions and sesame oil. Great with a soy dipping sauce.
steps: Stir the flour and 1/2 teaspoon salt in a bowl, pour in the boiling water, and mix with chopsticks until shaggy.
Add the cold water and knead for about 5 minutes until the dough is smooth. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Divide the dough into 4 pieces. Roll one out very thin into a rough circle.
Brush with sesame oil, sprinkle with some of the remaining salt and scallions.
Roll it up into a long log, then coil it into a snail shape and tuck the end underneath. Flatten with your palm and roll out to a 6 inch round. Repeat with the rest.
Heat a thin layer of vegetable oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Fry each pancake for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until golden and crisp.
Cut into wedges and serve with the soy sauce and vinegar mixed for dipping.

title: Pork and Chive Dumplings
summary: Juicy pork and garlic chive filling folded into store-bought wrappers, then pan-fried or boiled. A good weekend project.

ingredients.name: soy sauce
ingredients.prep: divided: 1 tablespoon for the filling, 3 for dipping

steps: Mix the pork with 1 tablespoon of the soy sauce, the wine, sesame oil, ginger, salt and white pepper.
Stir in the broth a little at a time in one direction until the mixture is sticky and springy.
Fold in the chives just before wrapping so they do not release water.
Put a heaping teaspoon of filling in the center of a wrapper, wet the edge, and fold into a half moon, pleating the edge to seal.
Heat the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat and arrange the dumplings flat side down.
Fry until the bottoms are golden, about 2 minutes.
Pour in the water, cover, and steam for 6 to 7 minutes until the filling is cooked through and the water is gone.
Uncover and cook 1 more minute to re-crisp the bottoms.
Mix the remaining 3 tablespoons soy sauce with the vinegar for dipping and serve hot.

title: Pan-Fried Pork Buns
summary: Fluffy yeast buns stuffed with juicy pork, steamed in the pan and crisped on the bottom. Sheng jian bao at home.
steps: Stir the yeast and sugar into the warm water and let it foam for 5 minutes.
Mix in the flour and knead for 8 minutes until smooth. Cover and let rise for 1 hour until doubled.
Mix the pork with the soy sauce, wine, sesame oil, ginger and a pinch of salt, then stir in the broth until the filling is loose and sticky. Mix in the scallions.
Divide the dough into 12 pieces and roll each into a 4 inch round, thinner at the edges.
Fill each with a spoonful of filling and pleat the edges closed, pinching to seal.
Rest the buns on a floured tray for 15 minutes.
Heat the oil in a large nonstick skillet with a lid over medium heat and place the buns pleated side up.
Fry until the bottoms are golden, 2 to 3 minutes.
Add the water, cover, and steam for 8 to 10 minutes until the water is gone.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and cook uncovered for 1 minute more.

title: Steamed Pork Buns
summary: Soft, pillowy buns filled with sweet and savory pork. Steam a batch and freeze extras.
steps: Stir the yeast and 1 tablespoon of the sugar into the milk and let it foam for 5 minutes.
Mix in the flour, remaining sugar, oil and baking powder, then knead for 8 minutes until smooth.
Cover and let the dough rise for 1 hour until doubled.
Cook the pork in a skillet until no longer pink, then stir in the hoisin, soy sauce, oyster sauce and sesame oil.
Stir the cornstarch with 2 tablespoons water, add it to the pan, and cook until thick. Add the scallions and cool the filling.
Divide the dough into 12 pieces and roll each into a 4 inch round.
Spoon filling onto each, gather the edges up, and pinch closed.
Set each bun on a square of parchment and let rest for 20 minutes.
Steam the buns in a steamer over boiling water for 12 minutes, spaced apart.
Turn off the heat and wait 2 minutes before lifting the lid so the buns do not collapse.

title: Xiaolongbao Soup Dumplings
summary: Delicate dumplings that hold hot soup inside, made with a gelatin-rich broth that melts as they steam. Plan ahead for chilling.

ingredients.name: ginger
ingredients.prep: divided: 1 tablespoon grated, 1 tablespoon cut into thin matchsticks

steps: Warm the broth, whisk in the gelatin until dissolved, then chill in a shallow dish until firm, at least 2 hours.
Mix the flour with the hot water, knead until smooth, cover, and rest for 30 minutes.
Mix the pork with the soy sauce, wine, grated ginger (saving the matchsticks), sesame oil, salt and sugar until sticky.
Chop the set gelatin into small bits and fold it into the pork.
Roll the dough into a log and cut it into 30 pieces. Roll each into a 3 inch round, thinner at the edges.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center and pleat the edges up into a pouch, twisting the top closed.
Line a bamboo steamer with parchment or cabbage leaves and set the dumplings in it, spaced apart.
Steam over boiling water for 8 to 10 minutes.
Serve right away with the vinegar and ginger matchsticks. Bite a small hole and sip the soup first.

title: Shrimp Har Gow
summary: Translucent dim sum dumplings with a snappy shrimp filling. The wheat starch wrapper takes a little practice.
steps: Mix the shrimp with the bamboo shoots, cornstarch, sesame oil, sugar, salt and white pepper, plus the pork fat if using. Chill for 30 minutes.
Stir the wheat starch and tapioca starch together in a bowl.
Pour in the boiling water and stir quickly until a shaggy dough forms, then add the oil.
Knead the warm dough until smooth, then cover with a damp towel.
Roll the dough into a log and cut it into 24 pieces, keeping the rest covered.
Press each piece flat with the side of an oiled cleaver or a tortilla press into a thin 3 inch round.
Put a spoonful of filling in the center, fold the wrapper over, and pleat one side to seal.
Line a steamer with parchment and place the dumplings in it, spaced apart.
Steam over high heat for 6 to 7 minutes, until the wrappers are translucent.
Serve warm with soy sauce or chili oil.

title: Pork Siu Mai
summary: Open-topped dim sum dumplings with a bouncy pork and shrimp filling. Easy once you have the wrappers.
steps: Mix the pork, shrimp and mushrooms with the cornstarch, soy sauce, wine, sesame oil, sugar, ginger and white pepper.
Stir in one direction for 2 minutes until the filling is sticky and holds together.
Trim square wrappers into rounds if needed.
Hold a wrapper in your hand, place a heaping tablespoon of filling in the middle, and squeeze the sides up around it so it forms a cup with an open top.
Flatten the top with a spoon and tap the bottom so it stands flat.
Top each with a bit of diced carrot.
Line a steamer with parchment and set the siu mai in it, spaced apart.
Steam over boiling water for 10 to 12 minutes until the filling is firm.
Serve hot with soy sauce or chili oil.

title: Char Siu Barbecue Pork
summary: Sweet, sticky, red-edged roast pork in the Cantonese style. Great sliced over rice or tucked into buns.
steps: Whisk the hoisin, soy sauce, 2 tablespoons honey, wine, brown sugar, oyster sauce, five spice, garlic and sesame oil, plus the food coloring if using.
Put the pork in a zip bag with two thirds of the marinade, saving the rest. Refrigerate at least 4 hours or overnight.
Heat the oven to 425 F and line a rimmed baking sheet with foil. Set a rack on top.
Place the pork on the rack and pour a cup of water into the bottom of the pan to prevent burning.
Roast for 15 minutes, then brush with the reserved marinade.
Flip, roast 15 minutes more, and brush again.
Mix the last tablespoon of honey with a spoonful of water and brush on the pork.
Broil for 3 to 5 minutes until charred at the edges.
Rest the pork for 10 minutes, then slice against the grain.

title: Cantonese Roast Pork Belly
summary: Pork belly with shatteringly crisp crackling over juicy, seasoned meat. It needs an overnight dry-out in the fridge.
steps: Simmer the pork belly in a pot of water for 10 minutes, then drain and pat very dry.
Poke the skin all over with a skewer or a fork so the holes go through the skin but not into the meat.
Rub the wine, five spice, sugar and white pepper with 1 tablespoon salt into the meat side only.
Brush the skin with the vinegar and let it dry.
Refrigerate the belly uncovered, skin side up, for at least 8 hours or overnight until the skin feels like paper.
Heat the oven to 300 F. Cover the sides and bottom with foil, leaving the skin exposed, and rub the skin with the remaining salt.
Roast for 1 hour 15 minutes.
Raise the heat to 475 F and roast for 15 to 20 minutes more, watching closely, until the skin puffs and turns golden.
Rest for 15 minutes, then chop through the crackling with a heavy knife and serve.

title: Soy Sauce Chicken
summary: Whole chicken gently poached in a fragrant, sweet soy braise until glossy and tender. Serve with rice and the braising liquid.
steps: Combine the soy sauces, wine, rock sugar, water, ginger, scallions, star anise, cinnamon and garlic in a pot big enough for the chicken.
Bring to a boil and simmer for 10 minutes so the flavors blend.
Lower the chicken in breast side down, adding hot water if needed to cover about three quarters of it.
Cover and simmer very gently for 15 minutes.
Flip the chicken breast side up and simmer, covered, for 20 minutes more, until a thermometer in the thigh reads 165 F.
Turn off the heat and let the chicken sit in the liquid for 10 minutes.
Lift it out and rest for 10 minutes, then chop into pieces.
Spoon some of the braising liquid over the top and serve with rice.

photo.author: Dennis Wong from Hong Kong, Hong Kong

title: White Cut Chicken with Ginger Scallion Sauce
summary: Poached chicken that stays silky and juicy, served with a bright ginger and scallion oil. Simple and clean tasting.

ingredients.name: ginger
ingredients.prep: divided: 4 slices for the pot, the rest finely minced for the sauce

ingredients.name: scallions
ingredients.prep: divided: 3 cut into 2 inch lengths for the pot, the rest thinly sliced (about 1 cup) for the sauce

steps: Put the chicken in a pot with 4 ginger slices, the scallion lengths and the kosher salt, then add cold water to cover.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to a bare simmer.
Cover and cook for 20 minutes.
Turn off the heat and leave the pot covered for 30 minutes, until a thermometer in the thigh reads 165 F.
Move the chicken to a bowl of ice water for 10 minutes to firm the skin, then drain and pat dry.
Mix 1/2 cup minced ginger and 1 cup sliced scallions in a heatproof bowl with the salt.
Heat the oil until shimmering and pour it over the ginger and scallions. Stir in the soy sauce and vinegar.
Chop the chicken into pieces and serve with the sauce and rice.

title: Three Cup Chicken
summary: Taiwanese braised chicken in sesame oil, soy sauce and rice wine with lots of garlic and basil. Sticky, savory and fragrant.
steps: Pat the chicken dry. Heat the vegetable oil in a wide pot or clay pot over medium-high heat.
Brown the chicken in batches, about 3 minutes per side, then set aside.
Lower the heat to medium and add the sesame oil, ginger, garlic and chilies if using. Cook until the garlic is golden, about 2 minutes.
Return the chicken to the pot and add the soy sauce, wine and sugar.
Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Uncover, raise the heat, and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring, until the sauce is thick and clings to the chicken.
Stir in the basil until just wilted and serve with rice.

title: Cashew Chicken
summary: A takeout favorite made at home: tender chicken, crisp vegetables and toasted cashews in a glossy brown sauce.

ingredients.name: cornstarch
ingredients.prep: divided: 1 tablespoon for the chicken, 2 teaspoons for the sauce

steps: Toss the chicken with 1 tablespoon cornstarch and the wine and let it sit for 10 minutes.
Whisk the oyster sauce, soy sauce, sesame oil, broth and the sauce cornstarch together.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a wok over high heat and sear the chicken until browned and cooked through, about 5 minutes. Remove it.
Add the remaining oil and stir-fry the onion, celery and pepper for 3 minutes.
Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 30 seconds.
Return the chicken to the pan and pour in the sauce.
Cook for 1 to 2 minutes until the sauce is thick and glossy.
Stir in the cashews and serve over rice.

title: Lemon Chicken
summary: Crisp-coated chicken pieces tossed in a sweet-tart lemon sauce. Serve right away so they stay crunchy.

ingredients.name: cornstarch
ingredients.prep: divided: 1/2 cup for the coating, 1 tablespoon for the sauce

steps: Toss the chicken with the salt and beaten egg.
Mix the 1/2 cup cornstarch with the flour and coat each piece well, pressing it on.
Whisk the broth, lemon juice, sugar, honey, lemon zest and sauce cornstarch in a small saucepan.
Cook the sauce over medium heat, stirring, until it thickens and turns glossy, about 3 minutes.
Heat the oil in a deep skillet to 350 F.
Fry the chicken in two batches for 4 to 5 minutes until deep golden and cooked through.
Drain on a rack or paper towels.
Toss the chicken with the warm sauce, top with scallions, and serve with lemon slices.

title: Sesame Chicken
summary: Crispy fried chicken in a sticky, sweet and savory sesame sauce. Quick enough for a weeknight if you prep first.

ingredients.name: chicken thighs
ingredients.prep: boneless, skinless, cut into bite-size pieces

ingredients.name: cornstarch
ingredients.prep: divided: 1/2 cup for the coating, 1 tablespoon for the sauce

steps: Toss the chicken with the egg until coated.
Mix the cornstarch and flour and dredge the chicken, pressing it on.
Whisk the honey, soy sauce, vinegar, ketchup, sesame oil and garlic in a saucepan.
Stir the sauce cornstarch into the water, add it to the pan, and simmer 2 to 3 minutes until thick.
Heat the oil in a deep skillet to 350 F.
Fry the chicken in batches for 5 minutes until golden and cooked through, then drain.
Toss the hot chicken with the sauce until glossy.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and scallions and serve with rice.

title: Honey Walnut Shrimp
summary: Crispy shrimp in a creamy honey-mayonnaise sauce with candied walnuts. A restaurant classic that is easier than it looks.
steps: Boil the walnuts in a pot of water for 2 minutes, drain, and toss with the sugar while still warm.
Fry the walnuts in 1 cup of the oil for 2 to 3 minutes until golden, then drain on parchment and keep the oil for later.
Whisk the mayonnaise, honey, condensed milk and lemon juice in a large bowl.
Toss the shrimp with the salt and egg white, then coat well in the cornstarch.
Heat the oil to 350 F, adding more if needed.
Fry the shrimp in batches for 2 to 3 minutes until golden and crisp, then drain.
Toss the hot shrimp in the sauce until coated.
Top with the candied walnuts and serve right away.

title: Salt and Pepper Shrimp
summary: Shell-on shrimp fried until crackly, then tossed with garlic, chilies and a peppery salt. Eat them whole.

ingredients.name: shell-on shrimp
ingredients.prep: large, deveined with the shell left on

steps: Snip the shrimp shells along the back, devein, and pat very dry.
Toss the shrimp with the cornstarch and 1 teaspoon salt until lightly coated.
Heat the oil in a wok or deep pot to 375 F.
Fry the shrimp in two batches for 1 to 2 minutes until crisp and pink, then drain on a rack.
Pour off all but 1 tablespoon of oil.
Stir-fry the garlic, jalapenos and scallions over high heat for 1 minute.
Return the shrimp and sprinkle with the black pepper, Sichuan pepper if using, and a pinch of salt.
Toss for 30 seconds and serve hot.

title: Salt and Pepper Tofu
summary: Crisp-edged tofu cubes with a creamy middle, tossed with garlic, chilies and scallions.

ingredients.name: extra-firm tofu
ingredients.prep: drained and pressed, cut into 1 inch cubes

steps: Pat the pressed tofu very dry.
Mix the cornstarch with half the salt and pepper, and toss the tofu cubes to coat.
Heat the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the tofu in a single layer for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until golden and crisp. Work in batches if needed.
Move the tofu to a plate.
Add the garlic, chili and scallions to the pan and cook for 30 seconds.
Return the tofu, add the remaining salt and pepper plus the five spice if using, and toss to coat.
Serve hot with rice or as a snack.

title: Garlic Shrimp Stir-Fry
summary: Plump shrimp and plenty of garlic in a light savory sauce. It cooks in minutes.
steps: Pat the shrimp dry and toss with 1 teaspoon of the soy sauce.
Mix the remaining soy sauce, wine, sugar, cornstarch and water in a small bowl.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat.
Add the shrimp in a single layer and sear for 1 minute per side until just pink, then remove.
Lower the heat to medium and cook the garlic, ginger and pepper flakes if using for 30 seconds.
Return the shrimp, add the scallions, and pour in the sauce.
Toss for 1 minute until the sauce is glossy.
Drizzle with the sesame oil and serve over rice.

title: Shrimp with Lobster Sauce
summary: Shrimp in a silky egg-ribboned white sauce with ground pork and garlic. The sauce has no lobster in it.
steps: Heat the oil in a wok over high heat and cook the pork until browned, about 3 minutes.
Add the garlic and fermented black beans if using, and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the shrimp and cook 2 minutes until just pink.
Pour in the broth, wine, soy sauce and white pepper and bring to a simmer.
Stir the cornstarch into the water and add it, stirring until the sauce thickens, about 1 minute.
Lower the heat to medium and slowly drizzle in the eggs while stirring gently so they form ribbons.
Turn off the heat, sprinkle with scallions, and serve with rice.

title: Steamed Fish with Ginger and Scallions
summary: Delicate whole or fillet fish steamed until just done, then finished with sizzling oil and soy. Clean, fast and elegant.

ingredients.name: white fish fillets
ingredients.prep: such as cod, sea bass or snapper

steps: Pat the fish dry and set it on a heatproof plate with half the ginger scattered on top.
Bring water to a boil in a wok or large pot with a rack or steamer.
Steam the fish over high heat for 8 to 10 minutes, until it flakes easily at the thickest part.
While it steams, mix the soy sauce, wine, sugar, water and sesame oil.
Carefully pour off any liquid that collected on the plate.
Top the fish with the remaining ginger, the scallions, and cilantro if using.
Heat the vegetable oil until it just begins to smoke and pour it over the scallions so they sizzle.
Spoon the soy mixture around the fish and serve with rice.

title: Sweet and Sour Fish
summary: Crispy fried fish pieces in a glossy sweet and sour sauce with peppers and pineapple.

ingredients.name: cornstarch
ingredients.prep: divided: 1/2 cup for the coating, 1 tablespoon for the sauce

steps: Pat the fish dry, dip in the egg, then coat in the cornstarch.
Whisk the sugar, vinegar, ketchup, water, soy sauce and sauce cornstarch in a bowl.
Heat the oil in a deep skillet to 350 F.
Fry the fish in batches for 3 to 4 minutes until golden and crisp, then drain.
Pour off all but 1 tablespoon of oil from a wok or skillet.
Stir-fry the pepper and onion for 2 minutes over high heat.
Add the pineapple and the sauce and cook until thick and glossy, about 2 minutes.
Pour the sauce over the fish, or gently fold it in, and serve right away.

photo.author: Yun Huang Yong from Harbord, Australia

title: Red Braised Pork Belly
summary: Shanghai-style pork belly simmered until melting in a glossy, sweet soy sauce. Worth the wait.

ingredients.name: pork belly
ingredients.prep: skin on, cut into 1.5 inch cubes

steps: Blanch the pork in boiling water for 3 minutes, then drain and rinse.
Heat the oil in a wok or heavy pot over low heat and melt the sugar until it turns amber, about 3 minutes.
Add the pork and stir to coat in the caramel for 3 to 4 minutes.
Add the wine, soy sauce, dark soy sauce, ginger, scallions, star anise and cinnamon.
Pour in the water so the pork is almost covered and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer on low for 1 hour 15 minutes, until the pork is tender.
Uncover, raise the heat, and cook for 10 to 15 minutes, stirring, until the sauce reduces to a sticky glaze.
Serve over rice with a green vegetable.

title: Twice-Cooked Pork
summary: Sichuan pork belly simmered, sliced thin, then stir-fried with leeks in a spicy bean sauce.

ingredients.name: leeks
ingredients.prep: cut on the diagonal, white and light green parts only

steps: Simmer the pork in water with the ginger and scallions for 25 minutes, until just cooked through.
Cool the pork, then chill for 20 minutes so it slices easily.
Slice it very thin, about 1/8 inch.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat and fry the pork slices until the edges curl and brown, about 4 minutes.
Push the pork aside and add the doubanjiang, black beans if using, and garlic. Cook for 30 seconds until the oil turns red.
Stir in the hoisin, soy sauce and sugar.
Add the leeks and pepper and stir-fry for 2 to 3 minutes until crisp-tender.
Toss everything together and serve with rice.

title: Fish-Fragrant Pork
summary: Sichuan shredded pork in a sweet, sour and spicy sauce with wood ear mushrooms and bamboo. It has no fish at all.
steps: Toss the pork with the cornstarch and wine and let it sit for 10 minutes.
Mix the soy sauce, sugar, vinegar and broth in a bowl.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat and stir-fry the pork for 2 to 3 minutes until browned. Remove it.
Lower the heat to medium and cook the doubanjiang, garlic and ginger for 30 seconds until the oil turns red.
Add the bamboo shoots and mushrooms and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Return the pork and pour in the sauce.
Cook over high heat for 2 minutes until the sauce clings to the pork.
Stir in the scallions and serve with rice.

title: Fish-Fragrant Eggplant
summary: Silky eggplant in a sweet, sour, garlicky and mildly spicy Sichuan sauce. There is no fish in it.
steps: Toss the eggplant with 1 teaspoon salt and let it sit for 10 minutes, then pat dry.
Whisk the soy sauce, sugar, vinegar, cornstarch and water.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat and fry the eggplant in batches for 5 minutes until soft and golden, adding oil as needed. Remove it.
Lower the heat to medium and cook the doubanjiang, garlic and ginger for 30 seconds.
Return the eggplant and pour in the sauce.
Simmer for 3 to 4 minutes until the sauce is thick and the eggplant is tender.
Stir in the scallions and serve with rice.

title: Dry-Fried Green Beans
summary: Blistered green beans with garlic and a little pork, a Sichuan favorite. Cook them until wrinkled for the best flavor.
steps: Pat the green beans completely dry.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat and cook the beans, stirring now and then, for 6 to 8 minutes until wrinkled and blistered. Remove them.
Pour off all but 1 tablespoon of oil and cook the pork until browned, about 3 minutes.
Add the garlic, ginger, chilies and preserved greens if using. Cook for 30 seconds.
Return the beans to the wok and add the soy sauce, sugar and wine.
Toss over high heat for 1 minute.
Drizzle with the sesame oil and serve.

title: Garlic Bok Choy
summary: Crisp-tender bok choy with a lot of garlic and a light sauce. Ready in about ten minutes.
steps: Rinse the bok choy well, spreading the leaves to wash out any grit, and drain.
Mix the oyster sauce, soy sauce, sugar and water in a small bowl.
Heat the oil in a large skillet or wok over high heat.
Add the bok choy cut side down and cook for 2 minutes until lightly browned.
Add the garlic and stir for 20 seconds, without letting it burn.
Pour in the sauce, cover, and cook for 2 minutes until the stems are crisp-tender.
Drizzle with the sesame oil and serve right away.

title: Stir-Fried Gai Lan with Oyster Sauce
summary: Crisp Chinese broccoli in a glossy garlicky oyster sauce, ready in about 15 minutes. A classic side for any rice dinner.
steps: Trim the tough bottoms off the gai lan and cut thick stems in half lengthwise so they cook evenly. Rinse and shake dry.
Stir the oyster sauce, soy sauce, sugar, cornstarch and chicken broth together in a small bowl.
Bring a pot of water to a boil. Blanch the gai lan for 1 minute, then drain well.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat until shimmering.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir for about 15 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the gai lan and toss for 1 minute.
Stir the sauce again and pour it in. Cook, tossing, until it bubbles and turns glossy, about 1 minute.
Turn off the heat, drizzle with sesame oil and serve right away.

title: Stir-Fried Water Spinach with Garlic
summary: Tender hollow-stemmed water spinach tossed in a very hot wok with lots of garlic. It cooks in a few minutes, so have everything ready first.
steps: Wash the water spinach well in a few changes of water. Cut the stems and leaves into 3 inch lengths and keep stems and leaves in separate piles.
Shake off as much water as you can so the wok does not steam instead of sear.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat until it just begins to smoke.
Add the garlic and the red pepper flakes if using, and stir for 10 seconds.
Add the stems first and toss for 30 seconds.
Add the leaves, rice wine, soy sauce, salt and sugar.
Toss constantly for 1 to 2 minutes, until the leaves wilt and the stems are tender but still crisp.
Serve immediately with some of the garlicky juices spooned over the top.

title: Hot and Sour Shredded Potatoes
summary: Matchstick potatoes rinsed of starch and flash-fried with vinegar and dried heat stay crunchy and tangy. A famous cheap and cheerful home dish.

ingredients.name: potatoes
ingredients.prep: peeled and cut into thin matchsticks

steps: Cut the potatoes into thin matchsticks, about 1/8 inch thick.
Rinse them in cold water several times until the water runs mostly clear, then soak for 10 minutes and drain well.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the Sichuan peppercorns and chilies and stir until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Add the garlic, then turn the heat to high and add the potatoes.
Stir-fry for 2 minutes, then add the vinegar, soy sauce, salt and sugar.
Keep tossing for 2 to 3 more minutes, until the potatoes are tender but still crunchy.
Toss in the green onions and serve hot.

title: Stir-Fried Cabbage with Vinegar
summary: Torn cabbage seared over high heat and finished with a splash of vinegar. Smoky, tangy and ready in 15 minutes.

ingredients.name: cabbage
ingredients.prep: about 1 1/2 lb, torn into bite-size pieces

steps: Remove the tough core from the cabbage and tear the leaves into pieces about 2 inches wide. Keep the thick pieces and thin leafy pieces separate.
Mix the soy sauce, vinegar, sugar and salt in a small bowl.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat. Add the dried chilies and garlic and stir for 10 seconds.
Add the thick cabbage pieces and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add the leafy pieces and keep tossing until the edges begin to char, about 2 more minutes.
Pour the sauce around the edge of the wok so it sizzles.
Toss for 30 seconds and serve right away while crisp.

title: Smashed Cucumber Salad
summary: Cucumbers smashed into rough chunks soak up a garlicky, tangy dressing better than slices ever would. Cool, crunchy and quick.
steps: Lay the cucumbers on a cutting board and smash each one with the flat side of a cleaver or a heavy pan until it splits.
Tear or cut the smashed cucumbers into bite-size chunks.
Toss with the salt in a bowl and let sit for 10 minutes to draw out water.
Drain off the liquid.
Whisk the garlic, soy sauce, black vinegar, sugar, sesame oil and chili oil together.
Pour the dressing over the cucumbers and toss well.
Top with cilantro and serve cold, ideally within an hour.

title: Wood Ear Mushroom Salad
summary: Chewy, crunchy wood ear mushrooms in a sharp garlic and black vinegar dressing. A refreshing cold appetizer you can make ahead.
steps: Soak the dried wood ear in plenty of warm water for 30 minutes until fully soft. They expand a lot.
Rinse well and trim off any hard knots, then tear into bite-size pieces.
Boil the wood ear in a pot of water for 3 minutes, then drain and cool under cold water.
Whisk the garlic, black vinegar, soy sauce, sugar, sesame oil and chili oil in a large bowl.
Add the wood ear, carrots, green onions and cilantro.
Toss well and chill for at least 15 minutes before serving.

title: Tiger Salad
summary: A northeastern Chinese salad of cilantro, green onion, cucumber and chilies with a punchy soy and vinegar dressing. It is bright, sharp and very fresh.

ingredients.name: cilantro
ingredients.prep: stems and leaves, cut into 2 inch pieces

steps: Wash the cilantro and green onions and dry them very well so the dressing does not get watery.
Cut the cilantro, green onions and cucumber into similar lengths, about 2 inches.
Combine them in a large bowl with the sliced chilies.
Whisk the garlic, soy sauce, rice vinegar, sugar, sesame oil and salt in a small bowl until the sugar dissolves.
Pour the dressing over the salad just before serving and toss gently.
Serve right away so everything stays crisp.

title: Cold Sesame Noodles
summary: Chewy noodles in a creamy sesame and peanut sauce with garlic, chili and a hit of vinegar. Good straight from the fridge, so it is great for meal prep.
steps: Cook the noodles in boiling water according to the package until just tender.
Drain, rinse under cold water until cool, and toss with a teaspoon of sesame oil so they do not stick.
Whisk the tahini, peanut butter, soy sauce, rice vinegar, sugar, remaining sesame oil, chili oil, garlic and ginger in a bowl.
Add the hot water a little at a time, whisking, until the sauce is smooth and pourable.
Toss the noodles with the sauce until every strand is coated.
Top with cucumber, green onions and sesame seeds.
Serve right away, or chill for up to 2 days and loosen with a splash of water before eating.

title: Chongqing Hot and Sour Noodles
summary: Street-food style noodles in a spicy, tangy, numbing sauce with peanuts and greens. You build the sauce in the bowl and the hot noodles do the rest.
steps: Toast the Sichuan peppercorns in a dry pan for 1 minute, then grind them to a powder.
Divide the garlic, chili oil, soy sauce, black vinegar, sugar, sesame oil and ground peppercorns between two large bowls.
Pour the hot chicken broth into each bowl and stir to make the sauce.
Boil the noodles until just tender, adding the spinach for the last 30 seconds of cooking.
Drain the noodles and spinach well and divide between the bowls.
Toss to coat, then top with peanuts and green onions.
Serve immediately, stirring from the bottom as you eat.

title: Zhajiangmian
summary: Noodles topped with a rich, salty-sweet pork and fermented bean sauce, with crunchy raw vegetables on the side. The Beijing home classic.
steps: Mix the sweet bean sauce, doubanjiang, soy sauce, rice wine and sugar with the chicken broth in a bowl.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the garlic and ginger and stir for 20 seconds.
Add the pork and break it up. Cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and cook for 3 minutes.
Pour in the sauce mixture, bring to a simmer, and cook over medium-low heat for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring often, until thick and glossy.
Meanwhile, cut the cucumber and carrot into matchsticks and blanch the bean sprouts for 30 seconds.
Boil the noodles until tender and drain.
Divide the noodles into bowls, spoon the pork sauce on top and arrange the vegetables around it. Toss everything before eating.

title: Biang Biang Noodles
summary: Wide, chewy hand-stretched noodles from Shaanxi, topped with sizzling chili oil, garlic and vinegar. The dough only needs flour, water and salt.

ingredients.name: hot water
ingredients.prep: about 1 cup, a little less if the dough is wet

ingredients.name: vegetable oil
ingredients.prep: about 2 tbsp for the dough, the rest for sizzling

steps: Stir the flour and 1 tsp salt together and mix in the water until a shaggy dough forms.
Knead for 8 to 10 minutes until smooth, then rub with a little oil, cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Divide the dough into 6 pieces and roll each into a long rectangle about 1/4 inch thick. Brush with oil, cover and rest 10 more minutes.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Take one piece at a time, press a groove down the middle with a chopstick, then pull the two ends out to a long wide ribbon.
Tear each ribbon along the groove into two noodles and drop into the boiling water. Repeat with the rest.
Cook the noodles for 2 to 3 minutes, adding the bok choy for the last 30 seconds, then drain.
Put the garlic, chili flakes, ground peppercorns, soy sauce and vinegar over the noodles in a large bowl.
Heat the 1/3 cup oil until it just starts to smoke and pour it over the chili and garlic so it sizzles.
Top with green onions and toss everything together.

title: Scallion Oil Noodles
summary: Noodles tossed in slowly fried scallion oil with soy sauce. The Shanghai favorite that makes something wonderful out of almost nothing.

ingredients.name: green onions
ingredients.prep: white and green parts, cut into 2 inch pieces

steps: Cut the green onions into 2 inch pieces and dry them very well.
Put the oil and green onions in a small pot over medium-low heat.
Cook slowly for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring now and then, until the green onions are deep golden brown and crisp. Do not let them turn black.
Remove the pot from the heat and stir in the soy sauce, dark soy sauce and sugar. It will bubble, so stand back.
Boil the noodles until tender, saving a few tablespoons of cooking water, then drain.
Toss the noodles with the scallion oil and a splash of cooking water.
Serve topped with the fried green onions.

title: Chicken Chow Mein
summary: Tender chicken, crisp vegetables and noodles in a savory sauce. A quick takeout favorite made at home in one pan.
steps: Toss the chicken with 1 tbsp of the soy sauce and the cornstarch and let it sit for 10 minutes.
Mix the remaining soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar, sesame oil and chicken broth in a small bowl.
Cook the noodles in boiling water until just tender, drain and toss with a little oil.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok over high heat and cook the chicken until browned and cooked through, about 4 minutes. Remove it to a plate.
Add another tbsp of oil and stir-fry the carrots, celery and cabbage for 3 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook for 15 seconds.
Add the remaining oil and the noodles, and toss for 2 minutes.
Return the chicken, add the sauce and green onions, and toss until everything is hot and coated.

title: Beef Chow Fun
summary: Wide rice noodles seared in a very hot wok with tender beef and bean sprouts. The smoky wok flavor is the goal, so cook in small batches.

ingredients.name: rice noodles
ingredients.prep: fresh wide, or dried wide rice noodles

steps: Toss the beef with 1 tbsp soy sauce, the rice wine and the cornstarch and let it sit for 15 minutes.
If using dried noodles, soak them in warm water until pliable. If using fresh, gently separate the strands.
Mix the remaining soy sauce, dark soy sauce, oyster sauce and sugar in a small bowl.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok over very high heat and sear the beef for 1 to 2 minutes until just browned. Remove to a plate.
Add 2 tbsp oil, then the ginger, and the noodles. Spread them out and let them sit for 30 seconds to sear, then toss gently.
Pour in the sauce and toss until the noodles are evenly colored.
Add the bean sprouts, green onions and beef.
Toss for 1 minute, until the sprouts are just wilted, and serve immediately.

title: Shrimp Lo Mein
summary: Soft egg noodles tossed with plump shrimp and vegetables in a savory soy and oyster sauce. It comes together in about 25 minutes.
steps: Boil the noodles until just tender. Drain, rinse briefly and toss with a little oil.
Mix the soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar and sesame oil in a small bowl.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large wok over high heat. Cook the shrimp for 2 minutes until pink, then remove to a plate.
Add the remaining oil, then the carrots and mushrooms, and stir-fry for 3 minutes.
Add the garlic, ginger and cabbage and cook for 1 minute.
Add the noodles and sauce and toss for 2 minutes to heat through.
Return the shrimp, add the green onions and toss for 30 seconds before serving.

title: Yangzhou Fried Rice
summary: The classic banquet fried rice with shrimp, ham, egg and peas. Cold day-old rice is the secret to separate, fluffy grains.

ingredients.name: white rice
ingredients.prep: cooked and cold, about 1 1/3 cups uncooked

steps: Break up any clumps in the cold rice with your fingers.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok over high heat. Scramble the eggs until just set, then remove to a plate.
Add another tbsp of oil and cook the shrimp for 2 minutes until pink. Remove them as well.
Add the last tbsp of oil, then the ham, carrots and peas, and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add the rice and press it into the pan, tossing every 20 seconds, for 3 to 4 minutes until hot and some grains begin to toast.
Add the soy sauce, rice wine, salt and white pepper and toss.
Return the eggs and shrimp, add the green onions, and break up the eggs as you toss.
Serve hot.

title: Egg Fried Rice
summary: Fluffy rice with soft egg and green onions, simple and satisfying. It is the best way to use leftover rice.

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.prep: beaten with a pinch of salt

steps: Break up the cold rice with your hands so there are no big clumps.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok over high heat. Pour in the eggs and stir until they are about 80 percent set, then remove them.
Add the remaining oil and the green onion whites and stir for 10 seconds.
Add the rice and toss for 3 to 4 minutes until hot and bouncing in the pan.
Add the soy sauce, salt and white pepper and toss.
Return the eggs and break them into small pieces.
Stir in the green parts of the green onions and the sesame oil and serve.

title: Pineapple Fried Rice
summary: Sweet pineapple, savory ham and crunchy cashews in a curry-scented fried rice. Serve it in a hollowed pineapple if you want to show off.
steps: Break up any clumps in the cold rice.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok over high heat. Scramble the eggs, then remove them to a plate.
Add the remaining oil, then the garlic and ham, and cook for 1 minute.
Add the bell pepper and cook for 1 more minute.
Sprinkle in the curry powder and stir for 10 seconds.
Add the rice and toss for 3 minutes until hot.
Add the soy sauce and sugar and toss to coat.
Fold in the pineapple, eggs, cashews and green onions and cook for another minute. Serve hot.

title: Lap Cheong Fried Rice
summary: Sweet, savory Chinese sausage gives this fried rice deep flavor. Rendered sausage fat does most of the seasoning for you.

ingredients.name: chinese sausage
ingredients.prep: links, sliced thin on a bias

steps: Break up the cold rice with your fingers.
Cook the sliced sausage in a dry wok over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes until the fat renders and the edges caramelize. Remove the sausage.
Add the oil to the sausage fat and scramble the eggs until just set. Remove them as well.
Add the garlic and half the green onions and stir for 15 seconds.
Add the rice and peas and toss over high heat for 3 to 4 minutes until hot.
Add the soy sauce and white pepper and toss.
Return the sausage and eggs, drizzle with sesame oil and top with the remaining green onions.

title: Claypot Chicken Rice
summary: Rice cooked with marinated chicken, mushrooms and Chinese sausage until it forms a crisp golden crust on the bottom. A one-pot comfort meal.

ingredients.name: chicken thighs
ingredients.prep: boneless skinless, cut into bite-size pieces

steps: Mix the chicken with 1 tbsp soy sauce, the oyster sauce, rice wine, sugar, cornstarch, ginger and sesame oil. Marinate for 20 minutes.
Combine the remaining soy sauce and the dark soy sauce in a small bowl for drizzling.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a heavy pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the rinsed rice and stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the chicken broth, bring to a boil, then cover and cook on low for 10 minutes.
Quickly arrange the chicken, sausage and mushrooms on top of the rice. Cover and cook on low for 15 minutes more.
Drizzle the remaining oil around the edge of the pot, turn the heat to medium for 3 minutes to form a crust, then turn off the heat and rest for 5 minutes.
Drizzle with the soy sauce mixture, sprinkle with green onions, stir and serve, scraping up the crispy bits.

title: Century Egg and Pork Congee
summary: A silky rice porridge with tender pork and rich century egg. Comforting, mild and perfect for breakfast or a sick day.
steps: Combine the rinsed rice with the chicken broth in a large pot and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low, partly cover, and simmer for 60 to 75 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes, until the rice breaks down into a thick porridge.
Meanwhile, mix the pork with the soy sauce, cornstarch and a pinch of white pepper.
Stir half the ginger into the congee, then drop in small pieces of pork, stirring so they separate.
Simmer for 10 minutes until the pork is cooked through.
Stir in the century eggs, salt and the rest of the white pepper.
Ladle into bowls and top with sesame oil, green onions, cilantro and the remaining ginger.

title: Fish Congee
summary: A smooth rice porridge topped with delicate slices of marinated white fish, ginger and green onion. Light and very soothing.
steps: Boil the rinsed rice with the broth, then reduce the heat to low, partly cover and simmer 60 to 75 minutes, stirring occasionally, until creamy.
Mix the fish slices gently with the rice wine, cornstarch, soy sauce and half the ginger. Rest for 15 minutes.
Season the congee with the salt and white pepper.
Divide the raw fish slices among four warm bowls.
Ladle the boiling congee over the fish. The heat cooks it in about a minute.
Top with sesame oil, green onions, cilantro, the remaining ginger and peanuts if you like.
Serve immediately.

title: Wonton Noodle Soup
summary: Delicate pork and shrimp wontons and springy noodles in a clear, savory broth. Fold the wontons ahead and freeze extras.
steps: Mix the pork, shrimp, 1 tsp soy sauce, rice wine, sesame oil, ginger and white pepper. Stir in one direction until the filling is sticky.
Put a teaspoon of filling in the center of each wrapper. Wet the edges, fold into a triangle, press out the air and seal.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Cook the noodles until just tender, drain and divide among four bowls.
In the same water, boil the bok choy for 1 minute, then lift it out into the bowls.
Boil the wontons in the same water for 3 to 4 minutes until they float and the filling is cooked through.
Meanwhile, heat the chicken broth with the remaining soy sauce and season to taste.
Add the wontons to the bowls, ladle the hot broth over the top and sprinkle with green onions.

title: Beef Noodle Soup
summary: Fall-apart braised beef shank in a star anise and soy broth with chewy noodles. Make it on a weekend for the deepest flavor.
steps: Cover the beef with cold water in a pot, bring to a boil for 3 minutes, then drain and rinse off the scum.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the ginger, garlic and green onions for 1 minute.
Stir in the doubanjiang and tomato paste and cook until the oil turns red, about 2 minutes.
Add the beef, soy sauce, rice wine, star anise, sugar and beef broth.
Bring to a simmer, cover and cook gently for 2 1/2 hours, until the beef is very tender.
Remove the beef and slice or break into chunks. Strain the broth and skim off the fat.
Boil the noodles in a separate pot until tender, adding the bok choy for the last minute.
Divide the noodles and bok choy among bowls, add beef and ladle hot broth over the top. Finish with cilantro.

title: Lanzhou Hand-Pulled Beef Noodle Soup
summary: A clear, aromatic beef broth with daikon, chili oil and fresh hand-pulled noodles. The dough is easier to stretch than you would think.

ingredients.name: daikon radish
ingredients.prep: small, peeled and cut into chunks

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.prep: 2 tsp for the broth, 1/2 tsp for the dough

steps: Boil the beef shank in water for 3 minutes, then drain and rinse. Return it to a clean pot with 12 cups of water.
Add the ginger, star anise, Sichuan peppercorns, bay leaves and 2 tsp salt and simmer gently for 2 hours, adding the daikon for the last 30 minutes.
For the dough, stir the flour, baking soda and 1/2 tsp salt with about 3/4 cup warm water until a dough forms. Knead for 10 minutes, coat with oil, cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Remove the beef and daikon from the broth, slice the beef, and strain the broth. Keep it hot.
Roll the dough into a thick rope. Stretch and fold it a few times, then pull the ends apart to make a long noodle and repeat to make thinner strands.
Drop the noodles into boiling water for 1 to 2 minutes, then drain.
Divide the noodles among four bowls, then add beef and daikon.
Ladle hot broth over the top and finish with chili oil, green onions and cilantro.

title: Tomato Egg Noodle Soup
summary: A cozy weeknight soup of ripe tomatoes, silky ribbons of egg and tender noodles. It uses pantry basics and takes 25 minutes.
steps: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a pot over medium heat. Pour in the eggs and scramble gently until just set. Remove to a plate.
Add the remaining oil, then the garlic and tomato paste, and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, pressing them down, until they collapse into a saucy mixture.
Pour in the chicken broth, soy sauce, sugar and salt. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, boil the noodles in a separate pot until tender and drain.
Divide the noodles among bowls.
Stir the eggs into the soup, ladle it over the noodles and finish with green onions and sesame oil.

title: Pork Rib and Corn Soup
summary: A gently simmered Cantonese soup of pork ribs, sweet corn and carrots. Clear, mellow and comforting.
steps: Cover the ribs with cold water in a pot, bring to a boil for 5 minutes, then drain and rinse well.
Return the ribs to a clean pot with 10 cups of water and the ginger.
Bring to a boil, skim off any foam, then reduce the heat to low, cover and simmer for 1 hour.
Add the corn and carrots and simmer for another 30 to 45 minutes until the ribs are very tender.
Season with the salt and white pepper.
Ladle into bowls with a piece of corn and a few ribs each and top with green onions.

title: Winter Melon Soup
summary: A light, clear soup of tender winter melon and pork ribs. The melon turns translucent and sips like a broth.

ingredients.name: winter melon
ingredients.prep: peeled, seeded and cut into 1 inch chunks

steps: Cover the ribs with cold water, bring to a boil for 5 minutes, then drain and rinse.
Put the ribs, ginger and 8 cups of water in a clean pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer, cover and cook for 40 minutes.
Add the winter melon and mushrooms and simmer for 20 to 25 minutes until the melon is translucent and tender.
Season with the salt and white pepper.
Ladle into bowls and top with green onions and a few drops of sesame oil.

title: West Lake Beef Soup
summary: A silky, lightly thickened soup of finely minced beef, egg white and cilantro from Hangzhou. It looks elegant and takes about 25 minutes.
steps: Mix the beef with the rice wine and ginger and let it sit for 5 minutes.
Bring the chicken broth to a gentle boil in a pot.
Add the beef, stirring to break it into very small pieces, and simmer for 3 minutes.
Stir in the soy sauce, salt and white pepper.
Stir the cornstarch slurry and pour it in slowly, stirring, until the soup turns glossy and slightly thick.
Reduce the heat to low. Slowly drizzle in the egg whites while stirring gently so they form soft ribbons.
Stir in the cilantro, drizzle with sesame oil and serve hot.

title: Seaweed and Egg Drop Soup
summary: Dried seaweed and silky egg ribbons in a light, peppery broth. It takes about 10 minutes, so it is great with any meal.

ingredients.name: seaweed
ingredients.prep: dried laver, torn into small pieces

steps: Bring the chicken broth to a boil in a pot.
Add the seaweed, soy sauce, salt and white pepper and simmer for 2 minutes.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry and simmer until the soup is lightly thickened.
Turn the heat to low and slowly pour in the beaten eggs in a thin stream while stirring gently in one direction.
Let the eggs set for 10 seconds, then turn off the heat.
Stir in the sesame oil and green onions and serve.

title: Corn Egg Drop Soup
summary: A silky, gently sweet soup with ribbons of egg and tender corn. It comes together in about 15 minutes.
steps: Whisk the cornstarch and water together in a small bowl until smooth.
Bring the broth, ginger and soy sauce to a simmer in a medium pot over medium heat.
Stir in the cream style corn and simmer for 3 minutes.
Stir the cornstarch mixture again, then pour it into the soup while stirring. Simmer for 1 to 2 minutes until the soup thickens slightly.
Turn the heat to low. Slowly pour the beaten eggs into the soup in a thin stream while stirring gently in one direction, so the egg forms ribbons.
Turn off the heat. Stir in the white pepper and sesame oil and season with salt.
Ladle into bowls and top with the green onions.

title: Hot Pot at Home
summary: A fun table-top meal where everyone cooks thin slices of meat, vegetables and tofu in a bubbling broth. Set out a dipping sauce bar and let people build their own bowls.

ingredients.name: beef ribeye
ingredients.prep: frozen for 30 minutes, then sliced paper thin

steps: Soak the dried shiitake mushrooms in 1 cup of hot water for 20 minutes, then slice them and keep the soaking liquid.
Arrange the beef, shrimp, tofu, cabbage, enoki, spinach and noodles on platters.
Make the dipping sauce: whisk the sesame paste with a few tablespoons of warm water until smooth, then stir in the soy sauce, vinegar, garlic, chili oil and cilantro. Divide among small bowls.
Pour the broth into a wide pot or electric hot pot. Add the ginger, green onions, sliced shiitakes, their strained soaking liquid and the 2 tablespoons soy sauce.
Bring to a boil, then reduce to a steady simmer and set the pot on a burner at the table.
Cook the meat for 10 to 20 seconds, shrimp for 2 to 3 minutes, and vegetables and tofu for 2 to 4 minutes, dipping each into the broth with chopsticks or a small strainer.
Eat as you go, dipping everything in the sauce. Add the noodles near the end so they pick up the rich broth.
Add more broth or hot water as the pot reduces.

title: Chinese Steamed Egg Custard
summary: A soft, wobbly savory custard that is silky all the way through. It is a classic comfort dish that takes minutes of hands-on time.
steps: Beat the eggs gently in a bowl with the salt, trying not to create foam.
Slowly whisk in the warm water until the mixture is even. It should be about twice the volume of the eggs.
Pour the mixture through a fine mesh strainer into a shallow heatproof bowl or plate with a rim.
Skim off or pop any bubbles on the surface with a spoon.
Cover the bowl tightly with foil or a plate.
Bring about an inch of water to a simmer in a wok or wide pot with a steaming rack. Lower the bowl onto the rack.
Reduce the heat to low and steam for 10 to 12 minutes, until the custard is just set but still jiggles.
Drizzle with the soy sauce and sesame oil, sprinkle with green onion, and serve right away.

title: Tea Eggs
summary: Hard boiled eggs gently cracked and simmered in a spiced tea and soy bath, giving them a marbled look and deep savory flavor. Great as a snack or part of a meal.
steps: Place the eggs in a pot, cover with cold water and bring to a boil. Turn off the heat, cover and let sit for 10 minutes.
Move the eggs to an ice bath for 5 minutes, then drain.
Gently tap each egg all over with the back of a spoon so the shell is covered in fine cracks, but leave the shell on.
Return the eggs to the pot. Add the 3 cups water, tea bags, soy sauce, dark soy sauce, star anise, cinnamon, sugar, salt and peppercorns.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover and simmer for 1 hour.
Turn off the heat and let the eggs steep in the liquid for at least 1 hour, or refrigerate overnight for a deeper color.
Peel the eggs to reveal the marbled pattern and serve cold or warm.

title: Shrimp and Egg Stir-Fry
summary: Tender shrimp and soft, fluffy scrambled eggs cooked together in a hot pan. A fast weeknight dinner that is great over rice.
steps: Toss the shrimp with the cornstarch, shaoxing wine and a pinch of the salt. Let sit for 10 minutes.
Beat the eggs with the remaining salt and the white pepper.
Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a wok or large skillet over medium-high heat. Pour in the eggs and cook, gently pushing them toward the center, until just set but still soft. Move to a plate.
Add the remaining oil to the wok. Add the garlic and scallion whites and stir for 15 seconds.
Add the shrimp in a single layer and cook for about 1 minute per side until pink and curled.
Return the eggs to the wok, breaking them into large pieces.
Add the soy sauce and scallion greens, toss for 30 seconds, and serve with rice.

title: Chinese Chive and Egg Stir-Fry
summary: Fresh, garlicky Chinese chives folded into soft scrambled eggs. A simple everyday dish that is quick and full of flavor.
steps: Wash the chives and dry them very well so they do not splatter in the oil.
Beat the eggs with half of the salt, the shaoxing wine and the white pepper.
Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a wok over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Pour in the eggs. Let them set for a few seconds, then push and fold them gently until about 80 percent cooked. Transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining oil to the wok, then add the chives and the remaining salt. Stir-fry for about 45 seconds until bright green and just wilted.
Return the eggs to the wok and toss everything together for 20 seconds.
Drizzle with sesame oil and serve hot with rice.

title: Mongolian Beef
summary: Crisp-edged slices of beef in a sweet, savory soy and garlic sauce with plenty of green onion. It is faster and better than takeout.

ingredients.name: flank steak
ingredients.prep: sliced against the grain into thin strips

steps: Toss the sliced beef with the cornstarch until evenly coated, shaking off the excess.
Whisk the soy sauce, water and brown sugar together in a bowl until the sugar dissolves.
Heat the oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Fry the beef in two batches for 1 to 2 minutes per batch, until browned and crisp at the edges. Remove to a plate lined with paper towels.
Pour off all but 1 tablespoon of oil from the pan.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir for 20 seconds, then pour in the sauce and simmer for 2 to 3 minutes until slightly thickened.
Return the beef to the pan with the green onions and toss for 1 minute.
Stir in the sesame oil and serve over rice.

photo.author: Craig Dugas from Bozeman, Montana, USA

title: Pepper Steak
summary: Tender strips of beef with bell peppers and onion in a savory soy and ginger sauce. A classic stir-fry that is ready in half an hour.

ingredients.name: flank steak
ingredients.prep: sliced against the grain into thin strips

steps: Toss the beef with 1 tablespoon of the soy sauce, 1 tablespoon cornstarch and the shaoxing wine. Let sit for 15 minutes.
Mix the remaining soy sauce with the oyster sauce, broth and sugar.
Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a wok over high heat. Sear the beef in a single layer for 1 to 2 minutes until browned, then remove to a plate.
Add the remaining oil. Stir-fry the onion and peppers for 2 to 3 minutes until crisp-tender.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir for 20 seconds.
Pour in the sauce and bring to a simmer. Stir in the cornstarch slurry and cook until glossy and slightly thick.
Return the beef to the wok and toss for 1 minute to heat through.
Serve over steamed rice.

title: Beef with Black Bean Sauce
summary: Tender beef and peppers in a salty, savory sauce built on fermented black beans and garlic. Rich and bold, and great with plain rice.

ingredients.name: flank steak
ingredients.prep: sliced against the grain into thin strips

steps: Toss the beef with the soy sauce, 1 tablespoon cornstarch and the shaoxing wine. Let sit for 15 minutes.
Mix the broth, oyster sauce and sugar in a small bowl.
Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a wok over high heat. Sear the beef in a single layer for about 1 minute, then remove to a plate.
Add the remaining oil. Stir-fry the onion and pepper for 2 minutes.
Add the black beans, garlic and ginger and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in the sauce and bring to a simmer.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry and cook for 30 seconds until thickened.
Return the beef to the wok, toss for 1 minute, and serve with rice.

title: Cumin Lamb
summary: A bold northwestern Chinese stir-fry with lamb, toasted cumin, chili and plenty of aromatics. Smoky, spicy and very fast to cook.
steps: Toss the lamb with the soy sauce, shaoxing wine and cornstarch. Let marinate for 15 minutes.
Toast the cumin seeds and peppercorns in a dry skillet over medium heat for 1 to 2 minutes until fragrant. Coarsely grind them in a spice grinder or mortar.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat until smoking.
Add the lamb in a single layer and sear for 1 to 2 minutes without moving, then stir-fry until mostly cooked through.
Add the onion, garlic and ginger and stir-fry for 1 to 2 minutes.
Add the ground cumin and pepper mixture, the red pepper flakes and the salt and toss for 1 minute.
Toss in the green onions and cilantro, cook for 20 seconds more, and serve with rice or flatbread.

title: Black Pepper Beef
summary: Tender beef with onions and peppers in a glossy sauce with a hearty hit of coarse black pepper. A restaurant favorite you can make at home in under 30 minutes.

ingredients.name: flank steak
ingredients.prep: sliced against the grain into thin strips

steps: Toss the beef with 1 tablespoon soy sauce, the cornstarch and the shaoxing wine. Let sit for 15 minutes.
Stir the oyster sauce, 1 tablespoon soy sauce, brown sugar and broth together.
Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a wok over high heat. Sear the beef in a single layer for about 1 minute, then remove to a plate.
Add the remaining oil and stir-fry the onion and bell pepper for 2 minutes.
Add the garlic and black pepper and stir for 20 seconds.
Pour in the sauce and simmer for 1 minute.
Return the beef to the wok and toss until coated and heated through, about 1 minute. Serve over rice.

title: Orange Beef
summary: Crisp fried beef coated in a sticky, citrusy sauce with orange zest and a little heat. A take on the takeout classic that is easy to make at home.

ingredients.name: flank steak
ingredients.prep: sliced against the grain into thin strips

steps: Toss the beef with the beaten egg, then add the 1/2 cup cornstarch and toss until each piece is coated.
Whisk the orange juice, zest, soy sauce, sugar and vinegar in a bowl.
Heat the frying oil in a wok or heavy pot to 350 degrees F.
Fry the beef in 2 or 3 batches for 2 to 3 minutes until golden and crisp. Drain on a wire rack.
Pour off all but 1 tablespoon of oil from the wok. Add the garlic, ginger and red pepper flakes and stir for 20 seconds.
Pour in the orange sauce and simmer for 2 minutes.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry and cook until thick and glossy.
Add the beef and toss to coat. Top with green onions and serve with rice.

photo.author: Mack Male from Edmonton, AB, Canada

title: Sichuan Boiled Beef
summary: Silky beef and crisp greens in a fiery, numbing broth, finished with a sizzle of hot oil over chilies and peppercorns. Bold and unforgettable.

ingredients.name: flank steak
ingredients.prep: sliced against the grain into thin slices

steps: Toss the beef with the cornstarch, shaoxing wine and half of the salt. Let sit for 15 minutes.
Heat the 2 tablespoons oil in a large pot over medium heat. Fry the doubanjiang for 1 minute until the oil turns red, then add the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds.
Add the broth and bring to a boil.
Add the cabbage and bean sprouts, cook for 2 minutes, then move them with a slotted spoon to a large serving bowl.
Reduce the heat to a gentle simmer and add the beef, stirring to separate the slices. Cook for 1 to 2 minutes until just done.
Pour the beef and broth over the vegetables in the bowl. Season with the remaining salt.
Scatter the chilies, peppercorns and green onions over the top.
Heat the 1/4 cup oil until it just begins to smoke and carefully pour it over the chilies so they sizzle. Serve right away with rice.

title: Sichuan Boiled Fish
summary: Tender white fish poached in a spicy, numbing broth with cabbage and bean sprouts and topped with sizzling chili oil. A showstopper for spice lovers.

ingredients.name: white fish fillets
ingredients.prep: such as tilapia or cod, sliced into thin pieces

steps: Toss the fish with the egg white, cornstarch, shaoxing wine and half of the salt. Refrigerate for 15 minutes.
Heat the 2 tablespoons oil in a large pot over medium heat. Fry the doubanjiang for 1 minute until the oil turns red, then add the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds.
Pour in the broth and bring to a boil.
Add the cabbage and bean sprouts and cook for 2 minutes. Transfer them with a slotted spoon to a large serving bowl.
Reduce to a gentle simmer. Slide in the fish slices one at a time and cook for 1 to 2 minutes until opaque. Do not stir hard.
Carefully pour the fish and broth over the vegetables and season with the remaining salt.
Top with the chilies, peppercorns and green onions.
Heat the 1/4 cup oil until it just starts to smoke, pour it over the chilies so it sizzles, and serve right away with rice.

title: Spicy Fragrant Pot
summary: Mala xiang guo is a stir-fried pot of meat, vegetables and tofu in a spicy, numbing sauce that coats every bite. Customize it with whatever you have.
steps: Toss the chicken with the soy sauce and cornstarch and set aside.
Blanch the lotus root and broccoli in boiling water for 1 minute, then drain well.
Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a wok and fry the tofu cubes until golden on a few sides. Remove to a plate.
Add 2 more tablespoons oil and sear the chicken until cooked through, then add the shrimp and cook until pink. Remove to the plate.
Add the remaining oil to the wok on medium heat. Fry the doubanjiang, chilies and peppercorns for 1 minute until fragrant and the oil turns red.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the mushrooms and bell pepper and stir-fry for 2 minutes, then add the lotus root and broccoli.
Pour in the broth and sugar and bring to a boil. Return the chicken, shrimp and tofu to the wok.
Toss everything over high heat for 2 to 3 minutes until the sauce clings. Top with sesame seeds and cilantro and serve with rice.

title: Laziji Chongqing Chili Chicken
summary: Crisp fried chicken nuggets buried in a heap of dried chilies and numbing Sichuan peppercorns. The fun is hunting for the chicken among the peppers.

ingredients.name: chicken thighs
ingredients.prep: boneless and skinless, cut into 3/4 inch pieces

ingredients.name: dried red chilies
ingredients.prep: cut in half and seeds shaken out

steps: Mix the chicken with the soy sauce, shaoxing wine, ginger and green onions. Marinate for 30 minutes.
Toss the chicken with the cornstarch until each piece is coated.
Heat the frying oil in a wok or heavy pot to 350 degrees F.
Fry the chicken in batches for 3 to 4 minutes until golden and crisp. Drain on a rack.

Carefully drain all but 2 tablespoons of oil from the wok. Over medium-low heat, add the chilies and peppercorns and stir for 30 to 45 seconds until fragrant and dark red, taking care not to burn them.
Add the garlic and stir for 15 seconds.
Return the chicken to the wok and add the sugar and salt. Toss over high heat for 1 minute.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve hot.

title: Saliva Chicken
summary: Cold poached chicken in a tangy, nutty, spicy chili oil sauce. It is named for how mouth-watering it is. Poach ahead and finish in minutes.
steps: Place the chicken, ginger, green onion halves and shaoxing wine in a pot and cover with cold water.
Bring just to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover and cook for 12 to 15 minutes until the chicken reaches 165 degrees F inside.
Move the chicken to a bowl of ice water for 10 minutes to cool and keep it juicy.
Whisk the soy sauce, black vinegar, sugar, chili oil, tahini, garlic and ground peppercorns in a bowl.
Drain the chicken and slice it or shred it into pieces.
Arrange on a plate and spoon the sauce over the top.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds, peanuts and cilantro. Serve cold or at room temperature.

title: Sichuan Wontons in Chili Oil
summary: Juicy pork wontons in a sweet, savory, tangy and spicy sauce. Make a batch and freeze extras for later.
steps: Mix the pork with 1 tablespoon soy sauce, the shaoxing wine, ginger, chopped green onions, sesame oil, salt and pepper. Stir in the water a little at a time until the filling feels light and sticky.
Place a heaping teaspoon of filling in the center of each wonton wrapper. Wet the edges with water, fold into a triangle and press to seal, then pull the two corners together.
In a serving bowl, mix 3 tablespoons soy sauce, the black vinegar, sugar, chili oil, garlic and ground peppercorns.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil.
Cook the wontons in batches for 4 to 5 minutes, until they float and the filling is cooked through.
Lift the wontons out with a slotted spoon and drain well.
Spoon the wontons into the sauce, toss gently and top with cilantro. Serve right away.

title: Chili Oil
summary: A fragrant, crunchy chili oil with warm spices that goes with noodles, dumplings, eggs and everything in between. Keep a jar in the fridge.
steps: Combine the pepper flakes, sesame seeds, salt, sugar and soy sauce in a heatproof bowl, preferably metal or ceramic.
Heat the oil in a small saucepan over medium-low heat. Add the peppercorns, star anise, cinnamon, ginger, green onions and garlic.
Cook gently for 10 to 15 minutes, until the aromatics turn golden brown. Do not let them burn.
The oil should be about 250 to 275 degrees F. Strain the oil to remove the aromatics.
Pour about a third of the hot oil over the chili flakes and stir. It should sizzle.
Let it sit for 1 minute, then add the remaining oil and stir.
Cool completely, then transfer to a clean jar. Store in the refrigerator for up to 1 month.

title: Gong Bao Shrimp
summary: Shrimp stir-fried with peanuts, dried chilies and a sweet, tangy sauce. Quick enough for a weeknight and full of Sichuan flavor.
steps: Toss the shrimp with 1 tablespoon cornstarch, the shaoxing wine and the salt. Let sit for 10 minutes.
Whisk the soy sauce, black vinegar, sugar and cornstarch mixture together in a small bowl.
Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a wok over high heat. Cook the shrimp for about 1 minute per side until just pink. Remove to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium and add the remaining oil, chilies and peppercorns. Stir for 20 to 30 seconds until fragrant, being careful not to burn them.
Add the garlic, ginger and green onions and stir for 20 seconds.
Pour in the sauce and cook for 30 seconds until it thickens.
Return the shrimp and add the peanuts. Toss for 1 minute to coat and serve with rice.

title: Moo Shu Pork
summary: Shredded pork, cabbage, mushrooms and scrambled egg in a savory sauce, wrapped in thin pancakes with hoisin. It is hearty, colorful and fun to assemble.
steps: Toss the pork with 1 tablespoon soy sauce, the cornstarch and shaoxing wine. Let sit for 15 minutes.
Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a wok over medium-high heat. Scramble the eggs until just set, then remove to a plate and break into pieces.
Add 1 tablespoon oil. Stir-fry the pork for 2 to 3 minutes until cooked through, then remove to the plate.
Add the remaining oil, garlic and ginger and stir for 15 seconds.
Add the mushrooms, cabbage and carrot and stir-fry for 3 to 4 minutes until the cabbage wilts.
Return the pork and eggs to the wok. Add 2 tablespoons soy sauce, the sesame oil and green onions and toss for 1 minute.
Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet or microwave.
Spread each with hoisin, add some filling, fold in the bottom and roll up to eat.

title: Hoisin Chicken Lettuce Wraps
summary: Savory ground chicken with water chestnuts and mushrooms in a sweet-salty hoisin sauce, spooned into crisp lettuce cups. Light, crunchy and fast.
steps: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the ground chicken and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, breaking it up, until browned and cooked through.
Add the mushrooms and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until they release their liquid and it cooks off.
Stir in the garlic and ginger and cook for 30 seconds.
Stir in the water chestnuts, hoisin sauce, soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil and red pepper flakes. Cook for 2 minutes.
Stir in the green onions.
Spoon the filling into lettuce leaves, top with shredded carrot, and serve right away.
