title: Chinese Chicken Salad
summary: Crunchy cabbage, shredded chicken, mandarin oranges and crispy noodles with a tangy sesame ginger dressing. It is a refreshing, filling meal.
steps: Whisk the vegetable oil, rice vinegar, soy sauce, honey, sesame oil and ginger together in a small bowl or jar.
Add the napa cabbage, red cabbage, carrots, green onions and cilantro to a large bowl.
Add the shredded chicken and mandarin oranges.
Pour about two thirds of the dressing over the salad and toss well.
Top with the chow mein noodles, almonds and sesame seeds just before serving so they stay crunchy.
Serve with the remaining dressing on the side.

title: Chicken with Mushrooms Stir-Fry
summary: Tender chicken and golden mushrooms in a light garlicky brown sauce. A simple everyday stir-fry that is on the table in 25 minutes.
steps: Toss the chicken with 1 tablespoon soy sauce, 1 tablespoon cornstarch and the shaoxing wine. Let sit for 10 minutes.
Mix the broth, oyster sauce and 1 tablespoon soy sauce in a small bowl.
Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a wok over high heat. Stir-fry the chicken for 3 to 4 minutes until cooked through and remove to a plate.
Add the remaining oil and the mushrooms. Cook for 4 to 5 minutes until browned.
Add the garlic, ginger and green onions and stir for 30 seconds.
Pour in the sauce, bring to a simmer, and stir in the cornstarch mixture. Cook until thickened.
Return the chicken to the wok and toss for 1 minute. Finish with sesame oil and serve with rice.

title: Chicken and Broccoli
summary: Tender chicken and crisp-tender broccoli in a glossy garlic and ginger sauce. A takeout favorite that is easy to make at home.
steps: Toss the chicken with 1 tablespoon soy sauce, 1 tablespoon cornstarch and the shaoxing wine. Let sit for 10 minutes.
Mix the broth, oyster sauce, 1 tablespoon soy sauce, sugar and sesame oil in a bowl.
Blanch the broccoli in boiling water for 1 minute until bright green, then drain.
Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a wok over high heat. Stir-fry the chicken for 3 to 4 minutes until cooked through and remove to a plate.
Add the remaining oil, garlic and ginger and stir for 20 seconds.
Add the broccoli and sauce and bring to a simmer.
Stir in the cornstarch mixture and cook until glossy and thick.
Return the chicken to the wok, toss for 1 minute and serve over rice.

title: Chicken with Snow Peas
summary: Tender chicken and sweet, crisp snow peas in a light garlic ginger sauce. Fresh, quick and easy to like.
steps: Toss the chicken with the soy sauce, 1 tablespoon cornstarch and the shaoxing wine. Let sit for 10 minutes.
Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a wok over high heat. Stir-fry the chicken for 3 to 4 minutes until cooked through and remove to a plate.
Add the remaining oil, then the carrot. Stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir for 20 seconds.
Add the snow peas and salt and stir-fry for 1 to 2 minutes until bright green and crisp-tender.
Pour in the broth and oyster sauce and bring to a simmer.
Stir in the cornstarch mixture and cook for 30 seconds until thickened.
Return the chicken, add the sesame oil and toss for 1 minute. Serve with rice.

title: Hunan Chicken
summary: Chicken with broccoli, peppers and mushrooms in a spicy, garlicky sauce with a little heat from chili paste. Bold and satisfying.

ingredients.name: chicken thighs
ingredients.prep: boneless and skinless, cut into bite-size pieces

steps: Toss the chicken with 1 tablespoon soy sauce, 1 tablespoon cornstarch and the shaoxing wine. Let sit for 10 minutes.
Mix the broth, 2 tablespoons soy sauce, rice vinegar and sugar in a bowl.
Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a wok over high heat. Cook the chicken for 4 to 5 minutes until browned and cooked through. Remove to a plate.
Add the remaining oil, broccoli, bell pepper and mushrooms and stir-fry for 3 minutes.
Add the garlic, ginger, dried chilies and chili garlic sauce and stir for 30 seconds.
Pour in the sauce and bring to a simmer.
Stir in the cornstarch mixture and cook until thick.
Return the chicken to the wok, toss for 1 minute, and serve with rice.

title: Hunan Steamed Fish with Chopped Chilies
summary: Fish steamed under a blanket of salty, tangy chopped chilies and garlic. This version uses fish fillets for easy shopping, and the sauce is the star.

ingredients.name: chopped pickled red chilies
ingredients.prep: or fresh red chilies mixed with 1 teaspoon salt

steps: Place the fish on a heatproof plate and rub with the shaoxing wine and half of the ginger.
Heat the 2 tablespoons oil in a small pan over medium heat. Cook the garlic, black beans and remaining ginger for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the chilies, soy sauce and sugar and cook for 1 more minute.
Spoon the chili mixture evenly over the fish.
Set up a steamer with simmering water and place the plate inside.
Cover and steam for 8 to 10 minutes, until the fish flakes easily.
Scatter the green onions and cilantro over the fish.
Heat the finishing oil until smoking, then pour it over the green onions so they sizzle. Serve with rice.

title: Hunan Pork with Peppers
summary: Smoky, spicy pork stir-fried with fresh green chili peppers and fermented black beans. A home-style Hunan favorite with a strong, punchy flavor.
steps: Toss the pork with 1 tablespoon soy sauce, the shaoxing wine and cornstarch. Marinate for 15 minutes.
Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a wok over high heat until nearly smoking.
Cook the pork in a single layer for 2 minutes, then stir-fry for 2 to 3 more minutes until browned and cooked through. Remove to a plate.
Add the remaining oil and the chili peppers and bell pepper. Stir-fry for 2 to 3 minutes until blistered.
Add the garlic, black beans and ginger and stir for 30 seconds.
Return the pork to the wok. Add 2 tablespoons soy sauce, the sugar, broth and white pepper.
Toss over high heat for 1 to 2 minutes until the sauce clings. Serve with rice.

title: Dongpo Pork
summary: Cubes of pork belly braised until silky and melting in a rich soy and rice wine sauce. It takes patience, but most of the time is hands-off.

ingredients.name: pork belly
ingredients.prep: skin on, cut into 2 inch cubes

steps: Place the pork belly in a pot, cover with cold water and bring to a boil. Boil for 5 minutes, then drain and rinse.
Line the bottom of a heavy pot or Dutch oven with half of the green onions and ginger.
Arrange the pork belly cubes skin side down on top.
Add the shaoxing wine, soy sauce, dark soy sauce, sugar, star anise, cinnamon and water.
Add the remaining green onions and ginger. Bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Cover tightly, reduce the heat to the lowest setting and braise for 2 1/2 hours, until the pork is very tender.
Steam or blanch the bok choy for 2 minutes until tender.
Uncover the pot, remove the aromatics and boil the sauce for 5 to 10 minutes until slightly thick.
Spoon the pork and sauce over the bok choy and serve with rice.

title: Lion's Head Meatballs
summary: Big, tender pork meatballs simmered with napa cabbage in a light, savory broth. Cozy and filling over rice.
steps: Mix the pork, water chestnuts, green onions, ginger, egg, cornstarch, rice wine, 1 tablespoon of the soy sauce, salt, white pepper and sesame oil. Stir in one direction for a couple of minutes until the mixture feels sticky.
Shape the mixture into 4 large meatballs, wetting your hands so they do not stick.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat. Brown the meatballs for about 2 minutes per side, just to set a crust. They do not need to cook through.
Lay half of the cabbage in a heavy pot or Dutch oven. Set the meatballs on top, then cover them with the rest of the cabbage.
Pour in the broth, the remaining 2 tablespoons soy sauce and the sugar. Bring to a gentle boil.
Reduce the heat to low, cover and simmer for 45 minutes, until the meatballs are cooked through and the cabbage is silky.
Taste the broth and adjust the salt. Serve the meatballs and cabbage in bowls with plenty of broth and steamed rice.

title: Pearl Meatballs
summary: Pork meatballs rolled in sticky rice and steamed until the grains turn translucent and pearly. A classic dim sum favorite.

ingredients.name: carrots
ingredients.prep: sliced into rounds, for the steamer

steps: Rinse the sticky rice until the water runs mostly clear, then soak in cold water for at least 2 hours or overnight. Drain well and spread on a plate.
Mix the pork, mushrooms, green onions, ginger, rice wine, soy sauce, sesame oil, cornstarch, salt and white pepper. Stir in one direction until sticky and well combined.
Shape the pork into about 20 balls the size of a walnut.
Roll each meatball in the drained rice so it is fully coated, pressing lightly to help the grains stick.
Line a steamer with parchment with holes poked in it, or with carrot rounds. Arrange the meatballs with a little space between them.
Steam over boiling water for 25 to 30 minutes, until the rice is tender and translucent and the pork is cooked through.
Serve hot with a dipping sauce of soy sauce and rice vinegar if you like.

title: Steamed Spare Ribs with Black Bean
summary: Bite-size pork ribs steamed in a garlicky black bean sauce until fall-off-the-bone tender. A dim sum staple you can make at home.

ingredients.name: spare ribs
ingredients.prep: cut into 1.5 inch pieces by the butcher

steps: Soak the ribs in cold water for 20 minutes, changing the water once, to draw out some blood. Drain and pat dry.
Rinse the black bean sauce lightly if it is very salty, then mash it with the garlic and ginger.
Toss the ribs with the black bean mixture, soy sauce, rice wine, sugar, cornstarch and sesame oil. Marinate for at least 20 minutes.
Spread the ribs in a single layer on a heatproof shallow plate with a rim.
Bring water to a boil in a wok or large pot fitted with a steaming rack. Set the plate on the rack.
Cover and steam over medium-high heat for 35 to 40 minutes, until the ribs are very tender. Top up the water if it runs low.
Scatter the chili and green onions on top and serve with steamed rice.

title: Sweet and Sour Spare Ribs
summary: Pork ribs simmered until tender, then glazed in a glossy, tangy sauce. Sweet, sour and very sticky.
steps: Put the ribs in a pot with cold water to cover, add the ginger and rice wine, and bring to a boil. Boil for 5 minutes, skim the foam, then drain and rinse the ribs.
Heat the oil in a wok or wide pot over medium-low heat. Add the sugar and stir until it melts and turns amber.
Add the ribs and toss quickly to coat in the caramel, about 2 minutes.
Add the soy sauce, dark soy sauce, vinegar, ketchup, water and green onions. Bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer over low heat for 35 to 40 minutes, until the ribs are tender.
Uncover, raise the heat to high and cook, stirring, until the sauce reduces to a thick glaze that coats the ribs.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve right away.

title: Chinese Barbecue Spare Ribs
summary: Oven-roasted ribs with a sticky, sweet and savory red-tinged glaze, like the ones from a Chinese barbecue shop.
steps: Stir together the hoisin, honey, soy sauce, rice wine, brown sugar, garlic, ginger, five spice powder, ketchup, white pepper and sesame oil.
Pat the ribs dry and put them in a large zip-top bag or dish. Pour in the marinade, turn to coat and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Heat the oven to 300 F. Line a rimmed baking sheet with foil and set a rack on top.
Lift the ribs out of the marinade, saving it, and place them meat side up on the rack. Pour a little water into the pan to keep drippings from burning.
Cover loosely with foil and roast for 1 hour 30 minutes.
Meanwhile, simmer the leftover marinade in a small pot for 5 minutes until slightly thickened.
Raise the oven to 425 F. Uncover the ribs, brush with the cooked marinade and roast for 15 minutes, brushing once more halfway through.
Brush with a little extra honey, rest for 10 minutes, then cut between the bones and serve.

title: Braised Chicken Wings in Coke
summary: Chicken wings simmered in cola, soy sauce and ginger until sticky and glossy. A popular, easy Chinese home dish.

ingredients.name: chicken wings
ingredients.prep: split at the joints, tips removed

steps: Put the wings in a pot of cold water with 1 slice of ginger. Bring to a boil, cook for 2 minutes, then drain and rinse. Pat dry.
Heat the oil in a wide pan or wok over medium heat. Brown the wings for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden.
Add the remaining ginger and the green onions and stir for 30 seconds.
Pour in the rice wine, soy sauce and dark soy sauce, then add the cola. The wings should be about two-thirds covered.
Bring to a boil, reduce to medium-low, cover and simmer for 15 minutes.
Uncover, raise the heat and cook, turning the wings often, until the sauce reduces to a sticky glaze.
Taste and add salt if needed. Serve hot with rice.

title: Soy Braised Chicken Wings
summary: Wings simmered in a mellow soy, ginger and star anise sauce until deeply savory and lacquered.
steps: Boil the wings in water for 2 minutes, then drain and pat very dry.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium-low heat. Add the sugar and stir until it melts into a light amber syrup.
Add the wings and turn them to coat in the caramel, then brown for about 4 minutes.
Add the ginger, green onions and star anise and stir for 30 seconds.
Pour in the rice wine, soy sauce, dark soy sauce, oyster sauce and water.
Bring to a boil, cover and simmer on low for 20 minutes, flipping once.
Uncover, raise the heat and cook until the sauce is thick and clings to the wings. Serve with steamed rice and greens.

title: Chinese Braised Beef Shank
summary: Beef shank simmered slowly in soy, star anise and rice wine, then sliced thin. Great hot or cold.
steps: Put the beef in a pot of cold water, bring to a boil and cook for 5 minutes. Drain, rinse off the foam and wipe the pot clean.
Heat the oil in the pot over medium heat. Cook the ginger, green onions and garlic for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the beef, rice wine, soy sauce, dark soy sauce, sugar, salt, star anise, cinnamon and water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover and simmer for 2 hours, turning the beef halfway through.
Uncover and simmer for another 20 to 30 minutes, until a skewer slides in easily and the sauce has thickened.
Let the beef rest in the sauce for 15 minutes, then slice against the grain.
Spoon the sauce over the slices and serve with rice, noodles or on its own.

title: Tomato Beef Brisket Stew
summary: Soft chunks of beef brisket and sweet-tart tomatoes in a rich, comforting stew. Wonderful over rice or noodles.
steps: Cover the brisket with cold water, bring to a boil and cook for 5 minutes. Drain and rinse the beef.
Heat the oil in a Dutch oven over medium heat. Cook the onion, ginger and garlic for 3 minutes until fragrant.
Add the tomato paste and half of the tomato wedges. Cook, mashing the tomatoes, for about 5 minutes until jammy.
Add the beef, rice wine, soy sauce, sugar, star anise and water. Bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce to low and simmer for 1 hour 30 minutes.
Add the carrots, the remaining tomatoes and the salt. Simmer uncovered for 30 minutes, until the beef is very tender and the broth is rich.
Taste for salt and sugar, then serve over rice, topped with green onions.

title: Braised Tofu with Pork
summary: Golden pan-fried tofu simmered with savory ground pork and mushrooms in a glossy sauce.
steps: Pat the tofu dry. Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a large nonstick pan over medium-high heat and fry the tofu for about 8 minutes, turning, until golden on most sides. Remove to a plate.
Add the remaining oil and the pork. Cook, breaking it up, until browned, about 4 minutes.
Add the garlic, ginger and green onion whites and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the mushrooms and cook for 3 minutes until they release their liquid.
Stir in the rice wine, soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar, white pepper and broth. Bring to a simmer.
Return the tofu to the pan, cover and simmer gently for 8 minutes.
Stir the cornstarch mixture and drizzle it in, stirring, until the sauce turns glossy and thick.
Scatter with the green onion greens and serve with rice.

title: Home-Style Tofu
summary: Pan-fried tofu with tender peppers and a savory, slightly sweet brown sauce. A weeknight classic.
steps: Pat the tofu dry with paper towels so it browns well.
Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Fry the tofu for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden. Move to a plate.
Add the remaining oil and cook the carrots for 2 minutes. Add the garlic and green onions and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the bell pepper and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Stir in the soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar and water, then return the tofu to the pan.
Simmer for 3 minutes, spooning the sauce over the tofu.
Stir in the cornstarch mixture until the sauce thickens, then finish with the sesame oil. Serve with rice.

title: Mapo Tofu with Mushrooms
summary: A numbing, spicy Sichuan-style tofu with mushrooms standing in for the usual ground meat. Bold and satisfying.
steps: Bring a pot of salted water to a gentle simmer and slip in the tofu. Let it sit for 5 minutes off the heat, then drain gently. This firms it up.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat. Cook the mushrooms for 5 to 6 minutes until browned and their liquid cooks off.
Push the mushrooms aside, add the doubanjiang and fry for 30 seconds until the oil turns red.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir for 30 seconds.
Pour in the broth, soy sauce and sugar and bring to a simmer.
Slide in the tofu and simmer for 5 minutes, nudging it gently so it does not break.
Drizzle in the cornstarch mixture in two parts, stirring slowly, until the sauce is glossy.
Top with half of the Sichuan pepper, the green onions and the chili oil, and serve over rice.

title: Stir-Fried Tofu Skin with Celery
summary: Chewy tofu skin strips and crisp celery tossed in a quick garlicky stir-fry. Light, fresh and high in protein.

ingredients.name: celery
ingredients.prep: stalks, thinly sliced on the diagonal

steps: Soak the dried tofu skin in warm water for 30 minutes, or until fully pliable. Drain and cut into 1 inch wide strips.
Bring a small pot of water to a boil and blanch the tofu skin for 1 minute. Drain and set aside.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat. Add the garlic and chili and stir for 15 seconds.
Add the carrot and celery and stir-fry for 2 minutes until just crisp-tender.
Add the tofu skin, soy sauce, sugar and salt. Toss for 2 minutes until hot and well coated.
Drizzle with sesame oil and serve right away.

title: Buddha's Delight
summary: A big vegetarian stir-fry of mushrooms, tofu and crisp vegetables in a light, savory sauce. A classic for Lunar New Year.
steps: Soak the dried mushrooms in hot water for 30 minutes. Squeeze dry, slice and save 1/2 cup of the soaking water.
Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a wok over high heat and fry the tofu until golden, about 4 minutes. Remove to a plate.
Add the remaining oil, then the garlic and ginger, and stir for 15 seconds.
Add the carrots and mushrooms and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add the cabbage, bamboo shoots and water chestnuts and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Pour in the broth, mushroom water, soy sauce, oyster sauce and sugar. Add the tofu and glass noodles if using, and simmer for 4 minutes.
Add the snow peas and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the cornstarch mixture until the sauce thickens, finish with sesame oil and serve.

title: Stir-Fried Mushrooms with Garlic
summary: Mushrooms seared hot and fast with plenty of garlic and a splash of soy. Simple and deeply savory.
steps: Heat a large wok or skillet over high heat until very hot. Add the mushrooms without oil and cook, stirring, for 4 to 5 minutes until they release their water and it evaporates.
Push the mushrooms aside, add the vegetable oil and let it heat for a few seconds.
Add the garlic and stir for 20 seconds until fragrant, then toss with the mushrooms.
Add the rice wine, soy sauce, oyster sauce and sugar and stir-fry for 1 to 2 minutes until the mushrooms are glossy.
Season with white pepper, add the green onions and sesame oil, toss once and serve.

title: Garlic Eggplant
summary: Silky eggplant coated in a bold garlic, soy and vinegar sauce. Tender, sweet and tangy.
steps: Toss the eggplant with the salt and let it sit in a colander for 15 minutes. Squeeze out the liquid and pat dry.
Stir the soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, oyster sauce, cornstarch and water together in a small bowl.
Heat the oil in a large nonstick pan or wok over medium-high heat. Fry the eggplant in two batches for about 5 minutes each until browned and soft. Set aside.
Lower the heat to medium, add the garlic, ginger and chili garlic sauce and stir for 30 seconds.
Return the eggplant to the pan and pour in the sauce.
Cook, stirring gently, for 2 to 3 minutes until the sauce thickens and coats the eggplant.
Top with green onions and serve with steamed rice.

title: Stir-Fried Snow Pea Shoots
summary: Tender pea shoots wilted with garlic in a minute or two. Sweet, grassy and fast.
steps: Rinse the pea shoots well and drain, shaking off most of the water. Trim off any tough stems.
Heat the oil in a large wok over high heat until it just starts to smoke.
Add the garlic and stir for 10 seconds until fragrant but not brown.
Add all of the pea shoots at once and toss quickly for 30 seconds.
Splash in the rice wine and sprinkle with the salt and sugar. Toss for another 30 to 60 seconds until bright green and just wilted.
Drizzle with sesame oil if using and serve immediately.

title: Stir-Fried Lotus Root
summary: Crunchy lotus root slices stir-fried with a touch of vinegar for a refreshing, lightly tangy side.
steps: Peel the lotus root and slice it into thin rounds, about 1/8 inch thick. Soak in a bowl of cold water with a splash of vinegar for 10 minutes to prevent browning and remove excess starch.
Drain well and blanch in boiling water for 1 minute for a crisp texture, then drain again.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat. Add the garlic and chili and stir for 15 seconds.
Add the carrot and lotus root and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add the 1 tablespoon vinegar, salt and sugar and toss for 1 more minute.
Stir in the green onions, drizzle with the sesame oil and serve.

title: Stir-Fried Bean Sprouts
summary: Crisp bean sprouts tossed over blazing heat with garlic and green onion. Ready in about 10 minutes.
steps: Rinse the bean sprouts and drain them very well so they stir-fry rather than steam.
Heat a wok over the highest heat until smoking, then add the oil.
Add the garlic, green onions and chili and stir for 10 seconds.
Add the bean sprouts and toss constantly for about 1 minute.
Add the vinegar, soy sauce, salt and sugar and keep tossing for 30 to 60 seconds. They should stay crunchy.
Drizzle with sesame oil, toss once and serve immediately.

title: Braised Napa Cabbage with Glass Noodles
summary: Sweet, soft napa cabbage and slippery glass noodles simmered in a savory broth with pork. Warm and homey.
steps: Soak the glass noodles in warm water for 15 minutes until pliable, then drain and cut into shorter lengths with kitchen scissors.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Brown the pork, breaking it up, for 3 minutes.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the cabbage stems first and stir-fry for 2 minutes, then add the leaves and cook until they begin to wilt.
Pour in the broth, soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar and white pepper. Bring to a boil.
Nestle the noodles into the liquid, cover and simmer for 8 to 10 minutes until the cabbage is soft and the noodles are translucent.
Stir gently, scatter on the green onions and serve hot.

title: Ants Climbing a Tree
summary: Spicy glass noodles with crumbly ground pork, a Sichuan favorite named for the bits of meat clinging to the noodles.
steps: Soak the glass noodles in warm water for 10 to 15 minutes until pliable, then drain.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat. Cook the pork, breaking it into small crumbs, until browned, about 3 minutes.
Add the doubanjiang and fry for 30 seconds until the oil turns red.
Stir in the garlic and ginger, then the rice wine and soy sauce.
Pour in the broth and sugar and bring to a boil.
Add the noodles and toss. Simmer for 4 to 5 minutes until they absorb nearly all of the sauce.
Stir in most of the green onions and the sesame oil, top with the remainder and serve.

title: Glass Noodle Salad
summary: A cool, tangy salad of glass noodles, crisp vegetables and a garlicky soy-vinegar dressing. Good for hot days and picnics.
steps: Cook the glass noodles in boiling water for 5 to 7 minutes, or as the package says, until soft and clear.
Drain and rinse under cold water until cool. Drain very well and cut into shorter lengths with scissors.
Whisk the soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, sugar, garlic and chili oil in a large bowl until the sugar dissolves.
Add the noodles, carrot, cucumber, green onions and cilantro.
Toss everything well, then taste and add more vinegar or soy sauce as needed.
Chill for 15 minutes if you have time, top with crushed peanuts and serve.

title: Spring Rolls
summary: Crispy fried rolls with a savory pork and cabbage filling. Serve hot with a sweet chili or vinegar dip.

ingredients.name: cornstarch
ingredients.prep: mixed with 2 tbsp water, for sealing

steps: Heat the 1 tablespoon oil in a wok over high heat. Cook the pork until browned, about 3 minutes.
Add the garlic and ginger, then the mushrooms, carrot and cabbage. Stir-fry for 3 to 4 minutes until the vegetables are wilted.
Stir in the soy sauce, oyster sauce, sesame oil and white pepper, then the green onions. Spread on a tray and cool completely, draining off any liquid.
Place a wrapper with a corner pointing toward you. Spoon about 3 tablespoons of filling near the bottom corner.
Fold the bottom corner over the filling, fold in both sides, then roll up tightly. Brush the last corner with the cornstarch paste to seal.
Heat 2 inches of oil in a pot to 350 F. Fry 4 rolls at a time for 3 to 4 minutes, turning, until deep golden.
Drain on a rack, rest for a minute and serve hot with dipping sauce.

title: Potstickers with Chicken and Cabbage
summary: Juicy chicken and cabbage dumplings pan-fried until crisp on the bottom and steamed until tender on top.
steps: Toss the cabbage with the salt and let it sit for 10 minutes. Squeeze out as much liquid as you can with a clean towel.
Mix the chicken, cabbage, green onions, ginger, soy sauce, rice wine, sesame oil, white pepper and sugar. Stir in one direction until sticky.
Place a rounded teaspoon of filling in the center of a wrapper. Wet the edge, fold in half and pinch the edges together with a few pleats. Repeat with the rest.
Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a large nonstick skillet with a lid over medium-high heat. Arrange half of the potstickers flat side down.
Cook for 2 minutes until the bottoms are golden, then pour in about 1/3 cup of water and cover right away.
Steam for 6 to 7 minutes until the water is gone and the wrappers look translucent.
Uncover and cook for 1 minute more to re-crisp the bottoms. Repeat with the rest and serve with soy sauce and vinegar.

title: Shrimp Toast
summary: Crisp fried bread topped with a seasoned shrimp paste and sesame seeds. A restaurant appetizer that is easy to fry at home.
steps: Pat the shrimp dry and chop it, then mash it with the flat of a knife until it forms a rough paste.
Mix the shrimp with the egg white, cornstarch, green onions, ginger, rice wine, salt, white pepper and sesame oil. Stir until sticky.
Cut each slice of bread into 4 triangles. Spread a layer of shrimp paste on each one, then press the top into the sesame seeds.
Heat the oil in a wide pan to 350 F.
Fry the toasts shrimp side down for 1 to 2 minutes until golden, then flip and fry for 1 minute more.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with sweet chili sauce.

title: Crab Rangoon
summary: Crispy wonton pockets filled with creamy crab and cream cheese. A takeout favorite that is simple to make.
steps: Mix the cream cheese, crab, green onions, garlic, soy sauce and Worcestershire sauce until smooth.
Put 1 heaping teaspoon of filling in the center of a wonton wrapper.
Brush the edges with beaten egg, bring the corners to the center and pinch the seams to seal into a pouch. Press out the air as you go.
Heat the oil in a pot to 350 F.
Fry 5 or 6 at a time for 2 to 3 minutes, turning, until golden and crisp.
Drain on a rack and let cool for a couple of minutes, since the filling is hot. Serve with sweet chili sauce.

title: Chinese Sausage Rice in a Rice Cooker
summary: Sweet, savory Chinese sausage cooked right on top of jasmine rice so its juices soak in. A one-button dinner.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.prep: plus more as your cooker needs

steps: Rinse the rice in several changes of water until the water runs mostly clear. Drain.
Put the rice in the rice cooker with the water. Stir in the soy sauce and the dark soy sauce.
Stir-fry the mushrooms and ginger in the vegetable oil for 2 minutes, then scatter them over the rice.
Arrange the sausage slices over the top. Do not stir.
Close the lid and start the cooker on its regular white rice setting.
When it finishes, let it rest for 10 minutes with the lid closed.
Drizzle with the sesame oil, fluff gently, scatter with green onions and serve.

title: Sticky Rice in Lotus Leaf
summary: Sticky rice with chicken, mushrooms and sausage steamed in a lotus leaf, which gives it a lovely herbal aroma. A dim sum classic.
steps: Soak the sticky rice in cold water for at least 4 hours or overnight. Soak the lotus leaves in hot water for 30 minutes until soft, then wipe and cut each into 2 pieces.
Toss the chicken with 1 tablespoon of the soy sauce, the rice wine, cornstarch and ginger and marinate for 20 minutes.
Heat the oil in a wok and brown the chicken for 3 minutes. Add the sausage and mushrooms and cook 2 minutes more. Stir in the oyster sauce, the sugar and the green onions, then cool.
Drain the rice and steam it in a heatproof dish over boiling water for 20 minutes until partly cooked.
Mix the warm rice with the remaining soy sauce, the dark soy sauce and the sesame oil.
Place a lotus leaf piece on a work surface. Spoon on a portion of rice, press a well, add some chicken filling and cover with more rice.
Fold the leaf over into a neat parcel and tie with kitchen string if needed. Repeat to make 4 parcels.
Steam over boiling water for 40 minutes. Rest for 5 minutes and let each person unwrap their own at the table.

title: Zongzi
summary: Pyramid-shaped sticky rice dumplings wrapped in bamboo leaves with savory pork belly and mushrooms. Time-consuming but fun to make with family.
steps: Soak the sticky rice in cold water for at least 4 hours or overnight. Soak the bamboo leaves in hot water for 1 hour, then scrub and rinse them.
Marinate the pork in 2 tablespoons of the soy sauce, the dark soy sauce, rice wine, sugar and star anise for at least 2 hours or overnight.
Drain the rice and mix it with the oil, the remaining soy sauce, the oyster sauce and the salt.
Overlap 2 leaves and fold into a cone. Add 2 tablespoons of rice, a piece of pork, a mushroom piece, a bit of sausage and some peanuts, then more rice to cover.
Fold the leaves over the top to enclose the filling in a pyramid and tie it tightly with kitchen string. Repeat with the remaining leaves and filling.
Pack the zongzi in a large pot and cover with water by an inch, weighting them down with a plate.
Bring to a boil, then simmer on low for 2 hours 30 minutes, adding hot water as needed to keep them covered.
Let them cool slightly, then unwrap and eat warm. Leftovers freeze well.

title: Chinese Turnip Cake
summary: A savory steamed cake of daikon radish, rice flour and Chinese sausage, sliced and pan-fried until crisp. A dim sum classic.
steps: Brush an 8 inch square or round pan with oil.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a wok and cook the sausage, mushrooms and dried shrimp for 2 minutes. Remove.
Add the daikon and 1/2 cup of water to the wok. Cook for 8 to 10 minutes until the radish is soft and translucent.
Whisk the rice flour, cornstarch, remaining water, sugar, salt, white pepper and sesame oil into a smooth batter.
Stir the batter into the daikon with the sausage mixture and green onions. Cook, stirring, for 1 to 2 minutes until it thickens.
Scrape into the pan, smooth the top, cover with foil and steam over boiling water for 55 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool completely, ideally refrigerating for 2 hours, then slice into rectangles.
Heat a little oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat and fry the slices for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden and crisp. Serve with chili sauce.

title: Egg Tarts
summary: Flaky, buttery shells filled with a silky, lightly sweet egg custard, like the ones from a Hong Kong bakery. Bake until the custard just sets for the smoothest texture.
steps: Rub the cold butter into the flour and powdered sugar with your fingertips until it looks like coarse crumbs.
Stir in the egg yolk and cold water until a dough forms. Press it into a disk, wrap, and chill for 30 minutes.
Stir the sugar into the hot water until dissolved, then let it cool to room temperature. Whisk in the milk and vanilla.
Lightly beat the eggs, then whisk them into the sugar mixture gently to avoid bubbles. Strain through a fine sieve for a smooth custard.
Heat the oven to 400 F. Divide the dough into 12 pieces and press each into a muffin cup, thinly and evenly up the sides.
Pour the custard into the shells, filling them about 3/4 full.
Bake for 10 minutes, then lower the oven to 325 F and bake 12 to 15 minutes more, until the custard is just set with a slight wobble.
Cool in the pan for 5 minutes, then lift the tarts out and serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Mango Pudding
summary: A cool, silky pudding made from ripe mango and cream, set with gelatin. Serve it cold with a little extra mango on top.

ingredients.name: mango
ingredients.prep: peeled and pitted, plus a little diced for topping

steps: Sprinkle the gelatin over the cold water and let it sit for 5 minutes to soften.
Blend the mango into a smooth puree. You should have about 1 1/2 cups.
Stir the sugar into the hot water until dissolved, then add the softened gelatin and stir until fully melted.
Whisk in the evaporated milk and cream, then the mango puree.
Pour through a sieve into a pitcher to remove any lumps.
Divide among six small cups or ramekins and chill for at least 4 hours, until set.
Top with diced mango just before serving.

title: Sesame Balls
summary: Chewy, crisp-shelled fried balls of glutinous rice dough coated in sesame seeds and filled with sweet red bean paste. They puff up in the oil and are best eaten warm.
steps: Whisk the sweet rice flour and sugar together, then stir in the hot water until the dough comes together. Knead until smooth and add a teaspoon of water at a time if it feels dry. It should be soft like play dough.
Roll the red bean paste into 16 small balls and the dough into 16 equal balls.
Flatten a dough ball in your palm, set a bean paste ball in the center, and pinch the dough closed. Roll it smooth.
Brush or dab each ball with a little water and roll it in the sesame seeds until coated.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to 275 F. Fry the balls in batches, keeping them moving gently, until they float.
Raise the heat to 350 F and keep pressing the balls lightly against the pot with a spoon so they puff up, about 5 minutes.
Fry until golden brown, then drain on a rack and serve warm.

title: Tangyuan
summary: Soft glutinous rice dumplings with a sweet black sesame filling, served in a light ginger syrup. A comforting dessert for celebrations.
steps: Toast the black sesame seeds in a dry pan over medium-low heat until fragrant, about 3 minutes. Cool, then grind to a rough powder.
Mix the ground sesame with the sugar and softened butter into a thick paste. Chill for 15 minutes, then roll into 16 small balls.
Mix the sweet rice flour with the warm water until a smooth, soft dough forms. Add a little water if it cracks.
Divide the dough into 16 pieces. Flatten each, wrap it around a filling ball, and roll it smooth.
Bring the syrup water, ginger, and brown sugar to a simmer for 5 minutes.
In a separate pot, boil water and cook the dumplings in batches until they float, then cook 2 minutes more.
Scoop the dumplings into bowls and ladle the ginger syrup over them.

title: Red Bean Soup
summary: A warm, lightly sweet soup of tender adzuki beans. Eat it hot in winter or chilled in summer.
steps: Soak the beans in plenty of water for at least 4 hours or overnight, then drain.
Put the beans and fresh water in a large pot and bring to a boil.
Reduce to a gentle simmer, cover partly, and cook for 1 to 1 1/2 hours, until the beans are very soft and starting to break down.
Stir in the sugar and salt and simmer 10 minutes more, until dissolved.
Mash a few beans against the side of the pot if you like a thicker soup.
Taste and add more sugar if needed, then serve warm or chilled.

title: Almond Jelly
summary: A delicate, milky jelly with a soft almond flavor, cut into cubes and served in light syrup with fruit. It is refreshing and takes just a few ingredients.
steps: Whisk the agar powder into the water in a saucepan and let it sit for 5 minutes.
Bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring, and simmer for 2 minutes until the agar is fully dissolved.
Stir in 1/4 cup of the sugar until dissolved, then add the milk and almond extract and warm through without boiling.
Pour into a shallow dish and cool for 20 minutes, then chill for at least 2 hours until firm.
For the syrup, simmer the remaining 1/4 cup sugar with 1 cup of water for 3 minutes, then chill.
Cut the jelly into small diamonds or cubes.
Spoon into bowls, add the fruit, and pour the cold syrup over the top.

title: Steamed Milk Pudding
summary: A smooth, barely sweet custard of milk and egg whites, gently steamed until it jiggles. It is simple, light, and very Cantonese.
steps: Warm the milk and sugar in a small pot over low heat, stirring just until the sugar dissolves. Do not let it boil. Cool for 5 minutes.
Gently whisk the egg whites in a bowl without making foam, then slowly stir in the warm milk and vanilla.
Strain the mixture twice through a fine sieve and skim off any bubbles.
Divide among three heatproof cups or bowls and cover each with foil or a plate.
Set up a steamer with simmering water and place the cups inside.
Steam over low to medium-low heat for 15 to 18 minutes, until the puddings are set but still wobble slightly.
Serve warm, or chill for 2 hours and serve cold.

title: Chinese Almond Cookies
summary: Crumbly, buttery cookies with a toasty almond flavor, each topped with a whole almond. They are a classic for Lunar New Year.

ingredients.name: egg yolk
ingredients.prep: beaten with 1 tbsp water, for brushing

steps: Heat the oven to 350 F and line two baking sheets with parchment.
Beat the butter and sugar until light and fluffy, about 3 minutes. Beat in the egg and almond extract.
Whisk the all-purpose flour, almond flour, baking powder, and salt together, then mix into the butter mixture until a soft dough forms.
Roll the dough into 24 balls about 1 1/2 tablespoons each and place them 2 inches apart on the sheets.
Press a whole almond into the center of each, flattening the cookie slightly.
Brush the tops with the egg yolk wash.
Bake for 15 to 18 minutes, until the edges are golden, rotating the pans halfway through.
Cool on the pans for 5 minutes, then move to a rack.

title: Pineapple Buns
summary: Soft, milky Hong Kong bakery buns with a sweet, crackly cookie crust on top. There is no pineapple in them, the crust just looks like one.

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.prep: divided: 1/4 cup for the dough, 1/4 cup for the topping

steps: Mix the bread flour, 1/4 cup of the sugar, the salt, and yeast. Add the warm milk and 1 whole egg and stir into a shaggy dough.
Knead in 4 tablespoons of the butter and keep kneading for about 10 minutes, until smooth and elastic.
Cover and let rise in a warm place for 1 hour, until doubled.
For the topping, beat the remaining 4 tablespoons butter with 1/4 cup of the sugar, then mix in 1 egg yolk, the all-purpose flour, and the baking powder to make a soft dough. Chill 20 minutes.
Divide the bread dough into 8 pieces, shape each into a smooth ball, and set them on a lined baking sheet. Cover and let rise for 45 minutes.
Divide the topping into 8 pieces. Flatten each between parchment into a thin disk and lay one over each bun.
Beat the last egg, brush it over the topping, and score it in a crisscross pattern with a knife.
Bake at 350 F for 18 to 22 minutes, until deep golden. Cool slightly before eating.

title: Mantou Steamed Buns
summary: Plain, fluffy, slightly sweet steamed buns that are perfect for mopping up sauces or filling with braised meat. They freeze and reheat well.
steps: Stir the yeast and sugar into the warm water and let it sit for 5 minutes until foamy.
Mix the flour and baking powder in a large bowl, then add the yeast water and oil. Stir into a dough, adding a spoonful of water if it is dry.
Knead for 8 to 10 minutes until the dough is smooth and springy.
Cover and let rise in a warm spot for about 1 hour, until doubled.
Punch the dough down, roll it into a log, and cut it into 10 equal pieces. Shape each into a smooth round.
Set each bun on a square of parchment in a steamer basket, spaced apart. Cover and rest for 20 minutes.
Steam over boiling water for 15 minutes. Turn off the heat and leave the lid on for 5 minutes before lifting it, to prevent wrinkling.
Serve warm.

title: Scallion Flower Rolls
summary: Fluffy steamed rolls swirled with scallion and a little oil, twisted into pretty flower shapes. Serve them alongside soup or a stir-fry.
steps: Stir the yeast and sugar into the warm water and let it sit 5 minutes. Mix with the flour to form a dough, then knead for 8 minutes until smooth.
Cover and let rise for about 1 hour, until doubled.
Mix the green onions, oil, salt, and five spice powder in a small bowl.
Roll the dough into a large rectangle about 1/4 inch thick. Spread the scallion mixture evenly over it.
Roll the dough up tightly from the long side, then cut the log into 8 pieces.
Press a chopstick down the center of each piece, then pinch and stretch the ends and tuck them under to make a flower shape.
Place each roll on parchment in a steamer, cover, and rest for 20 minutes.
Steam over boiling water for 15 minutes, then leave the lid on for 3 minutes before opening.

title: Chinese Sesame Flatbread
summary: Flaky, layered flatbread with a sesame seed crust, baked until crisp outside and tender inside. Eat it plain or split it open for a sandwich.

ingredients.name: all-purpose flour
ingredients.prep: divided: 2 1/2 cups for the dough, 1/4 cup for the oil paste

steps: Mix the flour and salt, then stir in the hot water until a shaggy dough forms. Knead for 8 minutes until smooth, then cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Heat the oil until hot and pour it over the second measure of flour and the five spice powder. Stir into a smooth paste and let it cool.
Divide the dough into 6 pieces. Roll one into a thin rectangle and spread it with a spoonful of paste.
Roll it up into a log, coil the log into a spiral, and tuck the end underneath. Repeat with the other pieces and rest for 15 minutes.
Heat the oven to 450 F with a baking sheet inside.
Flatten each spiral into a disk about 1/2 inch thick. Brush the tops with the honey water and press into the sesame seeds.
Bake on the hot sheet for 12 to 15 minutes, flipping once, until golden and puffed.
Cool on a rack for a few minutes before serving.

title: Jianbing
summary: A Chinese street-food crepe cooked with a thin egg layer, brushed with sweet bean and chili sauces, and wrapped around a crunchy cracker. It makes a satisfying breakfast.
steps: Whisk the flours, water, and salt into a thin, smooth batter and rest for 15 minutes.
Fry the wonton wrappers in hot oil for 30 seconds per side, until golden and crisp. Drain on paper towels.
Heat a large nonstick skillet over medium heat and brush with a little oil.
Pour in about 1/4 of the batter and swirl quickly into a thin round. Cook for 1 minute until the surface is set.
Crack an egg on top, break the yolk, and spread it thinly across the crepe. Sprinkle with sesame seeds and some green onions.
Flip the crepe and brush the new top with sweet bean sauce and chili oil.
Add cilantro and two crisp wonton wrappers, then fold the sides in and roll up like a burrito.
Repeat with the remaining batter and serve hot.

title: Chinese Spinach with Garlic
summary: Spinach quickly stir-fried with lots of garlic until just wilted. It is a fast, bright side dish for any Chinese meal.
steps: Wash the spinach well and shake off most of the water. Trim any tough stems.
Heat a wok or large skillet over high heat until very hot, then add the oil.
Add the garlic and stir for 10 seconds, until fragrant but not browned.
Add the spinach in handfuls, tossing as it wilts.
Pour in the rice wine and sprinkle with the salt and sugar.
Stir-fry for 1 to 2 minutes, until the leaves are just wilted and still bright green.
Drizzle with sesame oil, toss once, and serve right away.

title: Taiwanese Braised Pork Rice
summary: Pork belly simmered until tender in a sweet and savory soy sauce with shallots, spooned over warm rice. Called lu rou fan, it is a Taiwanese comfort classic.

ingredients.name: pork belly
ingredients.prep: skin removed, cut into small 1/2 inch pieces

steps: Fry the shallots in the oil over medium heat for 6 to 8 minutes, until deep golden and crisp. Scoop out and set aside, keeping the oil in the pot.
Add the pork belly to the pot and cook over medium-high heat until lightly browned, about 8 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook 30 seconds, then pour in the rice wine and scrape up any browned bits.
Add the soy sauce, dark soy sauce, sugar, five spice powder, star anise, and water, and return half of the fried shallots to the pot.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low for 1 hour, stirring occasionally. Add the eggs for the last 30 minutes if using.
Uncover and simmer another 15 minutes, until the sauce is glossy and slightly thickened. Add water if it reduces too much.
Spoon the pork and sauce over rice, top with the remaining fried shallots, and add an egg to each bowl.

title: Taiwanese Popcorn Chicken
summary: Bite-size marinated chicken coated in sweet potato starch, fried until crunchy, and tossed with fried basil and white pepper. It is a night market favorite.

ingredients.name: chicken thighs
ingredients.prep: boneless, skinless, cut into 1 inch pieces

steps: Toss the chicken with the soy sauce, rice wine, garlic, sugar, five spice powder, white pepper, and egg. Marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot to 350 F.
Toss the chicken pieces in the starch, pressing so it sticks, then shake off the excess. Let them sit for a few minutes so the coating turns tacky.
Fry in small batches for 4 to 5 minutes, until golden and cooked through. Drain on a rack.
Raise the oil to 375 F and fry all of the chicken again for 1 minute for extra crunch.
Carefully fry the basil leaves for about 20 seconds, until crisp, and drain on paper towels. Stand back, as the oil will spatter.
Toss the chicken with the salt, a little more white pepper, and the fried basil. Serve hot.

title: Taiwanese Beef Noodle Soup
summary: A rich, spicy-savory broth with fork-tender braised beef shank, bok choy, and chewy noodles. The braise takes time but mostly looks after itself.
steps: Blanch the beef in a pot of boiling water for 3 minutes, then drain and rinse to remove scum.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the ginger, garlic, and green onions for 1 minute.
Stir in the doubanjiang and cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until the oil turns red.
Add the beef, rice wine, soy sauce, sugar, star anise, cinnamon, tomatoes, and water.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer gently for 2 to 2 1/2 hours, until the beef is very tender.
Taste the broth and adjust with soy sauce or water. Remove the whole spices if you like.
Boil the noodles according to the package, adding the bok choy for the last minute. Drain.
Divide the noodles and bok choy among bowls, top with beef, ladle the hot broth over, and add pickled greens if using.

title: Oyster Omelette
summary: A crisp-edged, chewy egg omelette with plump oysters and greens, topped with a sweet and tangy red sauce. This Taiwanese night market dish is easy to make at home.
steps: Whisk the starch with the water until smooth. Briefly toss the oysters in a spoonful of this slurry and set aside.
Mix the ketchup, sweet bean sauce, sugar, water, and sriracha in a small bowl for the sauce.
Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Add the oysters and cook for 1 minute, then add the greens and cook 30 seconds.
Stir the starch slurry again and pour it over the oysters. Cook for about 1 minute, until it turns translucent and sticky.
Beat the eggs with the white pepper and pour them over the top. Drizzle the rest of the oil around the edges.
Cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until the bottom is golden and crisp, then flip in sections and cook 1 minute more.
Slide onto a plate, spoon on the sauce, and sprinkle with cilantro.

title: Hainanese Chicken Rice
summary: Silky poached chicken served with fragrant rice cooked in the poaching broth, plus a zesty ginger scallion sauce. It looks simple but rewards patience.
steps: Rub the chicken all over with about 1 tablespoon of the salt, then rinse well. Pat dry.
Fill a large pot with enough water to cover the chicken and bring it to a simmer with the ginger and green onions.
Lower the chicken in, breast side up, and keep the water just below a simmer for 45 minutes. Do not boil.
Remove the chicken and plunge it into a bowl of ice water for 10 minutes to tighten the skin. Drain, pat dry, and rub with sesame oil. Reserve the broth.
Cook half of the garlic in the chicken fat for 1 minute, add the rice and stir for 2 minutes, then add 3 cups of the reserved broth and a pinch of salt.
Cook the rice in a rice cooker or covered pot over low heat for about 18 minutes, then rest 10 minutes.
Chop the chicken and arrange over the rice with cucumber slices. Drizzle with soy sauce and serve with the broth and ginger scallion sauce.

title: Cantonese Steamed Chicken with Mushrooms
summary: Tender chicken pieces marinated in ginger and wine and steamed with shiitake mushrooms until juicy. It is a light, classic Cantonese family dinner.
steps: Soak the dried mushrooms in hot water for 30 minutes, then squeeze dry, trim the stems, and slice. Save 2 tablespoons of the soaking liquid.
Mix the chicken with the soy sauce, oyster sauce, rice wine, cornstarch, sugar, sesame oil, ginger, and the mushroom liquid.
Fold in the mushrooms and marinate for 15 minutes.
Spread everything on a shallow heatproof plate.
Steam over high heat for 18 to 20 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and the juices run clear.
Scatter the green onions over the top.
Heat the vegetable oil until smoking and pour it over the green onions to release their aroma. Serve with rice.

title: Clams in Black Bean Sauce
summary: Fresh clams steamed open in a savory, garlicky black bean sauce with a touch of chili. Serve with plenty of rice to soak up the sauce.
steps: Soak the clams in cold salted water for 20 minutes to release grit, then drain and rinse.
Heat the oil in a large wok or deep skillet over high heat. Add the black beans, garlic, ginger, and chili and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the clams and toss to coat.
Pour in the rice wine, soy sauce, and broth. Cover and cook for 4 to 6 minutes, shaking the pan occasionally.
Remove the lid. Pick out any clams that have not opened and discard them.
Stir in the cornstarch mixture and cook for 30 seconds, until the sauce thickens slightly.
Toss in the green onions and serve right away.

title: Ginger Scallion Lobster
summary: Lobster pieces stir-fried with lots of ginger and scallion in a light, savory sauce. A special-occasion dish that cooks in minutes once the lobster is prepped.

ingredients.name: lobster
ingredients.prep: 1 1/2 lb each, live, or 4 lobster tails

steps: If the lobsters are live, chill them in the freezer for 20 minutes, then quickly kill them with a knife through the head. Cut them into pieces, with claws cracked and bodies chopped into sections.
Pat the lobster dry and toss lightly with 2 tablespoons of the cornstarch.
Heat half the oil in a large wok over high heat. Sear the lobster pieces for 2 minutes, then remove them.
Add the remaining oil, ginger, and garlic and stir for 30 seconds.
Return the lobster to the wok and add the rice wine, oyster sauce, soy sauce, sugar, and broth.
Cover and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until the shells are bright red and the meat is opaque.
Stir the remaining cornstarch with 1 tablespoon of water and add it with the green onions. Cook 30 seconds until glossy.
Drizzle with sesame oil and serve hot.

title: Kung Pao Tofu
summary: Crisp pan-fried tofu cubes tossed in a sweet, tangy, and mildly spicy sauce with peanuts and dried chilies. A satisfying vegetarian take on the Sichuan classic.

ingredients.name: firm tofu
ingredients.prep: pressed and cut into 3/4 inch cubes

steps: Pat the pressed tofu dry and toss it gently with the 2 tablespoons of cornstarch.
Whisk the soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, the 1 teaspoon of cornstarch, and water in a small bowl.
Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Fry the tofu for 8 to 10 minutes, turning, until golden and crisp on most sides. Remove to a plate.
Add the remaining oil, chilies, and peppercorns to the pan and stir for 20 seconds, until the chilies darken slightly.
Add the garlic, ginger, and green onions and stir for 30 seconds.
Return the tofu to the pan, pour in the sauce, and toss for about 1 minute, until glossy.
Stir in the peanuts and serve right away with rice.

title: Sichuan Mala Dry Pot Cauliflower
summary: Cauliflower stir-fried until browned and tossed with dried chilies, numbing Sichuan peppercorns, and bean paste. Dry pot dishes are bold, spicy, and fun to share.
steps: Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a wok over medium-high heat. Fry the cauliflower for 6 to 8 minutes, tossing, until browned in spots and tender-crisp. Remove it.
If using bacon, fry it in the same wok until crisp, then remove it and leave the fat.
Add the remaining oil, chilies, and peppercorns and stir over medium heat for 30 seconds.
Add the doubanjiang, garlic, and ginger and cook for 1 minute until fragrant and the oil turns red.
Add the onion and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Return the cauliflower and bacon to the wok. Add the soy sauce and sugar and toss for 2 minutes.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and green onions and serve hot. The chilies are for flavor, so you do not need to eat them.

title: Stir-Fried Celery with Pork
summary: Crunchy celery and tender sliced pork stir-fried in a light garlicky sauce. A quick weeknight dish that goes well with rice.
steps: Toss the pork with the soy sauce, rice wine, and cornstarch and let it sit for 15 minutes.
Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a wok over high heat. Stir-fry the pork for 2 minutes until just cooked, then remove it.
Add the remaining oil, garlic, and ginger and stir for 15 seconds.
Add the celery and carrot and stir-fry for 2 to 3 minutes, until crisp-tender.
Return the pork to the wok and add the oyster sauce, salt, and white pepper.
Toss for 1 minute until everything is coated and hot, and serve with rice.

title: Pork with Garlic Sauce
summary: Thin slices of poached pork belly or leg chilled and served with a spicy, savory, garlicky sauce. This Sichuan cold dish is great for summer.
steps: Put the pork in a pot with the ginger, green onions, and rice wine. Cover with cold water and bring to a boil.
Reduce to a gentle simmer and cook for 30 to 35 minutes, until a chopstick slides through easily.
Remove the pork and let it cool, then chill it in the fridge for at least 20 minutes so it slices cleanly.
Mix the garlic, soy sauce, vinegar, chili oil, sugar, and sesame oil in a bowl.
Slice the pork as thinly as you can and arrange it on a plate with the cucumber.
Spoon the sauce over the pork and top with cilantro.

title: Shredded Pork with Green Peppers
summary: Thin strips of pork and green pepper stir-fried quickly in a savory sauce. Simple, fast, and a staple of home Chinese cooking.
steps: Toss the pork strips with the first measure of soy sauce, the rice wine, and cornstarch. Let sit for 15 minutes.
Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a wok over high heat and stir-fry the pork for 2 minutes, until it just turns white. Remove it.
Add the remaining oil, garlic, and ginger and stir for 15 seconds.
Add the peppers and stir-fry for 2 to 3 minutes, until crisp-tender.
Return the pork, then add the second measure of soy sauce, the oyster sauce, and the sugar.
Toss for 1 minute, drizzle with sesame oil, and serve with rice.

title: Sweet and Sour Shrimp
summary: Crisp-coated shrimp tossed in a glossy, tangy red sauce with pineapple and peppers. Fry the shrimp just before serving to keep them crunchy.

ingredients.name: cornstarch
ingredients.prep: plus 1 tsp for thickening the sauce

steps: Pat the shrimp dry and toss with the salt and beaten egg.
Stir the ketchup, sugar, vinegar, and soy sauce together in a small bowl and set aside.
Heat the oil in a pot to 350 F. Coat the shrimp in the 1/2 cup cornstarch, shaking off the extra.
Fry the shrimp in two batches for 2 to 3 minutes, until golden and crisp. Drain on a rack.
Pour off all but 1 tablespoon of oil from a wok. Stir-fry the garlic and bell pepper over high heat for 1 minute.
Add the pineapple and the sauce, bring to a simmer, and stir in the cornstarch mixture until thick and glossy.
Add the shrimp, toss for 15 seconds to coat, and serve at once with rice.

title: Chinese Pickled Vegetables
summary: Crunchy quick pickles of cabbage, carrot, and cucumber in a sweet, tangy, lightly spicy brine. Ready the next day and keeps for about a week.
steps: Toss the cabbage, carrots, and cucumbers with the salt and let them sit for 30 minutes.
Rinse the vegetables under cold water and drain well, then squeeze out extra moisture and pat dry.
Warm the vinegar, sugar, and water in a small pot until the sugar dissolves, then add the peppercorns and chilies and cool completely.
Pack the vegetables into a clean jar with the garlic and ginger.
Pour the cooled brine over the vegetables until they are covered.
Seal and refrigerate for at least 12 hours before eating. Keep chilled for up to 1 week.

title: Ginger Scallion Sauce
summary: A fragrant raw sauce of minced ginger and scallion softened with hot oil. Spoon it over rice, noodles, chicken, or steamed fish.
steps: Combine the green onions, ginger, and salt in a heatproof bowl and stir well.
Heat the oil in a small pan until it shimmers and just starts to smoke, about 2 minutes.
Carefully pour the hot oil over the scallion mixture. It will sizzle.
Stir in the soy sauce and the vinegar if using.
